products.name: Clawdmeter
products.scope_note: In scope: an open-source DIY desk display for Claude Code usage limits, with a mascot and hook-driven alerts. github.com/BenjAngelone/clawdmeter is not this product and should not be merged. It is a separate one-commit, 1-star project of the same name (the "Benja" pixel robot on a Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-1.69, 240x280), checked 2026-11-18. unverified: the MakerWorld "clawd-meter" listing (2906020) and other community MakerWorld cases. MakerWorld returns 403, so these rest on search snippets only.
products.one_liner: Open-source ESP32 desk display (flagship: Waveshare 2.16" 480x480 AMOLED) that shows Claude Code 5-hour/weekly limit meters over Bluetooth. An animated pixel Clawd reacts to hook events and raises permission/question alerts. Buttons act as a BLE keyboard, e.g. hold for voice push-to-talk, Shift+Tab to cycle modes.
agents_supported: OpenAI Codex CLI (trial: usage meters and reset credits only, no mascot reactions)

agent_status.note: Clawd reacts to hook events. He points on a prompt or a back-after-gap event and waves once when a turn of 2+ min stops. He puts on a ~20 s 'show' after activity level 3 holds for 5 min. The docs say the status line's rotating verbs are a health indicator, 'not a report of an active model request'. There is no explicit idle/working/done readout. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/clawd-director.md

multi_session.note: Polls several Claude Code config dirs (accounts) plus Codex and shows the account whose usage rose most recently. Hooks pass an active-session count (n) to the device. Alerts can come from any session. No per-session overview or switching. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md and https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/protocol.md

permission_alert.note: Device shows 'Permission needed!', 'Question for you', 'Waiting for you!' (idle) or 'MCP request!'. A big Clawd walks on and waves/points, with optional chime on the board and/or the computer, and the tray mirrors it. Configurable via alert_on. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md

approve_from_device.note: No dedicated approve/deny. The buttons are a BLE keyboard and can be remapped to Enter, Esc, Tab, Space or Shift+Tab sent to the focused window. That answers a Claude Code prompt only if the terminal has focus. A tap dismisses the alert on the device. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md

jump_to_session.note: Not mentioned. The user guide lists every tray-menu item and button action, and none of them focuses a terminal or session. Buttons send keys to whatever window is focused.

token_usage_cost.note: Usage is shown only as a percent of plan limits. Spend-capped (enterprise) accounts show spend % and billing-period progress. Token counts and $ amounts are not shown ('Spend amounts aren't sent'). https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/daemon-parity.md

plan_limits.note: Core feature: session (5-hour) and weekly % with reset countdowns. Optional pace marker colours bars green/amber/red against elapsed window time. Shows a Fable weekly-limit strip, weekly-only Ultra accounts, and Codex reset credits with expiry dates. macOS menu bar can show the higher %. Optional reset chime. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md

personal_baseline_levels.note: Clawd's mood comes from a 0-3 hook activity level and a usage-rate mood that 'stays tuned for the 5-hour window'. Nothing is calibrated to the user's own history. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/protocol.md

test_build_red_green.note: Tool calls count as hook events only toward the activity level. The guide says 'full tool-call payloads are not written to the event log', so test/build results are never inspected. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md

loop_stuck_detection.note: Not among the beats and reactions in the director spec, which lists all of Clawd's triggers. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/clawd-director.md

drift_away_detection.note: Only relays Claude Code's own idle-prompt notification as 'Waiting for you!' (opt-in 'idle' in alert_on). A 'back after a gap' hook event (e:b) wakes Clawd, and the screensaver starts after 10 min with no engagement. No detection of the user switching apps. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/protocol.md

ai_session_recap.note: No summaries in the README or user guide. Prompt text is not logged. The only model call is a short Haiku message (no tools) used to read rate-limit headers.

history_dashboard.note: The desktop app's Overview and tray show current meters and reset times only. The user guide describes no multi-day history.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: None documented.

leaderboard.note: None documented.

character_personality.note: Clawd mascot with a detailed 'director' built on named animation principles (anticipation, follow-through, staging). He has a corner seat with mood-picked idle acts and full-size scene 'shows' (racing car, skateboard, soccer, sailing, etc.). There is also a face screensaver with blinks and glances, a peek-on-tap, joy jumps on a fresh limit window, and an attention walk-on. An 'Animation silliness' slider runs from No-nonsense to All-nonsense. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/clawd-director.md

sound_voice_out.note: Optional alert chime and reset chime on boards with a speaker (3 beeps on buzzer boards), plus an optional chime on the computer. No speech. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md

voice_input.note: Holding BOOT sends Space as a push-to-talk key for Claude Code's own voice input on the computer. The docs describe no use of the board's own microphones. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md

physical_controls.note: Flagship has 3 buttons (BOOT, PWR, GPIO18) plus a capacitive touchscreen. Buttons can be remapped to Space/Shift+Tab/Tab/Enter/Esc, media keys, brightness or custom shortcuts (e.g. Teams mute). A tap dismisses alerts or brings up Clawd's face. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md

second_screen_mode.note: Dedicated BLE desk display. 28 boards are listed (1 flagship, 6 stable, 21 experimental), from 135x240 sticks and 240x240 LCDs to 480x480 AMOLED/RGB panels and e-paper. https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter

products.price_text: The software (desktop app and firmware) is free. You buy the hardware yourself. The flagship Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.16 is USD 29.99-31.99 on Waveshare (without or with a 3.7V battery), as of 2026-11-18. CNX Software quoted about $30 on AliExpress and $40.99 on Amazon on 2026-05-14. Cheaper experimental boards such as 'Cheap Yellow Display' units also work. unverified: printable cases are free community models on MakerWorld. Not sold as a finished product. The README's Waveshare links carry an affiliate ID (aff_id=149786).
products.license: No license file (GitHub shows none). The README's 'Licensing gray area warning' says the code is 'non-proprietary', but the author will not apply a copyleft license himself. The repo includes Anthropic's proprietary fonts (used without permission) and the copyrighted Clawd mascot, and he warns forkers about this.
products.privacy_note: No Clawdmeter account or server. The tray app reads the existing Claude Code OAuth token (Keychain or .credentials.json) read-only and calls Anthropic's own usage endpoint. While a session runs, it has Claude Code send one short Haiku message to read rate-limit headers. For Codex it calls ChatGPT's usage endpoint. Data goes to the board over BLE. The local event log keeps timestamps, event types and session IDs, not prompt text or tool payloads. Alerts store the notification message or first AskUserQuestion question, which is sent to the device. Update checks go to GitHub every 6 hours.
products.distinctive: One of the most-starred DIY Claude Code hardware meters (2,349 GitHub stars as of 2026-11-18). It has a polished cross-platform tray app that flashes firmware, installs hooks and configures the board, and it runs on 28 ESP32 boards. Clawd is an unusually elaborate animated character, with a 'director' spec built on classic animation principles. The board doubles as a BLE keyboard (voice push-to-talk, Shift+Tab mode cycling, custom shortcuts).
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are Claude Code-focused pixel-mascot companions with an optional DIY ESP32 desk screen, and both use hooks for permission/waiting alerts. Clawdmeter is built around plan limits: 5-hour/weekly %, resets, pace marker, Fable and Codex limits. It talks to its board over Bluetooth, has physical buttons and touch, plays chimes, and runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. The reference is built around work intensity measured against your own 30-day history. The reference also has moments Clawdmeter lacks: test fail-then-pass, loops, drifting away, goals and streaks, AI recaps, a 30-day history dashboard and a 'Go to it' focus button. Clawdmeter's nearest equivalent is a single wave after any turn of 2+ minutes. Unlike the reference, it does not show the robot on the Mac desktop, only in the macOS tray menu panel.
products.hardware: DIY. Flagship is the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.16: 2.16" 480x480 AMOLED with capacitive touch, ESP32-S3R8 with 8MB PSRAM and 16MB flash, and 3 buttons (PWR/BOOT/GPIO18). It also has a speaker, dual mics (no use documented), a QMI8658 IMU and an optional 3.7V 1000mAh battery via the AXP2101 PMU. Connects to the computer over BLE, using a custom GATT data service plus a standard HID keyboard/consumer-control service. Firmware is flashed over USB from the app. 6 stable boards besides the flagship: Waveshare ESP32-C6 AMOLED-2.16, S3 and C6 AMOLED-1.8, S3 AMOLED-2.06, S3 LCD-1.54 (240x240 IPS) and LILYGO T4-S3. 21 experimental community ports, including round AMOLEDs, Cheap Yellow Display boards, M5Stack FIRE/StickS3, 480x480 RGB panels (Guition 4848S040, SenseCAP Indicator, Waveshare LCD-2.1/2.8C/4) and e-paper. unverified: community 3D-printed cases on MakerWorld.
products.maker: Hermann Haraldsson (GitHub: HermannBjorgvin), a software developer who says he is 'not an embedded developer' and built it with Claude's help.

products.name: Claude Desktop Buddy / Hardware Buddy BLE API
products.one_liner: Anthropic's open BLE protocol in Claude for macOS/Windows, plus a reference ESP32 (M5StickC Plus) desk pet. The pet shows Claude Cowork and Claude Code activity and lets you approve or deny permission prompts with physical buttons.
agents_supported: Claude Code (inside the Claude desktop app; repo About says 'Claude Code Desktop')

agent_status.note: Protocol heartbeat (sent on every change plus a 10s keepalive) carries total/running/waiting counts, a one-line 'msg' and recent transcript 'entries' (REFERENCE.md). README lists 7 states: sleep, idle, busy, attention, celebrate, dizzy, heart. Caveat from the code: the reference firmware only shows 'busy' when 3 or more sessions are running (derive() in src/main.cpp), and 'celebrate' comes from a 'completed' field that REFERENCE.md does not document (src/data.h). The firmware does not use the per-turn 'evt: turn' events.

multi_session.note: Only aggregate counts across sessions (sessions/running/waiting) on the CLAUDE info page (src/main.cpp). No per-session list or switching. https://github.com/anthropics/claude-desktop-buddy/blob/main/REFERENCE.md

permission_alert.note: 'attention' state when prompt.id is present. On a new prompt the screen wakes, beeps (1200 Hz chirp) and shows the approval view with tool, hint and a seconds-waited counter that turns red after 10s. The red LED blinks while in attention (src/main.cpp). Press also says it 'buzzes' (https://www.yankodesign.com/?p=626244).

approve_from_device.note: Button A sends {cmd: permission, decision: 'once'} and B sends 'deny', echoing prompt.id (REFERENCE.md, src/main.cpp). The protocol only has approve-once or deny: no 'always allow' and no free-text answers.

jump_to_session.note: Device-to-desktop messages are only permission decisions and command acks. There is no focus or jump command (REFERENCE.md).

token_usage_cost.note: The pet stats page shows cumulative 'tokens' and 'today' tokens (src/main.cpp). These are output tokens only (REFERENCE.md). No $ cost.

plan_limits.note: The heartbeat schema has no quota, rate-limit or reset fields (REFERENCE.md).

personal_baseline_levels.note: Fixed thresholds: TOKENS_PER_LEVEL = 50000. Mood tier is the median response time of the last 8 approvals checked against fixed cutoffs (<15s, <30s, <60s, <120s), minus a penalty for the deny ratio (src/stats.h).

test_build_red_green.note: No test or build signal in the protocol or the firmware states. Only raw transcript lines.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Nothing for loops or stuck agents in the 7 documented states or the heartbeat fields.

drift_away_detection.note: Nothing on user presence or app focus. Only a device-side 30s screen-off timer and a waiting-seconds counter on the prompt.

ai_session_recap.note: 'msg' is a one-line status (example 'approve: Bash') and 'entries' are raw transcript lines. Neither is an AI-written summary (REFERENCE.md).

history_dashboard.note: Only lifetime counters (approvals, denials, nap time, tokens, level) and today's tokens. The desktop Hardware Buddy window polls a live status panel. There is no day-by-day history.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Levels as progression: a level up with confetti and the celebrate state every 50K output tokens, plus a 'fed' bar at 5K tokens per pip, mood hearts and an energy bar (src/stats.h, src/main.cpp). No streaks, daily goals or badges.

leaderboard.note: Single device, local only. Nothing in the protocol compares users.

character_personality.note: 18 ASCII pet species, each with 7 animations, plus custom 96px GIF character packs pushed over BLE. The bundled GIF pack is 'bufo' (README).

sound_voice_out.note: beep() on the M5 buzzer for prompt arrival, approve and deny, button presses and pairing. It can be turned off with the 'sound' setting (src/main.cpp, src/stats.h). No speech.

voice_input.note: Neither the protocol nor the firmware has any voice input.

physical_controls.note: Button A (next screen/approve), B (scroll/deny), hold A for the menu, power button (screen off, or hard off after 6s), shake (dizzy) and face-down (nap) via the IMU (README).

second_screen_mode.note: A dedicated 135x240 color screen on a separate battery-powered device (README, Yanko Design).

products.price_text: Firmware, protocol and API are free (MIT). The reference hardware is an M5StickC Plus, about $30 per press (CNX Software 2026-05-16, AliExpress/Amazon; Yanko Design 2026-05-20). RobotShop US lists the M5StickC Plus at $21.00 but out of stock (seen 2026-11-18). unverified: Switch Science (Japan) showing the original Plus out of stock and recommending the Plus2 (page returned HTTP 429 on 2026-11-18). If the Plus2 replaces it, a port may be needed, since the firmware targets the M5StickCPlus library. Requires the Claude desktop app (macOS or Windows) with a Claude account and Developer Mode on.
products.license: MIT (Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC). The bundled characters/bufo GIF assets are third-party art (bufo.zone) and not covered by the MIT license.
products.privacy_note: The device talks directly to the Claude desktop app over BLE (Nordic UART Service), with no extra cloud or API key. Transcript snippets, tool-call hints and the account owner's first name ('owner' command on connect) cross the radio link. Anthropic recommends LE Secure Connections bonding with a 6-digit passkey, but the desktop app also accepts unencrypted devices. The host Claude app itself needs a Claude account.
products.distinctive: This is a first-party, documented hardware-integration API from the agent vendor. Any BLE device that speaks Nordic UART plus newline-delimited JSON can show session counts, transcript lines and tokens, and can answer permission prompts, with no hooks or cloud. It is gated behind Developer Mode and labelled 'not an officially supported product feature'. The reference pet adds Tamagotchi mechanics (fed by tokens, mood from approval speed) and has drawn community ports and add-ons: a Waveshare ESP32 AMOLED port, Espressif's ESP Desktop Buddy library (both per CNX), and open PRs for an M5StickS3 port and a hooks-based bridge for the Claude Code VSCode extension.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlap: both are Claude-only characters that react to agent state and permission waits, and both offer an ESP32 desk screen. Differences: Buddy runs over BLE from the Claude desktop app (Cowork and Claude Code in the desktop app), not terminal Claude Code CLI hooks. A community PR (#53, open, not merged) adds a hooks-based bridge for the VSCode extension. You can approve or deny from the device, which the reference product does not do. Buddy has no desktop overlay or second-monitor scene and no 'Go to it' jump. Its levels are fixed 50K-token steps, not a personal 30-day baseline. It has none of the test/build, loop, drift or long-session moments, no AI recaps, no daily goal or streak and no history dashboard. Buddy has physical buttons, an IMU, a buzzer, an LED and a battery, and it is a protocol other makers can build on. The reference product's DIY board could in principle speak this protocol.
products.hardware: Reference: M5StickC Plus (ESP32-PICO; 135x240 color LCD; buttons A/B plus power; IMU; red LED on GPIO10; buzzer; LiPo battery). The 1.14in panel size and USB-C come from the vendor spec and were not re-checked. Connects over BLE Nordic UART with newline-delimited JSON. Firmware uses Arduino/PlatformIO (board m5stick-c) with the M5StickCPlus, AnimatedGIF and ArduinoJson libraries. Other boards need driver forks.

products.name: Agent Cat
products.scope_note: In scope. Discovery filed it as a desktop companion, but it is better described as a usage, quota and reset monitor with a RunCat-style menu-bar mascot. The Korean site's title is "Agent Cat — 무료 AI 사용량·쿼터·리셋 모니터" (Free AI Usage, Quota & Reset Monitor), and its hero line is "AI 코딩 한도를 메뉴바에서. 무료." The English hero line is "When your agents work, your cat runs."
products.one_liner: A free macOS menu-bar and Windows tray app. A pixel cat, or another selectable mascot (26 as of May 2026), sleeps, walks or runs as your coding agents work. The app tracks tokens, cost estimates and 5h/7d quota windows across many agents and accounts. It syncs to iPhone, Android, Apple Watch and Wear OS companion apps, and adds teams, collectible pins and an opt-in Claude-powered 'Reflect' session analysis.

agent_status.note: The cat sleeps, walks or runs with agent activity, measured from local metadata such as CPU, process count and token counts (https://hjsong.net/1050). Hook events also count (v26.46.0). The site's popover demo shows Working / All done / Resting states. The status is aggregate and activity-based, not a per-agent state machine.

multi_session.note: Shows the number of active agents and session time (https://disquiet.io/articles/Brs2lx) and covers many providers and accounts at once. With more than four accounts, the popover shows a one-line summary per provider (v26.41.3). v26.47.0 adds CLI launcher badges (claude, claude2–claude5, codex, codex2, gemini/agy, grok, cursor). No source shows a per-session list or switching between sessions.

permission_alert.note: v26.46.0 (2026-11-16) 'Adds read-only terminal input attention notices for supported Claude hooks'. This covers Claude only, is very new, and the format is not described (https://github.com/yong076/agent-cat-releases/releases/tag/v26.46.0).

approve_from_device.note: The release notes call the attention notices 'read-only', and the connector only reads data.

jump_to_session.note: No source mentions focusing or opening a terminal. Launcher badges are described only as display labels.

token_usage_cost.note: Per-agent tokens for today, this week and this month, plus the most recent model (Mac App Store). Usage by project. Cost estimates are included (site: '비용 추정'), and 'Costs use current list prices' (v26.41.x release notes).

plan_limits.note: Remaining 5h/7d (and model or credit) limits per account, reset times, reset notifications, Codex reset credits, and alerts to switch accounts when one hits its limit (site). Also opt-in unused-quota reminders (v26.46.0) and concentric multi-window quota rings (v26.47.0). The sandboxed Mac App Store build reads only Codex limits; the direct-download build covers all providers (iOS listing via https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=6804198497).

personal_baseline_levels.note: Optional alerts when you set a personal best or when usage suddenly spikes (Mac App Store 26.44.0 notes). Cat speed follows live process and CPU activity. No source says its levels are calibrated to your own history.

drift_away_detection.note: v26.46.0 caps the mascot at walking when agent processes sleep, which is about the agent, not the user leaving.

ai_session_recap.note: Reflect is an opt-in session analysis, and 'Analysis requires a logged-in current Claude Code CLI and a supported model' (v26.37.1, https://github.com/yong076/agent-cat-releases/releases/tag/v26.37.1). It produces per-session analysis details and a weekly report ('This week's reflection is ready', v26.36.1). Optional automatic analysis runs at 3 AM (v26.42.0). The exact content of the output is not described.

history_dashboard.note: Usage calendar, daily and weekly report summaries (v26.20.0), and a dashboard with History, Reports, Projects, Insights and Trends pages (v26.39.x). The iOS app shows 7-day usage trends.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: 'Collect pins as you reach usage and streak milestones.' You can equip one in the popover or share it as a card (https://agentcat.app/en).

leaderboard.note: Agent Team (join by invite code) lets members 'See member usage', with estimated cost. No ranking is mentioned. The public Trends page shows anonymous community aggregates (top model, highest 24-hour usage), not a user leaderboard.

character_personality.note: The menu-bar cat animates (sleeps, walks, runs) with agent activity. A 2026-05-26 review counted 26 selectable mascots, including a cheetah, golden retriever and baby dragon (https://hjsong.net/1050). v26.44.0 added mascot search, categories and favorites.

sound_voice_out.note: No source mentions sounds or speech beyond system notifications.

voice_input.note: No source mentions it.

physical_controls.note: Software only.

second_screen_mode.note: The iPhone app (with Home Screen widgets and a Live Activity in the Dynamic Island), the Android app, the Apple Watch app and the Wear OS app (tile and complication) show limits and usage synced from the desktop. They need an account and cross-device sync. There is no full-screen second-monitor mode.

products.price_text: Free as of 2026-11-18. The site lists ₩0 with no subscription, payments or locked features, and says reports, full history, cost estimates, pins and teams are all included. Former 'Pro' features (reports, full recap, cost estimate, full history, Agent Hub) became free for everyone in v26.35.0 (2026-08-26). Sign-in is optional and only needed for sync, teams and mobile. The Mac App Store, iOS and Google Play apps are free, and the Mac App Store listing is marked 'Contains Advertising'. An official T-shirt is sold separately on Marpple (price not seen).
products.license: The app is closed source: the releases repo says 'The product source code lives in a private repository'. The local connectors are source-available under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0, which is not OSI open source and prohibits commercial competitive use.
products.privacy_note: The direct-download build uses a local connector daemon (listens only on 127.0.0.1:8765, data in ~/.agentcat). It reads local stats, SQLite and telemetry files read-only, and its Claude UserPromptSubmit/Stop hooks discard prompt text. The Mac App Store build installs nothing extra and reads existing logs after a one-time home-folder grant. Prompts, responses and code are not stored or uploaded. Provider quota endpoints (Claude OAuth usage, ChatGPT Codex usage, Gemini Code Assist quota) are called only on explicit or optional managed refresh. An optional account enables cross-device sync, teams and mobile, which sync only limit percentages and usage aggregates. Anonymous telemetry is on by default and feeds the community Trends page. It can be turned off, but a minimal liveness ping (version, build, platform) remains. The Mac App Store privacy label lists email and user ID as linked to you, and usage data (including for advertising and marketing) as not linked.
products.distinctive: The broadest agent and account coverage in its niche: about 10 agents, multiple logged-in accounts per CLI, and alerts to switch accounts when one is blocked. It wraps this quota and reset tracking in a RunCat-style animated mascot. It also reaches beyond the desktop with Windows, iOS (Live Activity), Android, Apple Watch and Wear OS apps, plus teams, collectible streak pins, a community trends page and an opt-in Claude-powered 'Reflect' session analysis, all free.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlaps: a free, local-first desktop character whose motion reflects how hard the agent is working (cat sleep/walk/run vs. robot levels), Claude Code hooks, a history dashboard, streak-style rewards (pins vs. daily wins goal and streak), a new Claude 'terminal input' attention notice, and AI session analysis run through the user's own logged-in Claude Code CLI (Reflect), much like the reference's AI recaps. Differences: Agent Cat is mainly a multi-agent, multi-account quota, limit and reset monitor (Codex, Gemini, Cursor and others) on macOS and Windows, with phone and watch companions, teams and an optional account. Its cat speed comes from live process, CPU and hook activity, not a 30-day personal baseline. No source shows test/build, loop or drift reactions, a 'Go to it' jump-to-terminal, sounds, a second-monitor scene or DIY hardware.

products.name: CodeBurn
products.scope_note: In scope: an open-source monitor for the usage, cost and quota of AI coding agents. It comes as a TUI/CLI, a desktop app, a macOS menu bar app, a Windows tray app, a GNOME extension, a screen-edge Capacity Dock, a local web dashboard, a VS Code extension, an MCP server and a Claude Code plugin. github.com/AgentSeal/codeburn is the same repo under the old org name; it 301-redirects to getagentseal/codeburn. products.one_liner: Free, MIT-licensed, local-first tool that reads the session files AI coding agents already write and itemises token use, cost and plan quota across 42 tools. It flags waste (optimize, with a setup grade) and can stop loops and runaway spend through Claude Code hooks (Guard).
agents_supported: Vercel AI Gateway (reporting API, shown on its own row)

agent_status.note: Shows no per-session idle/working/waiting state. The menu bar's optional second row can show a count of running sessions (metric `activeSessions`; https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn/blob/main/docs/menubar.md). Hovering a Capacity Dock ring opens a glance card that 'tells you what is running right now and which limits are filling up' (README).

multi_session.note: The Sessions page and `codeburn sessions` list every session across all tools, with a per-turn drawer. v0.9.28 added a desktop session view with Inspect, Agents and Story screens. The menu bar can show a running-session count, and Capacity Dock profile rings show running sessions per Claude config directory. This is a cost list and session counts, not live handling of sessions. https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn/releases/tag/v0.9.28

permission_alert.note: README, docs and release notes describe no permission or waiting-for-input alerts. The alerts that exist cover quota thresholds (70/80/90% picker) and quota run-out forecasts in the menu bar and tray, early-reset notifications from the Capacity Dock, daily budget alerts in the GNOME extension, and Guard's in-session warnings.

approve_from_device.note: There is no approve/deny UI. Guard denies looping tool calls automatically through Claude Code hooks, and the user lifts a stop with `codeburn guard allow` in a terminal (docs/guard.md).

jump_to_session.note: Clicking a session opens an in-app drawer. The 'Preferred terminal' setting only opens CodeBurn's own Full Report or Optimize in Terminal or iTerm2 (docs/menubar.md). No feature focuses or resumes the agent's session.

token_usage_cost.note: The core feature. It shows tokens and $ by tool, model, project, git branch, task, session and PR, plus cache hit rate, cost per edit, monthly pace, and 162 ISO 4217 currencies (docs/configuration.md).

plan_limits.note: `codeburn plan set` and `codeburn quota` show live 5-hour and weekly windows, e.g. '42% used · resets in 3h 20m'. The Capacity Dock shows one ring per provider. v0.9.28 added quota run-out forecasts in the menu bar and tray ('· out 15:40') and a 70/80/90% alert picker. The README still says CodeBurn 'does not predict the hour you will run out', which contradicts the release notes. https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn/releases/tag/v0.9.28

personal_baseline_levels.note: codeburn.app says each session's cost is shown as a multiple of your median session. README: `optimize` flags sessions that cost more than twice their project's average, and compare cohorts show median/P90 cost per edit turn on your own history. There are no activity or intensity levels. https://codeburn.app

test_build_red_green.note: Guard counts failing shell commands (warns after 3, denies the 5th; a success does not reset the count). There is a 'Testing' task category, set when pytest or vitest appear in a command. The one-shot rate counts a retry when the same file is edited again after a shell command. Nothing marks the moment a test goes from fail to pass. https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn/blob/main/docs/guard.md

loop_stuck_detection.note: Guard (opt-in Claude Code hooks): an identical tool call repeated 4 times in a row gets a warning and the 8th is stopped. A command that fails 3 times gets a warning and the 5th try is stopped. It warns at $5 and stops at $15 per session. All limits can be changed in guard.json. https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn/blob/main/docs/guard.md

drift_away_detection.note: It reads transcripts on disk only. No presence or app-focus detection is described in the README, docs or changelog.

ai_session_recap.note: README: task classification uses 'no model call anywhere' and the rules are deterministic. The MCP server makes no network call of its own. The nearest features: the Claude Code plugin's `/codeburn:cost` skill lets the user's own Claude summarise today's spend, and the desktop 'Story' screen 'tells a prompt in plain sentences' (method not stated).

history_dashboard.note: Desktop Overview shows the last thirty days day by day. A daily history of cost, tokens and per-project/per-model split is kept for ten years. Also: compare periods, a PR yield page, CSV/JSON export and a local web dashboard (`codeburn web`).

streaks_goals_achievements.note: No streaks, goals or XP. Optimize's grade rates setup health, not progress. The GNOME extension's daily budget alerts are spend caps, not goals.

leaderboard.note: No team or leaderboard features. `codeburn share --pair` and `codeburn devices` only combine the user's own machines on the local network.

character_personality.note: UI is charts, tables, a flame icon and usage rings. The README, docs and site show no mascot or character.

sound_voice_out.note: Sound is not mentioned in the README, docs or release notes. It is not stated whether the quota or early-reset system notifications play a sound.

voice_input.note: No voice input. It is a monitoring tool only.

physical_controls.note: Software only.

second_screen_mode.note: No dedicated display or full-screen mode. The Capacity Dock is a screen-edge rail or floating widget overlay.

products.price_text: Free and open source (MIT) as of 2026-11-18. README: 'no account, no paid tier and no feature held back for one'. Funded by GitHub Sponsors (github.com/sponsors/iamtoruk): companies sponsor at Bronze, Silver or Gold for logo placement, and Gold teams get their issues triaged first. Installs via npx/npm, Homebrew, macOS .app (signed and notarized), Microsoft Store or .exe (winget package AgentSeal.CodeBurnMenubar), Linux .deb/.rpm/AppImage, a VS Code extension (works in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity and VSCodium) and a Claude Code plugin.
products.license: MIT
products.privacy_note: README: no account, no API key, no proxy, and 'The CLI sends nothing'. Prompts, code and project names stay local. Network calls: LiteLLM prices (cached 24h), provider APIs for live quota (signed with the tools' local credentials), Frankfurter FX rates (non-USD only), Cursor usage export (about hourly; can be disabled) and GitHub for install commands. The desktop app, macOS menu bar and Windows tray send anonymous telemetry. Since v0.9.28 it is on by default in every region, including the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland. The Windows tray asks once with Accept and Decline, and the setting can be turned off in Settings. codeburn.app still describes telemetry as opt-in, which contradicts the README and release notes. The VS Code extension sends no telemetry. Multi-device pairing (`share --pair`) is optional and LAN-only.
products.distinctive: It covers the most tools of any token/cost tracker (42 per README) and adds waste analysis on top of spend: `optimize` grades setup health, estimates savings and applies or undoes fixes. Guard hooks actually stop looping tool calls, repeatedly failing commands and runaway $ in Claude Code. Very high traction for the category: about 11.9k GitHub stars and roughly 277k npm downloads in about 7 months.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlap: local-first, no account, reads Claude Code session data. It has a menu bar app, a 30-day overview and long-term daily history, and it detects loops; CodeBurn's Guard goes further and blocks them through hooks. It can show a count of running sessions. Differences: CodeBurn is a cost, quota and efficiency analytics tool for 42 agents on macOS, Windows and Linux, and it tracks $ and 5-hour/weekly plan limits that the reference lacks. It has no character, no per-session live agent state, no permission-waiting alerts, no 'Go to it' jump, no drift detection, no test fail-to-pass moments, no daily goal or streak, no AI recaps, no second-screen scene and no hardware. Its only personal baseline is cost against the user's own median or project average, not intensity levels.

products.name: Notchi
products.scope_note: In scope: a free, open-source macOS notch app that turns Claude Code and Codex hook events into an animated pixel-art mascot. You can answer Claude permission prompts from the notch, and it shows quota, cost and token usage. The official site is notchi.app. Windows ports by other developers (notchi-for-windows, pixel-companion) are separate projects listed in the README.
products.one_liner: Animated pixel-art companion in the MacBook notch. It reacts live to Claude Code and Codex hook events, lets you answer Claude permission prompts and questions from the notch, and shows quota, cost and token usage.
agents_supported: T3 Code (a host app: jump-to-host support in v1.2.6)
Devin Local (on main since 2026-09-27 commits; not in any tagged release as of v1.2.7)

agent_status.note: README: reacts in real time to thinking, working, permission requests, compaction, errors and completions. A state machine maps these to idle, working, sleeping, compacting and waiting (NotchiState.swift). Expanding the notch shows a live activity feed. v1.2.5 added an elapsed timer to the working indicator.

multi_session.note: README: supports multiple concurrent sessions, each with its own mascot from the Claude or Codex sprite family. The source has SessionListView and SessionRowView.

permission_alert.note: README: reacts to permission requests with a waiting state. Optional attention and completion sounds play (custom sounds since v1.1.1, https://github.com/sk-ruban/notchi/releases?page=2) and are muted while a terminal or supported editor is frontmost.

approve_from_device.note: v1.1.3: answer Claude permission requests and AskUserQuestion prompts from the notch, by number keys or click, with grouped answers. Escape cancels. Codex prompts are display-only when Codex has no reply action, so this is Claude-only (https://github.com/sk-ruban/notchi/releases).

jump_to_session.note: v1.1.2 added session jumping, and v1.2.6 added T3 Code host-app jumps. TerminalJumpService activates the hosting app process: Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, Warp, VS Code, Cursor, Zed, JetBrains and others. That brings the app to the front, not a specific tab or window. Codex desktop sessions open their exact thread via a codex://threads/ URL (source: notchi/Services/TerminalJumpService.swift).

token_usage_cost.note: README: tracks daily cost and token usage over the last 30 days, per provider or combined. v1.2.3 added an All tab that combines Claude and Codex costs.

plan_limits.note: README: click to see usage quota. The collapsed notch shows a usage ring (v1.2.0/v1.2.1). v1.2.4 added a Main Usage Bar setting for Session or Weekly quota. v1.2.7 shows extra usage in dollars and 'No spending cap' (https://github.com/sk-ruban/notchi/releases). Devin quota is on main.

personal_baseline_levels.note: The state machine maps hook events to fixed sprite states, and emotion intensity is scored per prompt by an LLM. Nothing in the README, releases or source computes levels against the user's own history.

test_build_red_green.note: Generic only: the README says it reacts to errors, and the activity feed marks each tool call as success or error, with error in red (ToolStatus in SessionStats.swift and ActivityRowView.swift). Nothing in the source detects tests, builds or type checks, or a fail-then-pass sequence.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Indirect only, and only with the optional API key. The sentiment prompt classifies a user prompt expressing 'feeling stuck' or frustration as sad, and the mascot reacts (EmotionAnalyzer.swift). Nothing detects repeated agent actions or loops: no such feature appears in the README, the releases or the source.

drift_away_detection.note: Indirect only: notification sounds play only when no supported terminal or editor is frontmost (TerminalFocusDetector and SoundService in the source), so they reach you when you are in another app. There is no explicit away or drift state.

ai_session_recap.note: The LLM is used only to classify prompt sentiment. The source has no summary or recap code (grep for 'summar' or 'recap' finds only a hook status badge).

history_dashboard.note: v1.2.0 added a cost and usage dashboard (CostDashboardView) with daily cost and tokens over 30 days and per-day hover. v1.2.1 added the hovered day's top model. On main, Devin is in the All chart.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: No streak, goal, achievement or XP code in the source, and none in the README or release notes.

leaderboard.note: Local single-user app with no account. No leaderboard or team comparison in the README, the releases or the source.

character_personality.note: Pixel-art mascots drawn in Aseprite: Claude and Codex sprite families, plus Devin otters on main. Emotions (happy, elated, sad, neutral, sob) come from LLM sentiment analysis of your prompts. Also bob animations and grass, water or ground island scenes (v1.2.6).

sound_voice_out.note: README: optional event sound effects, with importable custom sounds (v1.1.1), auto-muted when the terminal is focused. No speech: 'speech' appears in the source only as a filter for TTS models in the model catalog.

voice_input.note: No dictation or speech-recognition code in the source, and none in the README or releases.

physical_controls.note: Software only. Input is click, hover, keyboard number keys and a configurable global shortcut (GlobalShortcutService). Haptic feedback came in v1.0.4. The product has no physical controls of its own.

second_screen_mode.note: Lives in the notch. A screen picker (ScreenPickerRow in Appearance settings) can place the panel on another display, and v1.2.4 fixed sizing on screens without a notch. There is no full-screen second-monitor mode and no display device of its own.

products.price_text: Free and open source (GPL-3.0-only). Optional GitHub Sponsors support helps cover the Apple Developer account for signed and notarized builds (README). As of 2026-11-18.
products.license: GPL-3.0-only (README License section and repo page; the GitHub API reports gpl-3.0)
products.privacy_note: Hooks send event JSON to the app over a local Unix socket, and no account is needed. For usage stats it reads credentials from the macOS Keychain (the README tells you to click Always Allow) and fetches quota from the provider. Optional sentiment analysis sends each submitted prompt to Anthropic, OpenAI or a custom endpoint with your own API key. That is one API call per prompt (NotchiStateMachine.swift calls EmotionAnalyzer on each user prompt). Updates come through Sparkle. The README has no telemetry statement, and the source has no telemetry or analytics code.
products.distinctive: A pixel-art mascot in the MacBook notch whose mood comes from LLM sentiment analysis of your prompts. You can answer Claude permission requests and AskUserQuestion prompts inline from the notch. It also shows quota rings, a 30-day cost and token dashboard across Claude and Codex (Devin on main), and the git branch and open PR in the session header (v1.2.5).
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are free, local-first macOS pixel-art characters driven by Claude Code hooks. Both show live agent state and permission waits, play sounds, jump to the session's host app and keep 30-day history. Notchi differs in several ways. It lives in the notch (the README requires a notch MacBook). It supports Codex, with Devin on main. It lets you approve and answer Claude prompts from the notch, and it shows plan quota and $ cost. It lacks the reference's personal-baseline intensity levels, test fail-then-pass moments, behavioural loop and drift detection, daily goal and streak, AI session recaps, second-monitor scene and DIY desk screen.

products.name: viberank
products.scope_note: In scope as gamification of AI coding. It is a public leaderboard with spend tiers, streaks, friend leagues and monthly Wrapped recaps, built on ccusage token and cost data. Unverified: an unrelated VibeRank on Product Hunt is a challenge platform for prompt engineers and should not be confused with this one. This claim was not re-checked because the search budget ran out.
products.one_liner: A free, open-source (MIT) web leaderboard that ranks developers by API-equivalent AI coding spend and tokens. The data comes from ccusage and is submitted with `npx viberank-cli`, a daily autosubmit, a web upload, curl or an MCP server. It has per-tool boards, profiles, spend tiers, streaks, private leagues and monthly Wrapped recaps.

agent_status.note: Only daily usage aggregates from ccusage are uploaded. Nothing shows the agent's live state.

multi_session.note: It adds up usage across tools and machines, and profiles show 'Parallel tools' and 'Parallel machines' ratios, but there is no view of individual sessions.

permission_alert.note: Nothing alerts on agent permission requests. The only warning is `viberank status`, which flags 48 hours without a successful submission (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sculptdotfun/viberank/main/CHANGELOG.md).

token_usage_cost.note: Boards sort by Cost, Tokens or Efficiency. Profiles show API-equivalent spend, $/day average, input/output/cache-read/cache-creation tokens, cost by model, cache hit rate and cost per 1M tokens (https://www.viberank.app/profile/metalcorpe).

plan_limits.note: No tracking of 5-hour or weekly windows. The /calculator page only suggests which subscription tier your usage justifies, and the usage-limit pages are blog posts.

personal_baseline_levels.note: Tiers use fixed lifetime-dollar thresholds (Spark $0+ up to Hypernova $250K+). Profile percentiles compare you with other developers, not with your own history.

test_build_red_green.note: Only aggregate usage reports are sent, so it cannot see test or build results.

ai_session_recap.note: Monthly Wrapped is a numbers card (rank, spend, tokens, active days, longest streak, top model) with almost no prose. It is not an AI-written summary (https://www.viberank.app/wrapped/2026-10/metalcorpe).

history_dashboard.note: Profiles include a yearly activity heatmap, a 12-month 'Monthly API-equivalent' chart, spend by weekday, tools by active days and models by cost. The board filters by All, 7d or 30d (https://www.viberank.app/profile/metalcorpe).

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Profiles show the current and longest streak (e.g. 'Streak 0d', 'Longest streak 46d') and 'Tier progress' toward the next of 7 spend tiers (Spark, Ember, Flame, Blaze, Inferno, Supernova, Hypernova). There are also README rank badges. No daily goals or achievements (https://www.viberank.app/profile/metalcorpe).

leaderboard.note: This is the core product: a public global board with a top-3 podium, per-tool boards (/tool/claude, /tool/codex, /tool/gemini and more) and a Verified filter. Private leagues hold up to 100 members, are joined by invite code and need GitHub sign-in (https://www.viberank.app/leagues).

products.price_text: Free as of 2026-11-18. The site lists no pricing or paid plans, and the source code is MIT-licensed. The repo mentions a paid sponsor slot in the CLI's post-submit line (SPONSOR_CLI_NOTICE), and employers contact the /hire page by email with no published price. Neither is a charge to users.
products.license: MIT
products.privacy_note:
Usage goes to a public leaderboard hosted on Vercel, with cookieless aggregate Vercel Analytics, and Supabase.
- **Public:** GitHub handle and avatar, usage totals, per-day breakdowns, models and tools, and league memberships.
- **Server-only:** the sign-in email (stored since 28 Aug 2026), a random machine ID, hashed API tokens, the raw ccusage payload, and per-month transcript file and byte counts with the folder path sent only as a hash.
- **Never sent:** transcript, prompt and code content.
- **Sign-in:** GitHub sign-in is optional for CLI submission. It is required for the verified badge, web upload and leagues.
- **Deletion:** The README says merges never delete history, which is held at its high-water mark. However, the privacy page lets users delete their own submissions at /settings/submissions and request permanent profile deletion through a GitHub issue. Published aggregates cannot be undone.
products.distinctive:
It is the best-known public spend leaderboard ('tokenmaxxing') for AI coding agents. It turns ccusage data into a competition, with:
- tiers from Spark to Hypernova (recalibrated in September 2026)
- streaks
- private leagues (added August 2026)
- monthly Wrapped share cards
- README badges
- an opt-in /hire board that lists engineers by measured usage.
It covers many agents beyond Claude Code and checks submissions on the server (per-model cost floors, token math, date sanity). It also offers a daily autosubmit through launchd, systemd or Task Scheduler, and an MCP server.
products.overlap_with_reference:
The two overlap only on gamification and history: both show token usage, multi-day history and streaks.

**viberank:**
- a public, cross-user leaderboard of API-equivalent dollar spend, with fixed tiers and leagues
- web-based, with submission to the cloud
- supports many agents through ccusage
- has no live agent state, character, permission alerts, Go to it, AI recaps, levels based on your own history, or detection of test results, loops or drift.

**The reference:**
- local-only, no account
- Claude Code only
- no leaderboard.

The two could complement each other rather than compete directly.

products.name: Vibe Buddy
products.scope_note: The discovery URL (chatgate.ai) is an aggregator write-up. The official site moved from vibe-buddy.byvova.com to vibebuddy.sh (308 redirect), so vibebuddy.sh is the primary_url. Early listings (chatgate, updated 2026-08-31; aat.ee, 2026-08-06) give 81x54x25 mm and shipping around September 2026, and aat.ee shows a $59 pre-order. The current site (re-read 2026-11-18) gives 82x50x34 mm, US$49, shipping 'around November 2026', and still calls the product 'a working prototype' whose software is not finished. Web search was unavailable during this check (budget used up), so no wider search for shipping news or reviews could be run. Facts come from pages opened directly, from the CLI binary's strings (2026.11.17.1, read but not run) and from the product photos.
products.one_liner: Palm-size, battery-powered orange desk robot linked over Bluetooth (or USB) to a companion CLI. Its 2-inch colour screen shows an animated face, Codex or Claude Code 5-hour/7-day usage-limit percentages and reset times, counts of running and finished tasks, and the agent's state (idle, working, needs you, done, out of limits).

agent_status.note: The face changes when the AI is working, needs an answer or approval, is done, or is out of limits (vibebuddy.sh FAQ 'What can it do?'). The CLI's face-state enum is idle/working/needs_you/done/out_of_limit. In the out-of-limit state 'Buddy counts down until your limit resets' (CLI 2026.11.17.1 strings, https://cli.vibebuddy.sh/releases/2026.11.17.1/vibebuddy-linux-x64).

multi_session.note: Only aggregate counts: 'The top-left number counts tasks running now' and 'The top-right number counts finished tasks' (CLI strings). The robot shows one selected agent (Codex or Claude Code) at a time, chosen in the CLI. There is no per-session overview or switching.

permission_alert.note: The 'needs you' face covers 'A question, approval or error' (CLI strings), and the screen wakes from sleep 'when an AI agent works or needs you'. It is visual only, with no sound.

approve_from_device.note: The robot has no documented input. Data flows one way: the CLI 'sends only limits, task counts, and the display state to the robot' (vibebuddy.sh FAQ). The Claude hooks only observe; the CLI strings contain no hook decision output.

jump_to_session.note: The robot has no input, and neither the site nor the CLI strings describe focusing a terminal or editor window.

token_usage_cost.note: Shows usage only as a percentage of plan limits. The site gives no token counts or $ cost. The CLI data model holds provider-reported credits and extra-usage spending, but no source shows these on the robot.

plan_limits.note: Shows Codex and Claude Code usage percentages and reset times for personal and business accounts (vibebuddy.sh). The photos show '5H 72% ends 5:17 AM' and '7D 60% ends Jul 23'. A 'Limits only' screen mode shows full-screen usage cards (CLI strings).

personal_baseline_levels.note: Shows provider-reported percentages of plan limits. No source describes levels computed from the user's own history.

test_build_red_green.note: The face states are only idle, working, needs_you, done and out_of_limit (CLI enum). The site describes no test or build results.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Not among the five face states, and not described anywhere.

drift_away_detection.note: Not among the five face states. Screen sleep and wake follow agent activity, not where the user is.

ai_session_recap.note: Only limits, task counts and display state reach the robot (vibebuddy.sh FAQ). No summaries are described.

history_dashboard.note: No history or analytics view appears on the site, the install page or in the CLI's settings UI strings (agent, screen, brightness, working/done faces, start at login). The CLI keeps an internal 'usage history', which it uses to detect quota changes.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Not described on the site or in the CLI. The product only shows limits and status.

leaderboard.note: No accounts or social features. No account is required, and data stays local (vibebuddy.sh FAQ).

character_personality.note: An orange pixel robot whose animated face changes by state. You can choose faces for some states (for example glasses, happy, love; 'Glasses + Sparkle'; five face pools in the CLI). The site captions a photo 'isn't it cute?'.

sound_voice_out.note: The site mentions no speaker or sound, the CLI strings contain no sound or speaker terms, the site's demo MP4s have no audio track, and the Waveshare board spec lists no speaker (https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-LCD-2).

voice_input.note: No microphone or dictation is described. Data flows only from the computer to the robot.

physical_controls.note: No buttons or touch are described. The CLI says 'No pairing-mode button is needed', and sleep, wake, brightness and face choice are all set from the CLI. The photos show only a screen on the front.

second_screen_mode.note: A dedicated device with its own 2-inch colour screen, running on battery or USB-C (vibebuddy.sh; panel spec inferred, see hardware).

products.price_text: As of 2026-11-18 (vibebuddy.sh): US$49, shipping not included (the HK page lists HK$379). A fully refundable US$5 deposit, taken through Stripe, reserves a unit and counts toward the price. Before production the maker emails to collect the remaining US$44 plus shipping and applicable taxes. There is no early-bird tier. The aat.ee launch listing (2026-08-06) showed a $59 pre-order price. On Product Hunt the maker wrote 'I decreased the price, now it's $49'. The chatgate write-up (updated 2026-08-31) already shows $49.
products.license: None published. The CLI is distributed only as closed prebuilt binaries from cli.vibebuddy.sh: a Go binary, with the macOS build signed and notarized. Firmware is served from firmware.vibebuddy.sh. Neither maker has a public GitHub repo for Vibe Buddy firmware or CLI (vovapyc and aalizelau repo lists, as of 2026-11-18).
products.privacy_note: A local CLI reads usage and activity on the computer and sends only limits, task counts and display state to the robot over Bluetooth (or USB). The vendor says prompts, keys, tokens and account details stay on the computer. The CLI sends anonymous usage stats and error reports by default; setting DO_NOT_TRACK=1 turns them off. No account is required. These are vendor claims and have not been independently verified.
products.distinctive: One of the few hardware gadgets for AI-coding agents available to order (as a pre-order). It focuses on plan-limit percentages and reset times for Codex and Claude Code, plus five face states and running/finished task counts. The robot is a 3D-printed case around what the CLI names as a Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-2 module, battery powered and linked over Bluetooth. A cross-platform CLI hooks into the agents. Two makers in Canada build it.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlap: both put a robot character on the desk that reflects Claude Code state (working, waiting for permission or input, done), and the reference's optional DIY ESP32 desk screen is a similar small-display idea. Differences: Vibe Buddy is sold hardware ($49 pre-order, Bluetooth, battery) and also supports Codex. Its main data point is plan usage-limit % and reset times (5-hour/7-day), which the reference does not track. It shows only five coarse states and running/finished task counts, with no input on the device. The reference is free macOS software with intensity levels calibrated to the user's own 30-day history, moment reactions (test/build red-green, loops, drifting to another app, long sessions), a Go-to-it button, a daily goal and streak, AI recaps and a 30-day history dashboard. Vibe Buddy's site and CLI show none of these.

products.hardware: Palm-size robot: 82 x 50 x 34 mm on the current site (earlier listings said 81 x 54 x 25 mm). Colour landscape LCD showing an animated pixel face, 5H/7D usage % with reset times, and task counters. Inferred display and chip: the CLI 2026.11.17.1 contains the firmware board target 'waveshare-esp32-s3-lcd-2', and Waveshare's ESP32-S3-LCD-2 is a 2-inch 240x320 IPS LCD (ST7789T3, SPI) on an ESP32-S3R8 with BLE 5, a Li-ion charging circuit and USB-C (https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-LCD-2). The CLI's API docs say the robot ID is 'derived from the full ESP32 factory MAC'. Screen modes are 'Face + limits' and 'Limits only' (full-screen usage cards), with brightness adjustable from the CLI. Built-in battery charged over USB-C (the CLI reads the battery in mV), so it can run unplugged. Linked over Bluetooth, or over USB when connected. Firmware updates go through the CLI. Orange 3D-printed enclosure. No user buttons, touch or speaker are documented.

products.name: CodexBar
products.scope_note: Upstream project steipete/CodexBar. Search results also show many forks and mirrors named CodexBar, and TokenBar, a paid app built on CodexBar's code. Those are separate products and are not profiled here. The README also lists community front-ends (Windows via WSL2, GNOME, KDE Plasma, Waybar, COSMIC and others), which are separate projects.
products.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app (with a Linux Qt desktop app and a CLI) that shows session, weekly and monthly usage limits, reset countdowns, credits and spend for Codex, Claude Code and over 100 other AI providers (114 in total).
agents_supported: OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock and other API providers (114 providers total)

agent_status.note: The opt-in Agent Sessions feature (v0.42.0) lists live local and SSH Codex, Claude Code and Pi-family sessions with a project or thread label. Opt-in Stay Awake (v0.67.0) adds a menu status indicator while a session is live. It does not show working, idle or waiting state, and the design doc lists permission-waiting state as a non-goal (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/CodexBar/main/docs/agent-sessions-design.md; CHANGELOG).

multi_session.note: Since v0.42.0 (2026-07-11) you can opt in to 'discover, list, and focus live local or SSH-connected Codex and Claude Code sessions from the menu and CLI'. It is off by default (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/CodexBar/main/CHANGELOG.md).

permission_alert.note: The design doc lists a permission-waiting state as a non-goal. Notifications cover quota use, upcoming resets, predictive pace alerts and credential expiry only.

approve_from_device.note: Agent Sessions only discovers, lists and focuses sessions. There is no approve or answer function.

jump_to_session.note: Local focus 'walks from the session PID to the owning terminal/editor application and raises the best matching window' when Accessibility permission is granted. Remote focus runs the same command over SSH. Exact tmux pane focus is a non-goal (agent-sessions-design.md).

token_usage_cost.note: Shows credit balances, Admin API spend dashboards, local cost scans for Codex and Claude (also as 'codexbar cost'), and per-provider 30-day costs in dollars and tokens (README; justgeek.fr review).

plan_limits.note: This is the core feature: per-provider session (5-hour), weekly and monthly windows with countdowns to the next reset. The menu bar icon is a two-bar meter (session and weekly). The Codex and Claude menus show a quota burndown with an even-use guide. Opt-in predictive pace alerts were added in v0.42.0 (README; CHANGELOG). Covers 114 providers as of 2026-11-18 (up from about 80 in September); Linux desktop app and CLI exist too.

personal_baseline_levels.note: Pace, burndown and predictive pace alerts are measured against even use within the quota window, not against the user's own history (README; CHANGELOG 0.42.0).

test_build_red_green.note: The Agent Sessions design says it 'never loads prompt/tool transcript bodies', so it cannot see test or build results.

loop_stuck_detection.note: It does not read transcripts or track agent state beyond whether a session is live (design doc).

drift_away_detection.note: It does not track whether the agent is waiting (a stated non-goal) or which app the user is in.

ai_session_recap.note: It never loads transcript bodies and has no summarization feature.

history_dashboard.note: Settings → Usage & Spend is a persistent view with daily, hourly, project and session breakdowns. A token-activity heatmap arrived in v0.48.0 (2026-08-06) and the view was rebuilt in v0.53.0 (2026-08-18). v0.73.0 (2026-10-07) added week and month grouping with drill-down and made the existing annual activity grid readable in Dark mode. There are also inline 30-day cost charts and History and Burn Down widgets. Codex history is kept in a SQLite store (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/CodexBar/main/CHANGELOG.md; README).

streaks_goals_achievements.note: The only celebration is confetti when a weekly limit resets. Neither the README nor the changelog mentions streaks, goals, XP or badges.

leaderboard.note: There is no CodexBar account and no compare feature. Since v0.44.0 there is a 'private local share card' for Usage & Spend (an image or copied totals), but it does not rank you against other users (CHANGELOG).

character_personality.note: The menu bar icon is a usage meter. The only flourish is reset confetti. There is no mascot or character.

sound_voice_out.note: The README mentions optional quota notifications and the changelog has no entry about sounds. The sources do not say whether notifications play a sound.

voice_input.note: It is a read-only monitor that does not send prompts to agents.

physical_controls.note: Software only.

second_screen_mode.note: It runs in the menu bar and offers WidgetKit widgets for the desktop and Notification Center. There is no dedicated full-screen or device display.

products.price_text: Free and open source under the MIT license. It installs from GitHub Releases or Homebrew: the README now gives 'brew install --cask codexbar', and codexbar.app still shows 'brew install --cask steipete/tap/codexbar'. Linux options are an AUR package and Linux tarballs. Updates arrive through Sparkle. No paid tier was found (as of 2026-11-18).
products.license: MIT
products.privacy_note: There is no CodexBar account or server. The README says parsing happens on-device by default. The app reuses existing provider sessions (OAuth, device flow, API keys, local files) and, if you opt in, browser cookies, so no passwords are stored. It then queries each provider's own usage endpoints and polls provider status. Agent-aware refresh and Agent Sessions ask before inspecting the process list and never load transcript bodies. Keychain access can be turned off. Opt-in iCloud Sync (off by default) syncs provider configuration, some preferences and per-device usage snapshots across Macs via CloudKit, with secrets in end-to-end-encrypted fields (CHANGELOG).
products.distinctive: It covers far more providers than any other tool in this market: 114, from Codex and Claude to Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, OpenRouter and Bedrock. All of them show in one menu bar meter with reset countdowns, burndown charts, widgets and a CLI. It is also very popular, with about 23.2k GitHub stars as of 2026-11-18. An opt-in Agent Sessions mode lists live Codex, Claude Code and Pi sessions, including ones over SSH, and focuses the terminal or editor that owns a session. A Stay Awake option keeps the Mac awake while sessions are live.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are free macOS apps that put Claude Code usage outside the terminal, and both can bring a session's terminal window to the front: CodexBar through opt-in Agent Sessions focus, the reference through 'Go to it'. CodexBar is an open-source quota, spend and limits tracker for 114 providers, with Linux and CLI support. It has no character or robot, no intensity levels measured against your own history, and no reactions to events such as tests failing then passing, permission waits, loops or drifting away. It also has no AI recaps, no daily goal or streak (only confetti when a limit resets) and no second-screen or desk hardware. The reference does not focus on plan-limit windows and reset countdowns, which are CodexBar's core.

products.name: Usagebar
products.scope_note: In scope: a usage and limit monitor for Claude Code. The GitHub URL github.com/hsnsdt/usagebar is not the source of this Mac app. It holds UsageTray, a separate Windows tray app by Sedat Okutan (okutan.org). As of 2026-11-18 it is MIT-licensed with 2 stars, 0 forks and 15 commits, and the README shows it is built with Tauri and Rust. The README calls it "the Windows counterpart of Usagebar on macOS" but does not say the two are affiliated. UsageTray has 24-hour, 7-day and 30-day usage history, CSV export, a 7-day token chart and an extra-usage spend display; those are not Usagebar features. No public repo for the macOS Usagebar app was found. unverified: the repo's creation date of 2026-09-22 (the GitHub API returned rate-limit and 403 errors during this check) and React in its stack.
products.one_liner: A paid macOS menu bar app ($9 one-time) for Claude Code. It shows how much of the 5-hour and weekly limits you have used, with reset timers, alerts at 50/75/90%, a low-context warning and today's message and token counts.

agent_status.note: The official feature list covers only limits, reset timers, notifications, context, model advice and auth. Its states (Normal / Almost hit / Context low) are usage states, not agent states.

multi_session.note: The mockup shows context for a single project. In Product Hunt comments the maker said it matches /usage and does not support teams. A question about multiple accounts got no answer.

permission_alert.note: Notifications cover usage thresholds (50/75/90%) and low context only.

token_usage_cost.note: Shows % used of the 5-hour and weekly windows, context tokens left (e.g. '88K left, 43% used of 155K usable'), and today's message and token counts ('Today Messages: 6 Tokens: 753.2K') in the homepage mockup. No $ cost is shown.

plan_limits.note: Live percentage for the rolling 5-hour and weekly windows, reset timers, a switch to a countdown near the limit, and notifications at 50%, 75% and 90%.

history_dashboard.note: Not on the current feature list; only today's totals are shown. At launch the maker said history and per-model breakdowns would be 'on the roadmap' (producthunt.com/products/usagebar). The Windows UsageTray has history, but it is a different product.

sound_voice_out.note: Uses system notifications. Sound is not mentioned.

physical_controls.note: Software only.

second_screen_mode.note: Menu bar popover only.

products.price_text: As of 2026-11-18 the human-facing homepage says "Get for Mac $9 — one-time, lifetime updates". Every buy button goes to a Stripe checkout (buy.stripe.com), and the JSON-LD offer is $9 USD. The markdown version of the homepage served to agents adds "(a free tier is also available)" but does not say what it includes. The maker's own blog (October 2026) says it costs "$9 as a one-time purchase" and names only /usage and the web dashboard as free alternatives. The DMG (v1.0.3) is publicly downloadable from usagebar.com, but whether it needs a licence key is unknown. At the Product Hunt launch on 2026-01-23 the maker called it "Pay What You Want", and Product Hunt still shows "Free Options". A competitor's page (sessionwatcher.com, checked 2026-10-06) found no free tier or trial.
products.license: Proprietary: the macOS app has no public source. At launch the maker said "Plan is to open source this too", but no repo was found. The hsnsdt/usagebar repo is the unrelated MIT-licensed Windows app UsageTray.
products.privacy_note: Reads Claude Code's OAuth credentials from the macOS Keychain and calls Anthropic's usage endpoint directly. No account or API key is needed. The site says no data leaves the machine except that call to Anthropic. The maker also said it reads local .json logs as a fallback and for API users. Since v1.0.3 it auto-updates through a Sparkle-style appcast at usagebar.com/appcast.xml, so it also checks usagebar.com for updates. It is distributed as a DMG outside the App Store. The website itself uses Plausible analytics.
products.distinctive: A narrow limit meter for Claude Code only: live 5-hour and weekly percentages in the menu bar, reset timers, threshold notifications, a low-context warning (1M-context detection added in v1.0.3) and today's message and token counts, plus 'model awareness' tips on moving from Opus to Sonnet or Haiku. The site doubles as an SEO funnel, with about 200 blog posts, a free 7-day Claude Code email course, and a sister app, Quickshot.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlap is small. Both are local-first macOS apps for Claude Code with no account. Usagebar tracks subscription limits (5-hour and weekly %, reset times, 50/75/90% alerts, low context, today's tokens), which the reference does not focus on. It has none of the reference's features: no character, no intensity levels or personal baseline, no moment detection (tests, permission waits, loops, drift), no Go to it, no goals or streaks, no AI recaps, no history dashboard, no second-screen mode and no desk hardware. Usagebar is sold for $9 one-time (an unexplained free tier is mentioned only in its agent-facing markdown); the reference is free.

products.name: VibeKeys
products.scope_note: This is a real, shipping product line from Second State Inc. with three keypads: Pro (wired), Plus (wireless) and Max (screen, mic, Wi-Fi remote). The same maker sells VibeBuddy ($69), a separate desk box that shows a task card and speaks a short line when agents need you, finish or fail. VibeBuddy's features are not counted here.
products.one_liner: A small keypad for AI coding with six clicky keys and a knob (Accept, Retry, YOLO, ESC, Voice, Usage). The $99 Max model adds an ESP32-S3 screen that shows live status for several Claude Code or Codex sessions, a microphone for voice prompts, and a Wi-Fi remote mode that mirrors and drives the agent's terminal over MQTT.

agent_status.note: Max only. In keyboard mode, vibekeys_app hooks for Claude Code and Codex send session events to the device over BLE. The screen shows one row per session, colored by state: dark green for work/tool/post, dark goldenrod for perm, dark orange for note/done, dark red for err. The docs say it shows the current operation (generating, thinking, running a tool), the user's query, whether the work is finished and 'Waiting for your input'. In the remote-mode picker, white means working and orange means stopped or waiting. Pro and Plus have no display. Sources: https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_firmware, https://vibekeys.dev/docs/claude-code-status/, https://vibekeys.dev/docs/codex-status/

multi_session.note: Max only. Keyboard mode keeps a table of up to 16 sessions, dropping the least recently active, and puts perm/err/done/note at the top. Sessions time out after 30 minutes. Remote mode lists every running vibetty session, and the knob switches between them without reconnecting. Sources: https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_firmware, https://vibekeys.dev/docs/remote-mode/

permission_alert.note: Max only. A Claude Code Notification(permission_prompt) or a Codex PermissionRequest maps to 'perm', shown as a dark goldenrod row meaning 'waiting for your permission' and sorted to the top. The status docs also list 'Waiting for your input'. The alert is visual only, because the Max has no speaker. Sources: https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_app, https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_firmware, https://vibekeys.dev/docs/claude-code-status/

approve_from_device.note: On every model, Accept sends Enter, ESC rejects and YOLO sends Shift+Tab ('allow all edits'). The Codex key profile maps YOLO to 'y' to approve. In keyboard mode these are plain keystrokes, so the agent's window must be focused. In Max remote mode (vibetty over MQTT), ACCEPT, NEXT and ESC send Enter, down-arrow and Esc straight to the chosen session's terminal, which the device shows. Sources: https://vibekeys.dev/docs/remote-mode/, https://vibekeys.dev/docs/codex-status/

jump_to_session.note: Max only, and only for sessions on an Omarchy (Hyprland) host or with a herdr win_id. Pressing the knob opens a session picker, and confirming sends a focus request that vibekeys_app uses to raise that window. Other sessions are grayed out and can't be selected. Source: https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_firmware

token_usage_cost.note: Only as a shortcut. The Pro's default 'Usage' key is labeled 'Token stats' ('Am I about to hit the token limit?'). It is remappable, the keystroke or command it sends is not documented, and no VibeKeys device shows usage itself. The Max page, docs and repos never mention tokens or cost. Source: https://vibekeys.dev/vibekeys-pro.html

plan_limits.note: The only hint is the Usage key text 'Am I about to hit the token limit?'. No limit tracking is documented anywhere.

personal_baseline_levels.note: The documented status set is fixed (work/tool/post/perm/note/done/err/end), with no intensity levels. Source: https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_app

test_build_red_green.note: Marketing says the Max screen shows 'build status' (Max page) and 'build progress' (blog), but the documented hook statuses have no test or build state. Only StopFailure maps to 'err'.

loop_stuck_detection.note: The documented hook-to-status mapping has no such state. Source: https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_app

drift_away_detection.note: The documented hook-to-status mapping has no such state. Source: https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_app

ai_session_recap.note: Not mentioned on the site, in the docs or in the repos. The status screen shows the user's query, not a summary.

history_dashboard.note: Not mentioned. The companion software is a BLE CLI with hooks.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Not mentioned.

leaderboard.note: Not mentioned.

character_personality.note: A keypad with a status table and a terminal view, with no mascot. The maker's separate VibeBuddy is a different device.

sound_voice_out.note: The Max page says the device has no speaker, Bluetooth audio or headphone output, and the maker is 'not promising one'. Pro and Plus have no audio output, only clicky switches. Source: https://vibekeys.dev/vibekeys-max.html

voice_input.note: On Pro and Plus, the Voice key toggles a host dictation app such as Typeless or Wispr Flow. On the Max in keyboard mode, MIC either sends Ctrl+Option to host dictation or, with built-in ASR on, records with its own mic, sends the audio to a Whisper-compatible endpoint you set up (Groq, OpenAI or self-hosted whisper.cpp/faster-whisper) and types the text over Bluetooth. In remote mode the transcript opens in an on-device editor, and ACCEPT sends it to the Claude Code or Codex terminal. PTT and toggle modes are both available. Sources: https://vibekeys.dev/docs/keyboard-voice-input/, https://vibekeys.dev/docs/voice-input/

physical_controls.note: Pro and Plus have six clicky remappable keys and a push rotary knob, and the Plus adds a layer button. The Max has ACCEPT, ESC, NEXT, BACKSPACE, YOLO/SWITCH, CUSTOM (/compact) and MIC keys (Kailh Blue hot-swap) and a push rotary knob. Sources: https://vibekeys.dev/vibekeys-pro.html, https://github.com/second-state/vibekeys_firmware

second_screen_mode.note: Max only. It has its own SPI LCD: V1 is 1.69in 240x280 and V2 is 1.47in 172x320. Source: https://vibekeys.dev/docs/

products.price_text: As of 2026-11-18 on vibekeys.dev: VibeKeys Pro $39 (wired), VibeKeys Plus $49 (wireless, 'Most popular'), VibeKeys Max $99 (3D printed to order, ships in 5 business days, delivery in 10-16 days), VibeBuddy (separate product) $69. Black Friday 2026 runs Nov 17 to Dec 1, 11:59pm PT, and is applied automatically in the cart with no code: $5 off any order (Pro $34, Plus $44, Max $94, VibeBuddy $64), $10 off orders of $138 or more, and $20 off orders of $168 or more. The Max early-bird price of $69 ended June 1, 2026 (Wayback captures of the Max page from 2026-05-21 and 2026-06-01; the comparison blog still shows $69). Free worldwide shipping with import duties and taxes included. Pro and Plus pages state a 1-year warranty.
products.license: The vibekeys_app CLI and hook plugin is GPL-3.0. The vibekeys_firmware (Rust, ESP32-S3) and vibetty repos are public but have no license: no LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt or COPYING file on main, and no license field in Cargo.toml (checked 2026-11-18). Even so, the Max page calls the firmware and service 'fully open source'. The maker's comparison blog lists Pro and Plus firmware as closed.
products.privacy_note: No account is needed. Pro and Plus act as USB or Bluetooth HID keyboards. On the Max, vibekeys_app hooks send session events to the device over BLE, and setup uses Web Bluetooth. Remote mode uses MQTT, either vibetty's built-in LAN broker (no auth, LAN only) or a cloud broker you choose, such as EMQX (credentials go in the URL, mqtts for TLS). Voice audio goes to an ASR endpoint you configure (Groq or OpenAI cloud, or self-hosted Whisper).
products.hardware: Pro: wired USB-C (1.5m cable), six clicky mechanical switches with PBT laser-etched keycaps, a rotary knob, ABS body, plug-and-play with no drivers, macOS and Windows. Plus: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi with USB-C charging, up to 15 days of battery, three key layers with L1/L2/L3 LEDs, RGB lighting only over USB, macOS, Windows and Linux. Max: ESP32-S3 with octal PSRAM running Rust firmware. Its SPI LCD is 1.69in 240x280 (V1) or 1.47in 172x320 (V2), marketed as 'TFT' and called 'OLED' on the blog, and the firmware also supports an optional I2C OLED. It has an I2S mic with an esp-sr front end, Bluetooth 5.0, Wi-Fi and USB-C, and a rechargeable lithium battery for up to 5h of continuous use. There is no speaker. Switches are Kailh Blue hot-swap, the case is 3D printed to order in a custom color, it measures about 130x90x30mm and weighs about 150g, and it gets OTA updates.
