products.distinctive: It is one of the few AI-coding keypads you can buy now: a $39 wired macro pad with dedicated Accept/Retry/YOLO/ESC/Voice/Usage keys. The Max, sold as open source although only the app repo carries a license, adds a color-coded table of up to 16 Claude Code and Codex sessions with 'waiting for permission' rows pushed to the top. It can also mirror and drive a live agent terminal over MQTT through the maker's vibetty bridge, and takes Whisper voice input from its own mic, so you can approve and prompt from across the room.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both show Claude Code state (working, waiting for permission, done or failed) outside the terminal on a small desk screen. VibeKeys is mainly a commercial input device. It lets you approve from the device (Enter, ESC and Shift+Tab keys, plus remote terminal mirroring), takes voice prompts, and works across agents: Claude Code and Codex through hooks, and others through keyboard shortcuts. It has a real multi-session picker, but window focus works only on Omarchy or herdr hosts. The reference is a free, software-first macOS app with a pixel robot character. It sets intensity levels from the user's own history, detects moments such as tests failing and then passing, loops and drift, and has daily goals and streaks, AI recaps and a 30-day dashboard. VibeKeys has none of these: no character, no gamification, no analytics and no sound (no speaker). The reference has no physical keys, no voice and no approve-from-device, and its DIY ESP32 screen is not sold.

products.name: Agent Paperclip
products.one_liner: Open-source Electron desktop pet, a Clippy-style paperclip by default, that shows Claude Code and Codex CLI status, context-token use and the 5-hour plan usage, with optional sounds when the agent is waiting or done.

agent_status.note: The pet shows seven live states (Thinking, Reading, Working, Waiting, Idle, Done, Error) from Claude Code hooks and from tailing Codex session files. A speech bubble shows the current action, for example 'Reading index.ts...'.

multi_session.note: Since PR #3 (merged 2026-03-07) a count badge appears when more than one session is active (SessionCount.tsx), and tokens are shown per session (up to 3, then '+N'). The most recently active session drives the pet's status. There is no per-session status view and no switching between sessions. https://github.com/fredruss/agent-paperclip/pull/3

permission_alert.note: The Waiting state means the agent 'Needs your permission or has a question'. It is set from Claude Code Notification hooks (permission_prompt, elicitation_dialog, idle_prompt) in src/hooks/status-reporter.ts. An optional sound plays on Waiting.

approve_from_device.note: The README lists only drag and right-click as controls. In the source (Pet.tsx, main/index.ts), left-click only drags, and the right-click menu holds just the sticker pack choice and a Sound toggle. There is no approve/deny UI.

jump_to_session.note: Pet.tsx has no click-to-focus handler. Left-click drags the pet and right-click opens the pack/sound menu.

token_usage_cost.note: Shows current context-window tokens (input plus cache, formatted as k/M), per session since PR #3. No dollar cost.

plan_limits.note: When idle, a badge shows the share of the 5-hour session window used and the time to reset, e.g. 'Claude: 42% · 3h'. It reads Claude's statusLine rate_limits.five_hour, and Codex's primary/secondary windows since PR #7 (2026-04-16, Codex tested only on macOS). Paid plans only. products.privacy_note: Status is written to ~/.agent-paperclip/status.json (and sessions.json). It records tool names, filenames, the first word of bash commands, search patterns cut to 20 characters, thinking snippets of about 40 characters, and token counts. It does not record prompts, replies to the user, file contents or full commands. The README says all data stays local and is never sent anywhere.
products.distinctive: A tongue-in-cheek Clippy-style paperclip pet with swappable illustrated sticker packs: a paperclip, a cartoon robot, a cloud, an SVG face, and a community Gandalf pack on main only. It covers both Claude Code (hooks) and Codex CLI (passive session-file tailing). It is cross-platform via Electron and shows context-token use and a 5-hour plan usage badge alongside a live status.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are free, local-first desktop pets driven by Claude Code hooks. Both show live agent state, flag when Claude is waiting for permission or input, and need no account. Agent Paperclip goes further on breadth: it also supports Codex CLI, runs on Windows and Linux, and shows context-window tokens, a 5-hour plan usage percentage with reset time, a session count, and Waiting/Done sounds. It lacks most of what sets the reference apart: personal-baseline intensity levels, test/build fail-then-pass reactions, loop and drift detection, long-session and goal moments, a 'Go to it' jump to the terminal, AI session recaps, a daily goal and streak, a history dashboard, a full-screen second-monitor scene and a DIY desk-screen option. Its character is an illustrated sticker per state with simple CSS motion (sway, bounce, tilt, pulse, shake). One pack (Bot1) is a cartoon robot, but none is pixel art and none has frame-by-frame animation.

products.name: Pixel Agents
products.scope_note: In scope. The repo moved from pablodelucca/pixel-agents to the org repo pixel-agents-hq/pixel-agents. The old URL returns a 301 redirect to the new one (checked 2026-11-18). Several GitHub forks and clones exist (pixel-agents-codex, zep-pixel-agents, Agent Friday's pixel office, Pixel Agent Desk), and a different extension with the same name by "Hootbu" is on the Marketplace. None of these are this product. unverified: the names of the clones and the Hootbu extension were not re-checked.
products.one_liner: A free, open-source (MIT) VS Code extension and standalone browser/phone app that shows each Claude Code session as an animated pixel-art character in a pixel office you can edit. Characters type, read and run commands as the agent does, and show speech bubbles and optional chimes when the agent needs input. It also has plan-limit and context "health bars".

agent_status.note: Characters animate to match live activity: they type when the agent edits, read when it searches and run commands (README). An idle agent rests and blinks (v1.6.0). By default status comes from Claude Code hooks, with JSONL transcript polling as a fallback. Waiting shows a green checkmark bubble (CLAUDE.md). Also runs outside VS Code: `npx pixel-agents` serves the office in a browser; listed on Open VSX. Roadmap names Codex, Gemini and Cursor.

multi_session.note: Each agent terminal gets its own character, and sub-agents and teammates get their own characters too (README). Agent cards line the office edge in VS Code, and desktop and phone share the same cards (v1.5.0/v1.6.0). 'Watch All Sessions' adopts sessions from other workspaces.

permission_alert.note: README: 'speech bubbles, plus optional chimes, when an agent needs input or permission or finishes its turn.' In hooks mode the PermissionRequest hook drives this. In heuristic mode a permission bubble appears after a 7 s timer with no data. The docs describe only in-office bubbles and the chime; no OS-level notification is documented.

approve_from_device.note: There are no allow/deny buttons. The standalone browser or phone app has an embedded terminal where you can type answers (v1.5.0: 'launch, watch, type into and close agents without VS Code'). On a phone an accessory key bar adds esc, tab, shift+tab, an arrow trackpad and more (CLAUDE.md). In VS Code you answer in the VS Code terminal.

jump_to_session.note: v1.5.0 changelog for agent cards in VS Code: 'clicking one raises its terminal and selects the character.' Clicking a sub-agent focuses its parent's terminal. On a phone, tapping a card first focuses the character, then opens its terminal (CLAUDE.md). Website: 'click-to-open terminals'.

token_usage_cost.note: Each agent has a context 'health bar' showing how much context is left. It is computed from the newest turn's input and cache tokens, coloured by share used (CLAUDE.md), and is called 'token fuel gauges' for teams in v1.4.0. There is no token total and no $ cost.

plan_limits.note: Opt-in usage bars show a weekly bar over a 5-hour bar with the % of plan left inside each, and reset times appear on hover (CLAUDE.md; v1.6.0 changelog). The data is Claude Code's statusLine rate_limits, read through a bridge that wraps your statusLine (subscribers only, after a session's first reply). On Windows, a custom status line is not wrapped yet.

personal_baseline_levels.note: Nothing in the README, changelog or 128k-character developer doc (CLAUDE.md) describes activity levels relative to the user's own history.

test_build_red_green.note: The developer doc and changelog describe no detection of test, build or type-check pass/fail results.

loop_stuck_detection.note: No loop or stuck detection is described. There is only an internal 30 s stale-session scan (CLAUDE.md).

drift_away_detection.note: 'Idle detection' in CLAUDE.md is about the agent's turn ending (turn_duration and a 5 s text-idle timer), not about the user being away.

ai_session_recap.note: Conversation titles are read from Claude Code's own transcript fields (custom-title, ai-title, last-prompt). Pixel Agents writes no summaries or recaps of its own.

history_dashboard.note: Recent conversations per Directory, with 'Show 5 more' and a title search, can be resumed with one click (v1.6.0). This is in the standalone office only (left sidebar or phone menu). There are no analytics or stats across days or weeks.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: No XP, streaks or achievements. The README roadmap lists 'Scores for whatever you care about' as a future 'Actually a game' goal and says 'Most of this is still ahead.'

leaderboard.note: No leaderboard or team comparison appears in the README, changelog, developer doc or roadmap.

character_personality.note: Pixel-art characters walk to desks, type, read, blink and rest, with speech bubbles. A Characters view designs them from a wardrobe with a pixel editor (v1.6.0). Animated pets (Claudio, Gitcat) can be petted (v1.4.0).

sound_voice_out.note: An optional ascending two-note chime (E5 to E6, Web Audio) plays when the waiting bubble appears (CLAUDE.md), and the README says chimes come with input, permission and finished-turn bubbles. The 'office radio' plays procedural 8-bit music with shareable song codes, and only when you press play (v1.6.0). There is no speech.

voice_input.note: No voice, microphone or dictation feature appears in the README, website, changelog or developer doc (no microphone or getUserMedia mention). Audio is used only for the chime and the radio.

physical_controls.note: Software only, with no hardware. The phone web app uses the phone's own touchscreen like any other app UI.

second_screen_mode.note: The standalone 'npx pixel-agents' serves the office as a browser app you could place on another monitor. Over Tailscale it becomes a home-screen web app on a phone, with the office and terminal as full-screen pages (v1.5.0). There is no dedicated hardware or explicit second-monitor mode.

products.price_text: Free and open source (MIT) as of 2026-11-18. There is no paid tier, Pro plan or waitlist on pixel-agents.com, and the Marketplace lists it as Free. Donations go through GitHub Sponsors and Ko-fi. Before v1.1.0, the v1.0.2 README said the full furniture catalog needed Donarg's 'Office Interior Tileset (16x16)', sold on itch.io for $2 USD and imported by hand. Without it you got basic characters and layout. v1.1.0 'replaces bundled proprietary tileset with open-source assets loaded via a manifest system', and v1.2.0 added external asset packs.
products.license: MIT
products.privacy_note: Runs locally in VS Code or as a local Node server, with no account. It reads Claude Code hooks and transcripts and doesn't modify Claude Code. Hooks are added only after consent. The standalone server uses a local token, and a client without it is read-only. Remote or phone access is the user's own optional choice, for example Tailscale Serve. Usage bars wrap the user's statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json after a confirmation step, and the bridge POSTs only rate_limits and context share to local Pixel Agents servers.

products.distinctive: A whole pixel-art office with one character per Claude Code session, including sub-agents and teammates. It has a layout editor, a character designer, pets and procedural 8-bit 'office radio'. It shows game-style 'health bars' for the 5-hour and weekly plan limits (% left, reset times) and for each agent's remaining context. It runs in a VS Code panel or as a standalone browser and phone app with an embedded terminal. It is one of the most popular projects in this category: about 10.3k stars, about 143k marketplace installs plus about 38k npm downloads, and the site claims 184k installs.
products.overlap_with_reference: Strong overlap in spirit. Both are free, local, Claude-Code-only pixel-art companions that show live agent state, alert when Claude waits for permission or finishes, and offer a one-click jump to the waiting terminal (Pixel Agents' agent cards raise the terminal). Differences: Pixel Agents lives in a VS Code panel or browser tab rather than on the macOS desktop, and runs on Windows and Linux too. It is built for many agents at once (an office of characters, sub-agents, embedded terminals, phone access over Tailscale) and adds plan-limit and context bars, which the reference lacks. It has none of the reference's motivational layer: no intensity levels against a personal baseline, no test or build fail-then-pass, loop, drift-away or long-session moments, no daily goal or streak, no AI recaps, no 30-day dashboard, and no DIY desk screen. Its roadmap mentions future 'scores' and game elements.

products.name: Vibe Island
products.one_liner: A paid native Swift macOS app that turns the MacBook notch into a control center for about 30 AI coding agents. It shows live session status and lets you allow or deny permissions, answer questions and review plans from the notch, with two-way control limited to Claude Code, OpenCode and MiMoCode. One click jumps to the exact terminal tab or pane, and it also tracks plan quotas.

agent_status.note: The notch panel shows live status for every running agent session. Sources: the site and the GitHub README ('Live session status for every running agent', https://github.com/vibeislandapp/vibe-island).

multi_session.note: All agents and sessions appear in one notch panel. After the 2-day trial, Free Mode shows only the current session, and multiple sessions need a license (site FAQ).

permission_alert.note: The notch expands with Allow/Deny buttons when an agent requests permission or asks a question, and notifications stay on in Free Mode. Alerts can be forwarded to an iPhone, mirrored to an Apple Watch, through the free Bark app (changelog 1.0.44, https://vibeisland.app/changelog; docs at https://vibeisland.app/docs/). Optional follow-up reminders ping once about requests still waiting (1.0.43).

approve_from_device.note: Allow or deny from the notch (the site mockup shows Deny ⌘N / Allow ⌘Y), answer AskUserQuestion options with a click or ⌘1-3, and preview plans in full Markdown before approving. Requires a license. Two-way control works only for Claude Code, OpenCode and MiMoCode; Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and the other agents are monitor-only (review dated 2026-08-29, https://vibecoding.app/blog/vibe-island-review).

jump_to_session.note: One click jumps to the exact tab or split pane in iTerm2, Ghostty, Terminal.app, Warp, WezTerm, Kitty, Zellij and IDE terminals (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf/Antigravity). It also works inside tmux across multiple sessions (1.0.37) and over SSH remote and cmux ssh (1.0.56). Some terminals fall back to only activating the app (1.0.42 mentions this fallback). Custom Jump Rules use a URL scheme plus a JSON rule (https://vibeisland.app/docs/). Requires a license.

token_usage_cost.note: No token or $ cost tracking per session. 1.0.56 added an optional output-speed (tok/s) display after the model name, and 1.0.55 shows Enterprise monthly limits in dollars (https://vibeisland.app/changelog).

plan_limits.note: The site says it shows remaining quota for Claude, Codex, Kimi, GLM and DeepSeek. Usage for Grok, Cursor, Kimi, MiniMax and Antigravity was added in 1.0.43 (2026-07-28). 1.0.55 added alerts when a 5-hour or weekly limit reaches 80% (the default), runs out or resets, and 1.0.56 shows Claude reset cards. Multiple accounts arrived in 1.0.45 and 1.0.48 (https://vibeisland.app/changelog).

personal_baseline_levels.note: Absent from the site, the README and the full 1.0.x changelog through v1.0.56.

test_build_red_green.note: No test or build-result detection anywhere in the changelog. 1.0.48 only stops tool failures from sounding like a whole-task failure, and the 'build' entries are about the app's own builds.

loop_stuck_detection.note: No loop or stuck detection in the site or the changelog through v1.0.56.

drift_away_detection.note: Presence-aware, but it does not detect drift to another app. Pop-ups are suppressed while you look at the agent's pane (1.0.53), and it stays silent in Focus mode, when the screen is locked, or while recording or sharing the screen (1.0.41). Usage and reset alerts wait while the Mac is asleep, locked or idle (1.0.56). Optional follow-up reminders ping once about requests still waiting or finished work you haven't looked at (1.0.43), and there is an idle-reminder sound toggle (~1.0.31) (https://vibeisland.app/changelog).

ai_session_recap.note: 1.0.33 surfaces Claude Code's own away-summary on idle session cards, and 1.0.45 adds 'session recaps for Codex and Grok'. The changelog doesn't say whether Vibe Island writes those recaps itself; no source shows it running its own AI summarizer (https://vibeisland.app/changelog).

history_dashboard.note: No history, stats or analytics view in the site, the README or the changelog. Usage shows only the current quota windows.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: No streaks, goals or achievements in the site or the changelog.

leaderboard.note: None. The site says 'No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry'.

character_personality.note: The changelog mentions a 'Pet' in minimized mode (1.0.28) and pixel-art glow and idle animations (1.0.7). The site, the vendor alternatives page and the third-party review describe no character, and no source shows it emoting (https://vibeisland.app/changelog).

sound_voice_out.note: '8-bit synthesized sounds for every event' and 'Import custom sound packs or craft your own' (site). It also has custom .wav/.mp3 per event (1.0.30), Quiet Hours (1.0.27) and a separate idle-reminder sound control. No text-to-speech is mentioned.

voice_input.note: No voice or dictation feature in the site, the docs or the changelog through v1.0.56.

physical_controls.note: Software only. Control is through on-screen buttons and keyboard shortcuts; no hardware or Stream Deck integration is listed.

second_screen_mode.note: On external displays and Macs without a notch it appears as a compact floating bar at the top center (site FAQ), and Follow Focus moves it across displays (1.0.27). There is no dedicated full-screen or separate-device mode. An iPhone app is only 'coming soon' with a waitlist (1.0.56).

products.price_text: As of 2026-11-18, the official site lists $19.99 one-time for 1 Mac, shown under an 'EARLY BIRD · PRICING' banner ('One-time purchase. No subscriptions.'). Tabs for 2 Macs and 3 Macs exist, but their prices are not visible on the page, the reel page or the alternatives page. Each license includes unlimited sessions and 1 year of updates; the app keeps working afterwards and renewal is optional. Every feature is free for 2 days with no card. After that, Free Mode shows the current session, notifications and usage, while multiple sessions, permission approval, answering questions, terminal jump and action shortcuts need a license. There is a 'Make a video, get up to 100% back' promo (vibeisland.app/reel/): 50% back at 2,000 organic views and 100% at 10,000 views on a single public video. Install by direct download or brew install --cask vibe-island. Unverified: earlier prices of $14.99 for 1 Mac and $34.99 for 3 Macs from April 2026 X posts (not seen on any official page).
products.license: Proprietary (closed source). The GitHub repo vibeislandapp/vibe-island is a 'community home' and issue tracker with README translations and SECURITY.md, no app source, no license file and no releases.
products.privacy_note: The site says 'No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry' and that session content, tool names and terminal metadata never leave the Mac. The changelog shows a network relay for license activation (1.0.0) and a server-authoritative trial system (1.0.10), so license and trial checks contact a server. The third-party review (2026-08-29) found no privacy policy page. Diagnostic reports are sent only when you export them. Optional iPhone and Watch alerts go through the third-party Bark app, and optional SSH Remote monitors agents on your own servers.
products.maker: Edward Luo, a solo developer. The site credits 'Built by Edward' and links to x.com/edwardluox; the full name comes from earlyterms.com. The launch post on @imedwardluo is attributed from a search snippet only.
products.maker_location: unverified: unknown (the maker posts in Chinese; no location is stated)
products.launch_date: v0.5.0 beta on 2026-03-03 (per earlyterms.com, a secondary source; the official changelog omits v0.x releases); v1.0.0 on 2026-03-27 (official changelog); public launch post on X on 2026-04-02 (date decoded from the post ID; post text not verified)
products.last_activity: v1.0.56 released 2026-11-14 (official changelog). It added a tok/s output-speed display, Claude usage-reset cards and a Liquid Glass panel option on macOS 26, plus an iPhone app listed as 'coming soon' with a beta waitlist in Settings.
products.hardware: none (software notch overlay). It runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs, uses under 100MB of RAM and needs macOS 14+ (stated on the reel page). Macs without a notch and external displays get a compact floating bar.
products.distinctive: It has the broadest agent coverage in the notch category: 30 agents and 20+ terminals, with precise split-pane, tmux and SSH jump and zero-config setup. It can approve, answer AskUserQuestion prompts and review Markdown plans from the notch with keyboard shortcuts, but only for Claude Code, OpenCode and MiMoCode. It also has quota alerts for 5-hour and weekly windows across many providers, SSH Remote and Bark phone and Watch forwarding. It ships very fast: v1.0.0 to v1.0.56 between 2026-03-27 and 2026-11-14.
products.overlap_with_reference:
Shared with the reference: a macOS desktop presence showing live agent status, permission-waiting alerts, a one-click jump to the waiting terminal, local-first operation with no account, and event sounds. Where Vibe Island goes beyond the reference:
- It is paid ($19.99 one-time) and multi-agent (about 30 agents, not just Claude Code).
- It approves, denies and answers from the notch for Claude Code, OpenCode and MiMoCode, which the reference deliberately does not.
- It adds plan review, 5-hour/weekly quota tracking and alerts, SSH remote agents and iPhone/Watch forwarding through Bark.
What it lacks that the reference has: personal-baseline intensity levels, moment detection (tests or builds failing then passing, loops, drifting to another app, long sessions), a daily goal and streak, AI recaps it writes itself (it surfaces Claude Code's away-summary), a 30-day history dashboard, a full-screen second-monitor scene and the DIY desk screen. Its 'pet' and pixel animations are minor, not an emoting character.

products.name: claude-code-buddy (TaoXieSZ)
products.scope_note: In scope. This is an open-source hobby fork of anthropics/claude-desktop-buddy. It adds macOS launchd daemons (cc-bridge, cursor-bridge, codex-bridge; OpenCode sessions are merged by cc-bridge) that feed agent state over BLE or USB serial to M5Stack devices. The PlatformIO envs cover an M5StickC Plus2 with an optional BugC2 walking chassis, an M5StickC Plus with RoverC, a StickS3, a CoreS3 StackChan, a Tab5 and a Cardputer-ADV (Agent Farm feed). The work also lives as the flagship sub-project of the maker's monorepo, TaoXieSZ/hardware-buddies (294 commits, 0 stars, last commit 2026-08-18, seen 2026-11-18). Some features, such as the Cardputer session switcher and AskUserQuestion answering, are implemented in cc-bridge here, but the matching Cardputer firmware sits in the sibling sub-project cardputer-adv-buddy. The discovery link anthropics/claude-code#45596 is a 'Bring Back Buddy' feature-request issue with about 288 timeline items. None of the 23 comments that load without login mention this project; the 265 hidden items were not checked in this pass. It is not a source for this project.
products.one_liner: DIY firmware plus Mac daemons that mirror Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode sessions onto M5Stack gadgets over BLE or USB. The gadgets are a StickC Plus2 that can ride a walking BugC2 chassis, a StackChan robot, a Tab5 and a Cardputer. You can approve permission prompts with a button, by keyboard, or with an experimental thumbs-up camera gesture.

agent_status.note: Persona states are sleep, idle, busy, attention, celebrate, dizzy and heart (docs/states.md). The StackChan shows SLEEP, IDLE, BUSY (with the tool name), ATTN and DONE (README). cc-bridge maps Claude Code hooks to these states (tools/cc-bridge/README.md).

multi_session.note: cc-bridge keeps per-session state with FIFO waiting (commit 300d571, 2026-06-25) and feeds a Cardputer session list. That list merges Claude, Cursor (bd319f3), OpenCode (fecb84e) and Codex (e87accf) sessions; Codex sessions are listed only when a live cmux pane exists (tools/codex-bridge/README.md). It also tracks total and running counts (bridge.py). Two daemons and two sticks can run side by side (README).

permission_alert.note: A PermissionRequest sets waiting=1 and the ATTN/attention state, showing 'approve: <tool>' (tools/cc-bridge/README.md; README). The StackChan plays hook-event voice clips. The device also shows a waiting state for Codex permission requests (tools/codex-bridge/README.md).

approve_from_device.note: README: with cc-bridge, button A on the stick approves a PreToolUse prompt and B denies it, synchronously. The StackChan has an experimental thumbs-up or thumbs-down camera gesture, wired end to end but dormant until WiFi and the [vision] extra are set up and not yet verified on hardware (docs/roadmap.md). Commits show Cardputer permission gating (fecb84e) and free-text and multi-question AskUserQuestion answers (6800c69, b852ddc). Cursor permission echo is still open (docs/roadmap.md), and Codex echo is not finished (tools/codex-bridge/README.md). The older tools/cc-bridge/README.md still says the stick cannot approve back into Claude Code, which contradicts the main README.

jump_to_session.note: On the Cardputer, selectSession focuses the matching cmux pane and raises cmux.app (commits 1aee6ac and ed1afac, 2026-06-23). Cursor panes were added in bd319f3 and OpenCode/Codex panes in 38fc2a8 (2026-07-06). It works only with the cmux terminal and the Cardputer (firmware in the sibling sub-project).

token_usage_cost.note: The StackChan OMC-HUD card shows model, context %, session, tokens and 5h/7d limits (README). statusline_hud.py forwards real token counts and context % from Claude Code's statusline. From hooks alone, token counts are approximate (tools/cc-bridge/README.md). No $ cost is shown.

plan_limits.note: The StackChan HUD shows 5h and 7d rate-limit %. statusline_hud.py reads rate_limits from Claude Code's statusline stdin and must be set as the statusLine.command (tools/cc-bridge/statusline_hud.py; docs/roadmap.md).

personal_baseline_levels.note: Levels use a fixed threshold: celebrate fires on a level-up every 50K tokens (docs/states.md). Nothing is relative to the user's own history.

test_build_red_green.note: Only generic tool failures are noticed. bridge.py handles PostToolUseFailure by setting 'failed: <tool>', logging the error and clearing any pending approval so the error animation shows (added in e1d8bb0, 2026-06-11; fix e16ef07, 2026-06-22). Nothing is specific to tests or builds, and no fail-then-pass transition is detected. https://github.com/TaoXieSZ/claude-code-buddy/blob/main/tools/cc-bridge/bridge.py

loop_stuck_detection.note: The only 'stale' logic found is a 10-minute session reaper that fixes counter drift (bridge.py; docs/roadmap.md). It does not detect the agent or user going in circles.

drift_away_detection.note: Only device-side auto-sleep after 15 to 30 s without button presses or session activity (docs/controls.md). No source shows detection of the user leaving while the agent waits.

ai_session_recap.note: The control plane (since split out into the agent-fleet project) shows Claude Code's own recap or activity verb in each session's status line, and adds a 'First Mate' LLM REPL backed by claude --print. Neither writes its own session recap (CHANGELOG.md).

history_dashboard.note: The localhost dashboard (127.0.0.1:18765) only has settings: volume, brightness, character pack and motion toggles (tools/cc-bridge/dashboard.py). The Cardputer Agent Farm feed scrolls recent trigger firings only. There is no cross-day history.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Inherited from upstream: a celebrate animation on a 'level up' every 50K tokens (docs/states.md), and pet energy that refills when the stick lies face-down for a nap (docs/controls.md). There are no streaks, daily goals or badges.

leaderboard.note: Local only. No accounts or team comparison appear in the README or dashboard.

character_personality.note: Animated character packs (clawd, calico, bufo, cloudling) react to each state (README). Also: BugC2 chassis motion and LEDs per state, a StackChan servo celebrate dance (docs/roadmap.md), and a Tab5 'living avatar' with idle-nap and pet-heart moods (commit b0614af, 2026-06-15).

sound_voice_out.note: The Plus2 buzzer chirps. The StackChan plays preloaded ElevenLabs voice clips on hook events (README). The Tab5 plays hook-event sound cues (commit 54b1f89, 2026-06-11). The StackChan also has an optional Agora ConvoAI voice-agent audio path (CHANGELOG.md).

voice_input.note: A push-to-talk gesture (tap, then hold A) relays a keystroke to a dictation app such as Typeless or Doubao (docs/controls.md). The StickS3 can act as a BLE push-to-talk dictation mic (README). An experimental voice control plane routes spoken commands to a cmux session after a thumbs-up (CHANGELOG.md).

physical_controls.note: Stick buttons A, B and power, plus shake (dizzy) and face-down (nap) (docs/controls.md). The StackChan has tap-to-wake and camera thumbs gestures (CHANGELOG.md; README). The Tab5 and Cardputer have keyboards (commits c6e8a4f and 6ac65ec; docs/cardputer-agentfarm.md). The BugC2 adds motors.

second_screen_mode.note: Dedicated M5 devices: a stick LCD, the CoreS3 StackChan LCD, the Cardputer 240x135 LCD and the Tab5. An Electron desktop-app preview exists but only runs on a mock event stream (README).

products.price_text: The software is free and open source (MIT). It is DIY: you buy the M5Stack hardware yourself (M5StickC Plus2 or Plus; optionally a BugC2 or RoverC, CoreS3 StackChan, Tab5, StickS3 or Cardputer-ADV) and flash it with PlatformIO. No kit is sold. Hardware prices were not checked. As of 2026-11-18.
products.license: MIT. The LICENSE text is MIT, copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC, inherited from upstream claude-desktop-buddy. unverified: GitHub's API license field (said to be NOASSERTION; the API was rate-limited on 2026-11-18).
products.privacy_note: At its core it runs locally: Claude Code hooks feed a Unix socket, then a launchd daemon, then BLE or USB to the device. The settings dashboard is on localhost. In the camera-gesture path, the StackChan streams JPEG frames over WiFi to the Mac, where MediaPipe runs, and only during permission prompts. The Cardputer Agent Farm feed polls a LAN HTTP API. The optional voice paths use cloud services: Agora ConvoAI voice agent and third-party dictation apps such as Doubao or Typeless.
products.distinctive: It is the broadest DIY M5Stack take on hardware buddies. One wire protocol drives a stick on a motorized BugC2 chassis that moves and lights up by state, a StackChan robot with servos, voice clips and camera thumbs-up/down approval, a Tab5 dashboard, and a Cardputer session switcher (bridge side here). It works across Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode. It adds approving from a button, answering AskUserQuestion on the device, push-to-talk dictation, and 5h/7d limit and context HUD data taken from the Claude Code statusline.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are macOS Claude Code companions with a character that reacts to working, waiting for permission and done states, and both use a small optional ESP32 desk screen. This project goes further on hardware and control. It is built around DIY M5Stack devices over BLE, with a walking chassis, servos, a camera and keyboards. It approves or denies from the device, answers questions, takes push-to-talk voice and supports Cursor, Codex and OpenCode. Its Cardputer can focus cmux panes. It lacks most of the reference's motivation layer: no intensity levels against the user's own baseline (a fixed level every 50K tokens instead), no test/build fail-then-pass moments (only generic tool-failure animations), no loop or drift detection, no daily goal or streak, no AI recaps of its own and no 30-day history dashboard. It has no on-desktop robot either; the Electron app only runs on mock data. Setup is heavy for developers (PlatformIO flashing, BLE pairing, launchd), while the reference is a free app.
products.hardware: Targets M5StickC Plus2: ESP32, 1.14in LCD, IMU, buzzer, buttons A and B, battery. Optional M5 BugC2 chassis: 4 DC motors and 2 RGB LEDs. An M5StickC Plus with RoverC also has envs (m5stickc-plus-claude-rover, m5stickc-plus-cursor-rover). M5Stack CoreS3 StackChan: ESP32-S3, 2.0in LCD, GC0308 camera, servos, 12 RGB LEDs, speaker. Also StickS3 (BLE PTT mic, plus -claude and -cursor envs), M5 Tab5 (ESP32-P4, 1280x720) and Cardputer-ADV (keyboard, 240x135 LCD, 2.4 GHz WiFi). Links are BLE to the Mac, USB serial for the Tab5, and WiFi for the StackChan camera and audio and the Cardputer Agent Farm feed. Nothing is sold; you supply the hardware.

products.name: ClaudeAssistant (FreakStudio) / 码克助手, a.k.a. Claude Buddy
products.scope_note: In scope. Finished desk hardware for Claude Code status, sold on Tindie and, per claude.freakstudio.cn, through the maker's Taobao shop. The same project appears as "ClaudeAssistant", "码克助手" and "Claude Buddy": the hook plugin is claude-buddy-plugin and the hook port variable is CLAUDE_BUDDY_PORT. It is a separate product from Anthropic's claude-desktop-buddy reference firmware. This one uses Claude Code hooks, installed as a plugin (README points to github.com/ChrisWu132/claude-buddy-plugin; a FreakStudioCN/claude-buddy-plugin repo also exists), plus a local Python daemon. It does not use the Claude desktop BLE API.
products.one_liner: ESP32/RP2040 desk pet sold in four builds: D-Shell touch panel with LED strip, Panel touch-screen dev board, Clock LED robot, and WizFi360 WiFi LED light. It shows the live state of Claude Code through hooks, using LED colors, pixel-character animation and TTS voice, and tracks several sessions at once.

agent_status.note: Five states: Idle (blue glow), Working (cyan sweep), Pending approval (yellow slow blink), Completed (green flash, 2 s), Error (red alternating). Working also sends the running tool, e.g. 'Read: README.md', in the m field (docs/state_machine.md, README_EN).

multi_session.note: 'The device tracks all sessions and surfaces the most important one', resolved by priority: error > pending > running > completed > idle. MAX_SESSIONS=5 in device/config.py. Sessions are named by cwd basename (12 chars). D-Shell and Panel show a multi-session history list (Tindie, README_EN, state_machine.md).

permission_alert.note: Notification(permission_prompt) and Notification(elicitation_dialog) set Pending: yellow slow blink, and the voice says 'Please check your terminal' (state_machine.md, README_EN, Tindie).

approve_from_device.note: hook_bridge.py header: 'v5 纯展示版: 设备仅展示状态，不参与审批; 审批由 Claude Code 自己在终端 UI 完成; hook_bridge 始终返回 {}'. The plugin repo also says the device is display-only and approvals stay in the terminal.

jump_to_session.note: Hooks push one way to the daemon and device. hook_bridge.py has no window-focus code and none is documented.

token_usage_cost.note: The wire format to the device is only n (name), s (state), m (tool message) and slot (state_machine.md). hook_bridge.py reads no token or cost data.

plan_limits.note: No quota or limit tracking. The wire format carries state only (state_machine.md).

personal_baseline_levels.note: A fixed hook-driven state machine (I/W/P/C/E) with no intensity levels (state_machine.md).

test_build_red_green.note: Any PostToolUseFailure or StopFailure sets a 3 s 'dizzy' Error state (highest priority) with an error voice line. This is generic tool failure: nothing specific to tests or builds, and no fail-then-pass detection (state_machine.md).

loop_stuck_detection.note: The documented state machine has no loop or stuck detection (state_machine.md).

drift_away_detection.note: Notification(idle_prompt) is only logged and does not change state. There is no user-away logic (state_machine.md).

ai_session_recap.note: No summaries. The device shows states and tool names only.

history_dashboard.note: Only a short on-device list of recent sessions (HISTORY_MAX_LEN=20) on D-Shell and Panel. No analytics across days or weeks.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: None in README, state machine or config. It is a status indicator only.

leaderboard.note: No accounts or cloud. It runs locally over BLE or LAN (Tindie privacy claims).

character_personality.note: D-Shell and Panel animate 8 preset pixel characters (claude, cat, robot, ghost, among_us, creeper, kirby, pikachu; config default 'robot'), and custom ones can be made with the /create-character skill (README_EN, device/config.py). The official page shows the desk pet as an orange robot in sunglasses (claude.freakstudio.cn). The error state is called 'dizzy'.

sound_voice_out.note: MAX98357A speaker on every build. Each state change has a voice announcement from Doubao TTS, with 200+ voices and adjustable speed and pitch. The repo ships 20 pre-generated .pcm clips in device/assets (connect, done, error, idle, pending, startup, working). Random lines play every 20-60 s while working or idle (device/config.py, README_EN).

voice_input.note: The hardware lists only a speaker amplifier (MAX98357A) and no microphone, so voice is output only.

physical_controls.note: Touch screens: Panel has CST816S and D-Shell has GT911. D-Shell also has two keys (DSHELL_KEY_UP=9, DSHELL_KEY_DOWN=3 in config.py). Clock and WizFi360 have a vibration sensor ('拍击检测 → 触发语音', tap detection triggers voice) and a vibration motor for status feedback. What touch and the keys do is not documented (device/config.py, README_EN).

second_screen_mode.note: A dedicated device. D-Shell and Panel have a 2.4in ST7789 TFT (320x240). Clock and WizFi360 are LED and voice only, with no screen.

products.price_text: Tindie: US$70.00 as of 2026-11-18. One price covers the listing, which describes four forms (D-Shell Panel, Panel, Clock, WizFi360). The page shows no per-variant prices, no stock count and no shipping rates. The maker also sells through its Taobao shop (Freak嵌入式, linked from claude.freakstudio.cn), price not checked. The hook plugin, daemon, compiled firmware and setup tool are free on GitHub for DIY builds. Custom voices need your own Volcengine Doubao TTS App ID and token.
products.license: None. The main repo has no LICENSE file and no license in the GitHub sidebar (seen 2026-11-18). The companion FreakStudioCN/claude-buddy-plugin repo says: 'No open-source license is attached; all rights reserved by FreakStudio.' Most device firmware is published only as compiled .mpy files, and the README offers full source and developer docs through a WeChat contact.
products.privacy_note: At runtime, Claude Code hooks send events to a local daemon on 127.0.0.1:57320, which pushes state to the device over BLE or LAN WiFi. Hooks fail open if the daemon is down. The maker says the device 'doesn't store your code, doesn't upload anything' and has 'no subscription, no cloud dependency' (Tindie). Generating custom voice clips calls the Volcengine Doubao TTS cloud API with the user's own credentials, at setup time.
products.hardware: Four builds share one MicroPython firmware. (1) D-Shell Panel, the 'official hardware': ESP32-S3, 2.4in ST7789 TFT, GT911 touch, LVGL animation, WS2812x8 LED strip, MAX98357A speaker, two keys (up/down). (2) Panel: Waveshare ESP32-S3 dev board, 2.4in ST7789 TFT (320x240), CST816S touch, MAX98357A speaker, no LED strip. (3) Clock: ESP32-C3, 2x WS2812B LEDs, MAX98357A speaker, vibration (tap) sensor and vibration motor, small box/orange-robot enclosure, USB-powered (README mentions 'USB or battery' in passing, with no battery spec). (4) WizFi360: RP2040 + WizFi360 WiFi, 2x WS2812B LEDs, speaker, vibration sensor and motor, WiFi TCP only. The ESP32 builds connect over BLE (or WiFi).
products.distinctive: One of the few finished, purchasable Claude Code status devices, from a Chinese embedded studio (Taiyuan). One $70 Tindie listing covers four builds, from a touch-screen panel with 8 pixel characters and an LED strip to a tiny LED robot clock with tap sensing. Spoken TTS announcements for every state (200+ Doubao voices) and aggregation of up to 5 sessions set it apart. The PC side is documented for Windows 10/11 only, and the device is deliberately display-only: no approvals and no usage data.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlap: Claude Code only and hook-driven, with a character that reacts to working, waiting for permission, stop/complete and errors, and an ESP32 desk screen. Differences: it is sold as finished hardware on Tindie and Taobao, while the reference is a free macOS app with an optional DIY board. Its PC side is documented for Windows 10/11 only, with no on-desktop pet or second-monitor scene. It adds TTS voice, LED strips, touch screens and keys, tap sensing and aggregation of up to 5 sessions. It has none of the reference's own-baseline intensity levels, token tracking, loop or drift detection, test fail-then-pass detection, daily goal or streak, AI recaps, 30-day dashboard or 'Go to it' window focus. Neither approves from the device.

products.scope_note: In scope. Do not confuse it with other projects called "AgentDeck": puritysb/AgentDeck (Stream Deck+, D200H, iOS/Android, ESP32, with an App Store app and its forks), andremarquezz/AgentDeck, JasonBates/agentdeck (a Herdr web dashboard) and eMeRiKa13/agent-deck. Those are different products by other makers. This one is the macOS Python program by GitHub user jakeparkcolde ("Coldbyte") for the plain 13-key Ulanzi D200.
products.one_liner: Open-source macOS program that drives an off-the-shelf Ulanzi D200 13-key LCD deck directly over USB HID, with no vendor app and stock firmware. It shows Claude Code and Codex agent status per project (Decide, Done, Working and Idle tiles that blink and jump to the window), plus 5-hour and weekly LLM quota with burn pace and reset times, alongside Mac health, git worktrees, a pomodoro, games and screensavers.
agents_supported: Antigravity CLI (agy): quota over SSH, and counted as 'A' on the agents page

agent_status.note: Page 3 groups agents by project into tiles labeled Decide N (yellow blink: waiting for a permission or an answer), Done N (green blink), Working N (blue border) or Idle, with C/X/A counts for Claude, Codex and agy. State comes from hooks: for Claude Code, SessionStart sets idle, UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse set working, PermissionRequest sets blocked (Decide) and Stop sets done. Codex reports through its notify setting (agent-turn-complete sets Done). Sources: docs/GUIDE.en.md; https://github.com/jakeparkcolde/agentdeck/blob/main/hooks/agent_hook.py

multi_session.note: Groups many Claude Code and Codex sessions by project, with a count of how many are running. Pressing the same tile again moves to the next session or tab in that project. It can read hook state from other Macs over SSH (hooks.hosts). Herdr mode shows lead panes with their sub-agents and can zoom a pane. Sources: GUIDE.en.md; hook_agents.py.

permission_alert.note: A PermissionRequest hook (or a Notification that mentions permission) turns the project tile into a yellow blinking 'Decide N'. Agent alerts also pull the deck out of the screensaver. The README pitch is 'who's waiting for my approval?'. Sources: hooks/agent_hook.py, GUIDE.en.md, README.en.md.

approve_from_device.note: Pressing an alert tile only jumps to the agent's window and stops the blinking. hook_agents.py only selects tabs and windows with AppleScript or open; it sends no keystrokes or answers to the agent. The closest feature: on the worktrees view, press twice to send a canned 'tidy up' request to a lead agent (needs Herdr).

jump_to_session.note: One press jumps to the exact tab in iTerm2 or Terminal (matched by tty with AppleScript). It opens the project window in VS Code or Cursor (open -b with the cwd) and brings the app forward for Ghostty and others. Sessions on another Mac are display-only. Sources: GUIDE.en.md; https://github.com/jakeparkcolde/agentdeck/blob/main/hook_agents.py

token_usage_cost.note: Usage appears on the deck only as quota percentage used or left (plus Flow and Higgsfield credit counts). usage.py computes today, week and 5-hour block token totals from local Claude and Codex logs, but pages.py renders no token counts, and there is no dollar cost anywhere. Sources: https://github.com/jakeparkcolde/agentdeck/blob/main/usage.py, https://github.com/jakeparkcolde/agentdeck/blob/main/pages.py

plan_limits.note: Pages 1-2 show 5-hour and weekly quota left for Claude (through a status-line wrapper), Codex (an undocumented chatgpt.com backend endpoint) and agy (official CLI over SSH). They also show burn pace (too fast or on track against time elapsed), a 'Best now' LLM pick, a 'next reset' tile and per-window reset countdowns (pages.py). Tiles warn when you are spending too fast or will leave quota unused (commits of 2026-11-13). Flow and Higgsfield credits are optional.

personal_baseline_levels.note: Pace compares quota used with time elapsed in the window. It is a fixed formula, not the user's own history (GUIDE.en.md).

test_build_red_green.note: The agent page states are only Decide, Done, Working and Idle (plus an error state on StopFailure). PostToolUseFailure only maps to 'working'. pages.py has nothing about tests or builds.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Not in the feature guide or in pages.py. The only state labels are Decide, Done, Working and Idle.

drift_away_detection.note: Not in the feature guide. The 10-minute idle screensaver is about the deck sitting idle, not about the user leaving while an agent waits.

ai_session_recap.note: No session summaries. Presentation mode can record lectures into the maker's separate agentnote tool, which is unrelated to agent sessions.

history_dashboard.note: Only current quota and status are rendered. pages.py shows no history across days or weeks.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: The arcade and tycoon games save scores and coins, but nothing is tied to coding activity. A pomodoro timer exists, with no streaks or goals.

leaderboard.note: No comparison with other users. Game scores are saved locally only.

character_personality.note: The aquarium, fireplace, rain and beach screensavers have animated creatures, but they are scenery and do not react to agents.

sound_voice_out.note: Optional synthesized sound effects play on the Mac speaker for games, the intro and screensaver ambience. They are off by default, and the D200 has no speaker. sfx.py has no sound for agent alerts and no text-to-speech. The pomodoro end sends a macOS notification with sound. Sources: GUIDE.en.md, https://github.com/jakeparkcolde/agentdeck/blob/main/sfx.py

voice_input.note: The microphone is used only to record lectures in presentation mode, not to prompt agents.

physical_controls.note: 13 LCD keys on the Ulanzi D200 plus a wide tile. Tap and hold (0.8 s or more) do different things: page arrows, home or brightness cycle, jump to an agent. Destructive device cleanups need a double hold. Worktree actions arm on the first press and run on a second press within 10 s. Holding the wide tile for 2 s downloads an update. Source: GUIDE.en.md.

second_screen_mode.note: The D200 is a separate desk device with its own LCD keys. Its pages show quota, agents, machines and so on.

products.price_text: The software is free and open source (MIT) as of 2026-11-18. It needs an Ulanzi Stream Controller D200 bought separately. The README links the Ulanzi store (ulanzi.com/products/stream-deck-d200), Ulanzi's official AliExpress store (an affiliate link that pays the maker a commission) and AliExpress search, and gives no price. unverified: $59.99 on Ulanzi's US store and €63.95 on the EU store (a previous researcher's search snippets; Ulanzi pages returned HTTP 429 on 2026-11-18). The README says the D200X and D200H are untested. unverified: their prices ($99.99 and $69.99).
products.license: MIT. A NOTICE file credits the upstream redphx/strmdck (MIT) for the D200 wire protocol and the protocol notes in jcalado/companion-surface-d200.
products.privacy_note: Runs as a Python process on the Mac with no account or maker server. Agent state comes from local hook files in ~/.cache/d200/agents and, optionally, over SSH from the user's other Macs. Quota lookups go straight to each provider with the user's own credentials: the Claude status-line JSON, the token from Codex's auth.json sent to chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage (an undocumented endpoint), and the agy CLI over SSH. Optional extras: the Korean stock pages call Naver's unofficial m.stock.naver.com API (on in the example config). Google Flow and Higgsfield credits and AliExpress order and parcel import use a dedicated local headless Chrome profile (~/.cache/d200/ali-browser, bound to 127.0.0.1) that the user logs into by hand.
products.hardware: A third-party Ulanzi Stream Controller D200 with stock firmware. d200.py defines 13 buttons in a 5+5+3 layout with 196×196 icons, and a wide 458×196 tile that fills the last two slots of the bottom row. It talks over USB HID (VID 0x2207, PID 0x0019). The device has no speaker. agentdeck sends a ZIP of the PNG icons with content-hashed names so the device redraws only the icons that changed. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac and Python 3.11+. The maker sells no hardware. unverified: USB-C connector.
products.maker: Coldbyte (GitHub: jakeparkcolde), a solo developer. Most commits are co-authored with Claude.
products.maker_location: Likely South Korea, though not stated. This is inferred from the Korean-first README, the Korean stock heatmap page, Korean commit messages and code comments, and a profile on the Korean builder community jocoHunt.

The README is available in Korean, English, Japanese and Chinese and has a 40-second intro video. unverified: no press, Reddit, HN or X coverage (not re-searched).

products.distinctive: It turns a cheap, off-the-shelf 13-key LCD macro pad into an agent console without flashing firmware. Blinking yellow and green tiles grouped by project jump to the exact iTerm or Terminal tab or the VS Code/Cursor window, and it follows sessions across several Macs over SSH. It pairs this with a multi-provider quota page (Claude, Codex, Antigravity) that shows burn pace, reset times and the best LLM to use now, plus git worktree cleanup that can delegate to a lead agent through Herdr. It is also a kitchen-sink desk deck: Mac health with Mole, a pomodoro, presentation remote, Korean stock heatmap, AliExpress parcel tracking, arcade and board games, and pixel-art screensavers.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are free, local-first and macOS-only. Both show Claude Code's live state, flag when Claude is waiting for permission, and offer a one-press jump to the waiting terminal instead of approving remotely. Neither has voice input. agentdeck differs in four ways. It needs a purchased Ulanzi D200 instead of an on-screen robot or a DIY ESP32 screen. It also covers Codex, and quota for agy, Flow and Higgsfield. It handles many sessions per project and across several Macs. And it centers on plan limits (5-hour and weekly remaining, pace, reset). It lacks everything that makes the reference distinctive: intensity levels against the user's own baseline, detection of test failing then passing, loops and drift, an emoting character, AI session recaps, daily goals and streaks, and a 30-day history dashboard. Its extras are general desk-deck features with no link to coding activity: games, a pomodoro, stocks, parcels and Mac health.

products.name: V14 (MicStick V14) – The AI Workflow Console That Keeps You in the Flow
products.scope_note: In scope: a Kickstarter handheld remote billed as "Voice & Physical Control for Claude, Codex, and Other AI Coding Agents". FUNDING OUTCOME (re-checked 2026-11-18): it SUCCEEDED, but only just. Kicktraq says 'Funding Successful' and PledgeBox says 'Successful', at $2,018 of a $2,000 goal from 13 backers. It was not cancelled and did not fail, and with 13 backers it is not a breakout, so the 'one breakout' funding analysis should count it as funded but tiny. The following were not reachable on 2026-11-18: the Kickstarter campaign and rewards pages (403), the BackerKit tracker (403), and Kickstarter stats.json and Wayback Machine captures (both blocked by the tooling). The web search budget was also used up, so the tier prices and estimated delivery date still could not be found. Gadgetify says it is aimed at people who use AI agents for 'coding, video editing, other tasks'. The URL slug still reads 'the-ai-coding-remote' while the title is now 'AI Workflow Console', so the campaign was renamed. This is not the same product as VibeKeys, AgentDeck or the Ulanzi AU05 Vibe Key, which Gadgetify links separately.
products.one_liner: A small Kickstarter handheld remote with a color screen and Bluetooth. You hold a button and speak an instruction to a selected Claude or Codex session, see the session's status, confirm or cancel actions, and switch sessions, all without going to the terminal.
agents_supported: Claude (Claude Code implied by 'AI coding remote')

agent_status.note: Gadgetify: the built-in display shows 'session status' so you can keep up with what your agents are doing (https://www.gadgetify.com/micstick-v14/). The campaign subtitle advertises a 'Color Display' (PledgeBox/Kicktraq).

multi_session.note: Gadgetify: it is meant for multiple AI agents and has 'buttons to confirm, cancel, and switch sessions' (https://www.gadgetify.com/micstick-v14/). The phrase 'handheld session console for multi-agent coding' comes only from an earlier Kickstarter FAQ snippet and was not re-checked (403).

physical_controls.note: Gadgetify: push-to-talk top button; buttons to confirm, cancel and switch sessions; hot-swappable buttons; keys can be set for common actions such as music control (https://www.gadgetify.com/micstick-v14/).

products.distinctive: A voice-first handheld remote rather than a desk display. You hold the top button, speak a full instruction to the selected Claude or Codex session, then confirm or cancel on physical, hot-swappable keys while a small color screen shows session status. It advertises local Paraformer speech recognition and Bluetooth. It is a very small campaign that only just funded (13 backers, $2,018 of $2,000).
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlap: both show AI coding agent (Claude) status away from the terminal on a dedicated screen. Differences: V14 is paid hardware built for control, not ambient motivation. It has voice prompts, on-device confirm/cancel and session switching, supports Codex as well as Claude, and targets macOS and Windows. The reference app never approves from the robot and has no voice or physical controls (apart from a knock on one DIY board). No source shows V14 having the reference's strengths: intensity levels based on the user's own baseline, reactions to test or build failures, loop or drift detection, daily goals or streaks, AI recaps, a history dashboard or a character.

products.name: Token Monitor (Fractal Manifold)
products.scope_note: In scope: a complete, campaign-ready hardware desk display for AI coding usage, with signed firmware at v1.0.1 or later. It was never funded or mass-produced. Kicktraq shows the Kickstarter (Aug 6 to Sep 5, 2026) as 'Unsuccessful'. On 2026-11-18 tokenmonitor.dev still said 'Live on Kickstarter', and fractalmanifold.com still listed the product (calling the third provider 'Gemini') with no store or pre-order link. I found no relaunch, pre-order or store. Do not confuse it with Javis603/token-monitor (a software widget) or RoryLi98/TokenMonitor (a Windows taskbar app), which are unrelated products with the same name. The same maker also publishes token-monitor-hud, a Claude Code band plugin that needs no hardware (v1.0.0, 2026-10-23).
products.one_liner: 4-inch ESP32-S3 Wi-Fi touchscreen desk display showing live quota %, token counts and estimated spend for Claude Code, Codex CLI and Antigravity CLI. A local open-source (MIT) broker on the laptop feeds it. Its Kickstarter failed in Sep 2026.

agent_status.note: On-screen data is quota % bars, token totals, estimated spend, plus clock, weather and sunrise/sunset. The broker parses only token-count fields from CLI transcripts, so it has no agent working/waiting state (https://tokenmonitor.dev/how-it-works.html).

multi_session.note: Totals are per provider, not per session. Auto-rotate cycles between the Claude, Codex and Antigravity provider screens (autorotate_enabled in the settings SKILL.md), but there is no session overview. Each broker reads only the machine it runs on, with no combined total across machines (https://tokenmonitor.dev/faq.html).

permission_alert.note: The official site lists the only alerts as low battery, limit overshoot and session rollover. None of them is a permission or input alert.

approve_from_device.note: Display-only. The device polls the broker for dashboard data and never contacts AI providers (https://tokenmonitor.dev/how-it-works.html).

jump_to_session.note: No source mentions it. The device is a separate Wi-Fi unit that talks only to a LAN broker, which tracks no sessions.

token_usage_cost.note: Token totals come from local CLI logs. Spend is estimated as tokens × the public LiteLLM list-price table, so on Pro/Max plans it is a notional figure, not a bill (https://tokenmonitor.dev/how-it-works.html).

plan_limits.note: Percentage bars of each provider's reported quota, fetched from its usage API about every 90 s (https://tokenmonitor.dev/how-it-works.html). CNX lists 'session limits' and 'reset timers' (https://www.cnx-software.com/2026/08/07/token-monitor-an-esp32-s3-desktop-display-that-tracks-ai-coding-assistant-usage/), but does not name 5-hour or weekly windows. The device alerts on limit overshoot and session rollover. Only the companion token-monitor-hud band explicitly shows Claude 5-hour and 7-day bars, with reset time, pace at reset, burn rate and 80%/95% toasts (https://github.com/fractal-manifold/mcp-marketplace/tree/main/plugins/token-monitor-hud).

personal_baseline_levels.note: On-screen data is fixed quota %, token totals and spend (how-it-works.html). The HUD measures pace against linear spend within the window, not against the user's own history.

test_build_red_green.note: The broker parses only token-count fields from CLI transcripts (https://tokenmonitor.dev/how-it-works.html).

loop_stuck_detection.note: No source mentions it. The broker collects only token counts and provider quota.

drift_away_detection.note: No source mentions it. The broker collects only token counts and provider quota, with no app-focus or presence data.

ai_session_recap.note: No source mentions it. The broker reads only token-count fields.

history_dashboard.note: No built-in multi-day history. The on-screen data listed in how-it-works.html is live totals only. A user-written script can feed its own time series into the optional custom panel (line, bar, pie, table or text, up to 4 tiles) (https://tokenmonitor.dev/setup.html), but that is DIY.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: No source mentions it. The on-screen data is limited to quota, tokens and spend.

leaderboard.note: No source mentions it, and there is no vendor account or cloud to compare users through (https://tokenmonitor.dev/faq.html).

character_personality.note: An on-device pet exists: the settings skill exposes pet_enabled, pet_species (an animal enum) and pet_name, which are 'device-owned' and apply live (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fractal-manifold/mcp-marketplace/main/plugins/tokenmonitor/skills/settings/SKILL.md). The official plugin page lists 'pet' among the settings areas (https://tokenmonitor.dev/plugin.html). No source describes the pet's behaviour, emotes or link to usage.

sound_voice_out.note: Built-in speaker for alerts, with an adjustable alert volume that defaults to 80% (https://tokenmonitor.dev/faq.html). The alerts cover only low battery, limit overshoot and session rollover. No source mentions voice.

voice_input.note: No source mentions a microphone, voice or dictation feature, and CNX's hardware list has no mic. The device only receives dashboard data.

physical_controls.note: 4-inch 5-point capacitive touchscreen: swipe up for the custom panel, tap to lock the theme, on-screen Wi-Fi picker and keyboard, and a Settings menu. PWR and BOOT side buttons handle wake, restart, power-off, pairing mode and factory reset. The controls cover navigation and settings only and never send input to the agent (https://tokenmonitor.dev/setup.html, https://tokenmonitor.dev/faq.html).

second_screen_mode.note: A dedicated always-on 4-inch 480×480 desk display (86×86 mm). It goes to standby after 20 minutes without changes.

products.price_text: Kickstarter rewards per CNX (2026-08-07): Super Early Bird €99 (≈$115, first 50 backers, white device, excluding shipping and tax) and Standard Early Bird €120. Retail price was never stated. The campaign ended Unsuccessful on Sep 5, 2026 (Kicktraq). As of 2026-11-18 tokenmonitor.dev still advertises the €99 Super Early Bird and 'Live on Kickstarter', but I found no working way to buy: no store or pre-order on tokenmonitor.dev or fractalmanifold.com. price_usd is that advertised €99 ≈ $115, used as a reference rather than a price anyone can pay today. The broker and plugins are free (MIT).
products.ship_date: CNX (2026-08-07) said first shipments were expected in November 2026. The campaign failed on 2026-09-05, so no units ship through Kickstarter. As of 2026-11-18 I found no other sales channel.
products.launch_date: 2026-08-06 (Kickstarter launch)
products.last_activity: Latest repo commit on 2026-10-23: token-monitor-hud 1.0.0. The broker and plugin reached 1.0.3 on 2026-10-03, and plugin 1.0.2 (mDNS broker discovery) shipped on 2026-09-22, so software work continued after the failed campaign (github.com/fractal-manifold/mcp-marketplace/commits/main). The Kickstarter ended 2026-09-05, 'Unsuccessful' (Kicktraq). tokenmonitor.dev was still online on 2026-11-18, still showing the outdated 'Live on Kickstarter' text.
products.license: The broker (tokenmonitor-mcp), MCP plugin and docs are MIT according to the official FAQ, and the GitHub repo is MIT. CNX reported Apache-2.0 instead. The device firmware is proprietary, with Ed25519-signed OTA updates and automatic rollback.
products.privacy_note: No vendor account, telemetry, analytics or crash reporting. The broker runs on the user's machine and listens only on the LAN (port 8765), with HMAC-SHA256-signed, replay-protected polls and AES-256-CTR for sensitive control payloads. It uses the user's existing CLI login to call each provider's usage API, and also fetches the public LiteLLM price list and GitHub firmware info. It is not built to read or send prompts or code. The device talks only to the broker, pool.ntp.org and Open-Meteo.

spot_check.note:
I checked every figure against today's Kicktraq pages and PledgeBox mirrors, and they all match: CtrlVibe HK$80,514 from 59 backers; AgentDeck CA$597 of CA$71,000 from 3 backers; Token Monitor EUR 1,153 of EUR 28,000 from 10 backers.

Context and caveats:

1. **CtrlVibe was funded.** It reached 805% of its HK$10,000 goal, so "raised little" is true only in absolute terms.
2. **The US$ figure is not on any page I could read.** Kicktraq shows HKD only, and the Kickstarter stats endpoint was blocked. HK$80,514 at about 7.85 HKD/USD comes to about US$10,260, so "about US$10,261" is consistent.
3. **Years are inferred.** Kicktraq and PledgeBox give no year. 2026 comes from CNX articles dated August 5 and 7, 2026, and from AgentDeck showing 12 days left on 2026-11-18.
4. **AgentDeck's length differs by source.** Kicktraq says 61 days and PledgeBox says 60. Both end on December 1.
5. **Token Monitor's creator and goal differ by source.** Kicktraq names the creator only as "Jorge" (Madrid, Spain), while CNX names the company as Fractal Manifold. CNX gave the goal at launch as EUR 25,000, but Kicktraq and PledgeBox show EUR 28,000. The campaign ended on 2026-09-05.

products.name: c9watch
products.scope_note: In scope. It is a multi-agent session monitor with a menu-bar app, a dashboard and a JSON CLI that agents can use to watch each other. It makes the work of AI coding agents visible outside the terminal and handles several sessions at once.
products.one_liner: Free, open-source (MIT) Tauri app for the macOS menu bar and desktop, plus a JSON CLI for macOS and Linux. It finds every running Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent and Pi session by scanning processes, shows which are working, which need attention and which are idle, and adds cost tracking, quota meters, history search and a LAN web/phone view.

agent_status.note: Real-time Working / Needs Attention / Idle status per session. It polls processes every 2 s (dev.to write-up) and parses the session JSONL. An optional Claude Code hook bridge reports permission prompts directly. The menu-bar tray popover gives an overview of all sessions, and a pixel grid status bar animates on state changes (v0.3.0). https://c9watch.mclee.dev/changelog/

multi_session.note: Monitor tab groups all sessions by status or by project (with git branch info). Attention inbox, provider filter, subagent visibility. The maker built it for running Claude Code across 10+ terminal tabs (Show HN text via hnshowcase.com).

permission_alert.note: Needs Attention state for permission requests and user questions, sorted to the top. Native macOS notifications with settings for events, content, sound and per-session cooldown (v0.10.0). Codex sandbox-escape approvals are heuristic and show after 35 s. Cursor Agent has no needs-you state. https://c9watch.mclee.dev/compatibility/

approve_from_device.note: Session controls are Stop, Open terminal/IDE and Rename (plus a copyable RESUME command chip in History). The v0.1.0 notes said 'approve permissions', but v0.2.0 'removed custom permission banner, macOS handles prompts natively', and no current doc lists approval. The hooks doc says the hooks 'can't affect permission decisions', and v0.10.0 says 'c9watch does not approve prompts' for Cursor. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/minchenlee/c9watch/main/docs/claude-hooks.md

jump_to_session.note: 'Open the parent terminal or IDE'. Since v0.9.0 it focuses the matching Terminal.app/iTerm2 target by tty. Since v0.5.0 it restores minimized windows. Since v0.6.0 it focuses an existing JetBrains window. The site lists VS Code, Cursor, Zed, iTerm2, Ghostty, Terminal.app, Alacritty, kitty, WezTerm, Warp, Hyper, tmux, Antigravity and 13 JetBrains IDEs. Not available for Cursor Agent or Pi sessions. https://c9watch.mclee.dev/changelog/ and https://c9watch.mclee.dev/

token_usage_cost.note: Cost tab with daily, per-project and per-model spend computed from token metadata (Claude Code, plus Codex estimates and Pi), with a USD/TOKENS toggle. Per-session cost in the CLI. 'Token distance' rice-stack visualizer of total tokens.

plan_limits.note: v0.10.0 quota meters for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in the toolbar and tray, with reset times and an elapsed-time marker for each window. Claude Code needs an optional status-line bridge. https://github.com/minchenlee/c9watch/releases/tag/v0.10.0

personal_baseline_levels.note: No levels or baselines in the feature list.

test_build_red_green.note: 'While you were away' counts commands run and files edited but does not read test or build results.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Health badges (fresh/stale/partial/unavailable/unknown) show whether the data is current, not whether an agent is stuck or looping. The changelog handles killed or dead sessions, not loops.

drift_away_detection.note: 'While you were away' (v0.11.0) shows what a waiting session did since you last opened it, pressed FOCUS or left the c9watch window. That is a catch-up summary only. Nothing detects or nudges you when you have drifted to another app while an agent waits.

ai_session_recap.note: The away summary is 'counted from the transcript on your machine, no AI summary'.

history_dashboard.note: History tab with metadata filters and deep content search across past sessions. Daily cost bar chart with per-project and per-model breakdowns.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Not in the feature list.

leaderboard.note: No comparison with other users. Token-distance PNG export is for sharing only.

character_personality.note: Utilitarian dashboard UI with a pixel grid status bar. No mascot or character.

sound_voice_out.note: Only the sound on native macOS notifications, which can be set in notification settings (v0.10.0). No speech. https://github.com/minchenlee/c9watch/releases/tag/v0.10.0

voice_input.note: Not in the feature list.

physical_controls.note: Software only.

second_screen_mode.note: Web dashboard served on port 9210 that a phone, tablet or other browser can open after QR or code pairing (LAN access is opt-in). It is a remote view, not a dedicated display device or a full-screen second-monitor mode. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/minchenlee/c9watch/main/docs/mobile-migration-c0h.md

products.price_text: Free and open source (MIT) as of 2026-11-18. Install via Homebrew cask, an install script, a DMG from GitHub Releases, a CLI-only tarball (macOS/Linux) or a build from source. No paid tier.
products.license: MIT
products.privacy_note: Reads local agent files such as ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions, plus the process list. The maker's write-up says 'no telemetry'. The WebSocket server on port 9210 binds to loopback by default. LAN access for phones is opt-in, uses plain unencrypted ws://, and sends conversation content or allows opening terminals only if those options are switched on separately. Paired-device tokens are kept in memory only. No cloud account.
products.distinctive: It finds sessions by scanning OS processes, so it works with any terminal or IDE without plugins or launching from the app, and it covers several agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, Pi, OpenCode preview). The same binary is a JSON CLI (list/watch/wait/stop/cost) and ships a Claude Code skill, so agents can monitor and coordinate with sibling sessions. A test-backed status accuracy matrix and quota meters for three providers make it unusually thorough for a free tool. The README says it is built mostly with Claude Code and Codex.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlaps on live Claude Code status, permission-waiting alerts, bringing the waiting terminal forward (c9watch's Open, like the reference's 'Go to it') and history across days. Neither approves from the app. c9watch is a utilitarian multi-agent, multi-session dashboard. It adds cost and quota tracking, history and content search, a conversation viewer, a JSON CLI for agents and a LAN phone/web view. It has none of the reference's character, personal-baseline intensity levels, test red/green moments, loop or drift detection, daily goal and streak, AI recaps, second-monitor scene or DIY desk screen.

products.name: Ulanzi AU05 Vibe Key
products.one_liner: Wireless aluminium push-to-talk keypad for AI work. It has a voice key with a mic tuned for quiet speech, remappable keys (confirm and reject, for example) and a knob whose light shows AI agent status (Claude Code or Codex) through hooks.

agent_status.note: GREEN FUNDING: 'AIツールからの通知（Hooks機能）に対応しており、作業の進捗状況をひと目で把握できます', which says hooks notifications from AI tools show work progress at a glance. The Gadget Hunting review (https://gadgethuntingwithrr.com/reviews/ulanzi-vibe-key-review/), on a Mac with Claude Code, says the knob light 'connected to agent status' and told the reviewer it was working. Claypier names Codex and Claude Code hooks (https://claypier.com/en/ulanzi-au05-vibe-key-crowdfunding/). It is a single light, and no per-state colours are published. The third-party client https://github.com/makoshan/vibekey (commits Aug 27 to Sep 22, 2026) says official Ulanzi Studio did not cover the AU05 agent scenario, so official support is probably recent.

multi_session.note: Turning the knob 'scrolls or switches between sessions' (https://claypier.com/en/ulanzi-au05-vibe-key-crowdfunding/). GREEN FUNDING says the dial switches chats or tasks (チャットやタスクを切り替える) (https://greenfunding.jp/lab/projects/9495). These are keystroke mappings. There is no overview of several sessions, and the light shows one status.

permission_alert.note: Claypier: 'when paired with Codex or Claude Code hooks the lights signal when an AI task is waiting on approval' (https://claypier.com/en/ulanzi-au05-vibe-key-crowdfunding/). The official product page could not be opened (HTTP 429), and neither the GREEN FUNDING page nor the reviewer mentions approval alerts.

approve_from_device.note: Claypier lists physical confirm and reject keys. Ulanzi's blog pitches it to users who approve or reject AI suggestions (https://www.ulanzi.com/blogs/knowledges/macro-pad-vs-ai-voice-keypad). These are keystrokes (Enter or Escape) sent to the focused window, not an agent API. The reviewer used confirm (Enter) only to send dictated text, not to approve prompts.

jump_to_session.note: Keys can trigger custom hotkeys, and Ulanzi suggests it for 'switching windows' friction. No source says one press brings the waiting terminal forward, and the reviewer had not set up tab switching.

token_usage_cost.note: It has no display, only lighting. No source mentions usage or cost.

plan_limits.note: No display. No source mentions quota or limits.

personal_baseline_levels.note: Lighting follows hook events. Nothing is calibrated to the user's own history.

character_personality.note: A keypad with a status light. No screen, character or mascot.

sound_voice_out.note: No speaker or sound output is mentioned in GREEN FUNDING, Newsshooter, green-keys or the review. Only a microphone is listed.

voice_input.note: Press or hold the voice key and speak. An omnidirectional mic is designed to pick up quiet speech. Text goes to the active app through the OS or a voice app (Typeless, ChatGPT, Claude). The device does no speech recognition itself (https://www.newsshooter.com/2026/09/06/ulanzi-au05-vibekey-ai-voice-input-keypad/, https://greenfunding.jp/lab/projects/9495, https://green-keys.info/ulanziau05-vibe-key-20261003/).

physical_controls.note: 3 customizable keys (the reviewer's set was mic, confirm and cancel), a rotary push knob and a power button, all remappable in Ulanzi Studio (https://greenfunding.jp/lab/projects/9495 spec 'コントロールノブ×1／カスタマイズキー×3', https://gadgethuntingwithrr.com/reviews/ulanzi-vibe-key-review/). Ulanzi's English blog says 'six physical keys', and the vibekey README says six physical controls. Switches are hot-swappable Gateron low-profile (Claypier).

second_screen_mode.note: No display. Status shows only through lighting.
