products.name: Tokscale
products.scope_note: In scope. It is an open-source usage, cost and quota tracker for AI coding agents, with a public leaderboard, groups, a Wrapped image and streaks. It covers the gamification and usage-monitor parts of the market. It has no live agent state and no desk or companion features.
products.one_liner: An open-source Rust CLI and Ratatui TUI that reads the local session logs of about 60 AI coding agents and IDEs. It shows tokens, estimated cost and vendor plan quotas. Users can opt in to submit aggregate usage to tokscale.ai, which has public profiles, a global leaderboard (humans, models, agents and groups) and a Spotify-style yearly Wrapped image.
agents_supported: plus about 25 more listed in the README (64 rows in its client table as of 2026-11-18)

agent_status.note: It reads session logs after the fact and reports usage. The TUI can auto-refresh (30 s to 1 h, off by default) and has an optional Minutely view, but it shows no idle, working or waiting state. https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale

multi_session.note: The Sessions tab and --group-by session,model list usage and cost per session across many agents. This is a retrospective view; it does not oversee or switch between live sessions. https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale

permission_alert.note: No notifications or permission alerts appear in the README feature list; it is an analytics tool.

token_usage_cost.note: Tokens (input, output, cache read/write, reasoning) and estimated $ cost, priced from LiteLLM data with an OpenRouter fallback and custom overrides. Breakdowns by model, client, workspace and machine. https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale

plan_limits.note: `tokscale usage` and the TUI Usage tab show vendor-reported quotas with % used and reset time, e.g. the Claude 5-hour session, weekly and model-scoped limits. Also covers Codex session/weekly, Copilot premium interactions, Cursor, Grok, Kimi, MiniMax, OpenCode Go, Sakana and others. https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale

personal_baseline_levels.note: The Kardashev-scale theme is framing only. Rankings use absolute tokens and cost; no levels computed against the user's own history are documented.

ai_session_recap.note: `tokscale report` uses an LLM (Apple FM by default, or Claude, Codex, Gemini, Kiro or MiniMax) to give each session a title, category, description and complexity. A second pass groups sessions into 3 to 8 task clusters. It summarizes where tokens went; it does not suggest next steps. https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale

history_dashboard.note: The TUI has Daily, Hourly, Monthly, Projects and Stats views (contribution graph). The web has 2D and 3D contribution graphs with day breakdowns, year filters and public profiles. https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Streaks only: the web frontend's Stats panel shows total cost, tokens, active days and streaks, and Wrapped shows the longest streak of active days. The TUI Stats tab is a contribution graph. No daily goals, XP, levels or achievements found. The 'badges' are shields.io-style GitHub embeds showing tokens, cost or rank. https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale

leaderboard.note: Public global leaderboard with Humans, Models, Agents and Groups tabs and period filters (all time, last month, this month, this week, custom), sortable by tokens or estimated cost. 2,503 ranked users as of 2026-11-18. Groups have reusable invitations (v4.21.0, 2 Nov 2026). https://tokscale.ai/leaderboard

physical_controls.note: Software only.

second_screen_mode.note: Terminal TUI and website only; no dedicated display mode.

products.price_text: Free and open source (CLI and core MIT; web app AGPL-3.0). Run with `bunx tokscale@latest` or `npx tokscale@latest`. tokscale.ai shows no paid tier; the project takes GitHub Sponsors. As of 2026-11-18.
products.license: MIT for the CLI and core (crates/); AGPL-3.0 for the web app (packages/frontend); compiled data in packages/frontend/src/content is CC BY 4.0
products.privacy_note: The CLI and TUI read session logs locally and can run without network requests (`--offline`); nothing leaves the machine until the user runs `tokscale submit`, or turns on `tokscale autosubmit`, which schedules submits with launchd, systemd, cron or Windows Task Scheduler. Submitting needs a GitHub OAuth login (read:user, user:email) or an API token for CI. The CLI then sends aggregates: token counts, estimated cost, daily breakdown, client and model IDs, message counts, session timing metrics, MCP server names, CLI version, and a device key and label. The policy says it never collects prompts, responses, code, file names or provider credentials. Submitted profiles are public and listed in the sitemap, so they may be indexed. The website uses cookieless Vercel Analytics. Quota display uses the user's local vendor credentials, e.g. the Claude OAuth credentials file or macOS Keychain (README). Source: https://tokscale.ai/privacy (updated 2026-07-30).
products.distinctive: It covers about 60 AI coding agents and IDEs with one Rust CLI and TUI, more than any similar tracker. It pairs that with a public social layer: a global leaderboard of humans, models, agents and groups, public profiles, GitHub README embed cards and a Spotify-style Wrapped image. It also shows vendor-reported plan quotas (Claude 5-hour and weekly, Codex, Copilot, Cursor and others) and LLM-written per-session task reports.
products.overlap_with_reference: Overlap: both read Claude Code logs locally to show token usage, keep multi-day history, track streaks and can write AI session summaries using the user's own Claude CLI. Differences: Tokscale is a cross-platform CLI, TUI and website covering about 60 agents. It adds $ cost, vendor plan quotas and a public competitive leaderboard with groups (opt-in, GitHub login). It has no live agent state, character, desktop presence or second-screen mode. It has no permission, stop, loop, test or drift moments, no 'Go to it' jump, and no levels calibrated to the user's own baseline; its Kardashev theme ranks absolute token burn against other people.

products.name: Lockpaw
products.one_liner: Free, open-source macOS menu bar app that covers every screen with one hotkey without sleeping the Mac, so agents keep running. The cover glows amber when a coding agent needs you and teal when it is done.

agent_status.note: Shows only on the lock cover, from hooks. Amber means waiting on you, teal means done, and a red dot marks an error. Each line shows the agent name and elapsed time, e.g. 'Claude Code 2m' (README). Per-agent state on the lock screen arrived in 1.6.2 (changelog). There is no 'working' state and no view of the current action, and nothing shows while the Mac is unlocked.

multi_session.note: The README says the lock screen shows 'one quiet line per session', each with its own status dot (e.g. 'Claude Code 2m', 'Codex 12m'). It is an overview only, with no switching between sessions.

permission_alert.note: Amber glow plus a notification naming the agent and project, e.g. 'Claude Code needs permission in my-app'. Hooks per the README: Claude Code uses Notification, Stop and StopFailure; Codex uses notify and a PermissionRequest hook. Codex approval pings were added in 1.6.0, though Codex alerts already existed by 1.2.0. Alerts can also go to a phone via ntfy, Pushover or a webhook.

approve_from_device.note: The cover is built to block input. The README, the site and the release notes describe only alerts and status, with no approve or deny action. You unlock (Touch ID or password) and answer in the terminal.

jump_to_session.note: Not mentioned in the README, the site, the changelog or the release notes.

token_usage_cost.note: Not a documented feature. It uses only notification/stop-type hooks and does not read transcripts.

plan_limits.note: Not a documented feature.

personal_baseline_levels.note: Not a documented feature.

test_build_red_green.note: The red dot comes from agent errors (e.g. Claude Code StopFailure), not from test or build results.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Not a documented feature.

drift_away_detection.note: It infers presence from lock state, not from app focus. Since 1.7.2 (2026-11-07) a presence file for Claude Code Remote Control means phone pings arrive only while you are away from the Mac. Source: https://getlockpaw.com/changelog

ai_session_recap.note: Not a documented feature.

history_dashboard.note: Not a documented feature.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Not a documented feature.

leaderboard.note: Not a documented feature. There are no accounts or analytics.

character_personality.note: An origami dog or cat mascot sits on the cover, or you can use your own image or none. Supporters get 4 extra mascots and seasonal skins. The mascot has a 'slow 12-second breathing cycle' and the screen 'breathes two slow waves of light' when an agent pings (README). There is no source showing the mascot emoting or reacting to agent state.

sound_voice_out.note: Optional alert sound, off by default, set in Settings > Agents ('The glow is always silent; turn on a sound in Settings → Agents'). No speech.

voice_input.note: Not a documented feature.

physical_controls.note: Software only. Locking uses a keyboard hotkey (Cmd+Shift+L), Shortcuts, Spotlight or Siri, and unlocking uses the Mac's Touch ID or password.

second_screen_mode.note: It covers every connected display full-screen and shows the agent glow and status lines (1.0.3 fixed the cover vanishing when an external monitor connects). It is only an away/locked cover, not a second-monitor view to use while working.

products.price_text: Free (MIT) as of 2026-11-18. The README says 'Lockpaw is free and stays free' and 'everything that ships stays free'. An optional one-time supporter licence is pay-what-you-want: '$9 is a fine thank-you, $19 if it saves your afternoons'. It unlocks four extra mascots, seasonal skins for the Dog and Cat, and no more asks. There is also a GitHub Sponsors link, and contributors get a supporter licence 'on the house'.
products.license: MIT
products.privacy_note: No analytics or accounts. The only network call is the signed update check, plus any services you turn on yourself. Optional phone pings (ntfy, Pushover, webhook) send only the agent name and event.
products.distinctive: Lockpaw turns a privacy screen cover into an away-from-desk agent beacon. It covers all displays without sleeping the Mac, and the cover glows amber or teal when an agent waits or finishes. Optional lid-closed mode (a root helper that runs pmset disablesleep while locked) keeps agents running with the lid shut, and alerts can be forwarded to a phone. Hook setup covers six agents through a CLI or Settings, in a native Swift app of about 15 MB.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are free, local-first macOS apps with no account. Both use Claude Code hooks to show when Claude is waiting for permission or has stopped, both have an optional sound and a mascot, and both can fill a whole display. They differ in when they are used. Lockpaw works only while the screen is locked and you are away, and covers six agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Aider), not Claude Code alone. It adds phone push forwarding, lid-closed mode and Touch ID unlock. It has no work-intensity levels or personal baseline, no token data, no test/build, loop or drift reactions, no daily goal or streak, no AI recaps, no history dashboard, no 'Go to it' button and no DIY desk screen. Its mascot is an origami dog or cat with only an idle breathing animation, not an emoting robot. It complements the reference as much as it competes with it.

products.name: CloudCLI (Claude Code UI)
products.one_liner: Open-source (AGPL-3.0) self-hosted web/mobile GUI that runs Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Codex and OpenCode sessions, with chat, files, git, shell, tool approvals and push notifications. A paid hosted version, CloudCLI Cloud, gives each user persistent containers.

agent_status.note: Streams agent output and tool calls live. The sidebar has a 'Running now' view ('Active work will appear here while a provider is processing'), and running task rows show the last tool name, a summary and a token count. v1.37.4 also reports turns driven from the Claude CLI as running. Seen in the v1.37.9 frontend bundle on npm and in the releases page.

multi_session.note: Sidebar of projects and sessions, auto-discovered from ~/.claude. README: 'Resume conversations, manage multiple sessions, and track history'. permission_alert.note: An in-chat 'Permission required' panel, plus opt-in web push, desktop and webhook notifications for the 'Action Required: Tool "X" needs approval', 'Run Stopped', 'Run Failed' and 'Background work finished' events. approve_from_device.note: Allow once, Always allow (saved as a rule) and Deny buttons in the web/mobile UI, plus answers to AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode and MCP elicitation requests (v1.37.8). It works through the SDK canUseTool hook, so it covers sessions CloudCLI runs itself, not prompts in a separate terminal. In bypass/auto modes the interactive prompts do not reach the UI. Default approval timeout is 55s (CLAUDE_TOOL_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS), seen in claude-runtime.provider.js.

jump_to_session.note: Clicking a push notification focuses an existing CloudCLI tab and sends it to /session/<id>, or opens a new window there (notificationclick handler in dist/sw.js). This brings up the session in its own UI, not a terminal or editor window.

token_usage_cost.note: A token-usage/context-window button in the composer, plus 'Total tokens used' with an input/output breakdown (bundle). CloudCLI Cloud (cloudcli.ai): Hobby EUR 7/mo (1 active environment, 2 CPU/4GB RAM; upgrade to 4 or 8 cores from EUR 9/mo); Growth EUR 20/mo (5 environments, 2 CPU/4GB each; Large 4 CPU/8GB EUR 9/mo, XL 8 CPU/16GB EUR 25/mo, extra environment EUR 5/mo); Team EUR 39/mo (5 environments, 5 members, owner/admin/member roles, central billing; extra environment EUR 5/mo); Enterprise custom. products.license: AGPL-3.0-or-later
products.privacy_note: Self-hosted mode runs on your own machine, and reaching it from a phone needs your own network or tunnel. CloudCLI Cloud is an account-based hosted container service. Optional outbound integrations: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for voice STT/TTS, a webhook for run events, and web push through the browser vendor's push service.
products.distinctive: One of the most popular open-source remote GUIs for coding-agent CLIs (14.7k GitHub stars as of 2026-11-18). It is a full IDE-like web/PWA client (chat, file editor, git, shell, browser panel, plugin system) that runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI and OpenCode itself. It adds in-UI tool approvals, push/desktop/webhook alerts that deep-link to the session, and voice in/out, and sells a hosted container version from EUR 7/mo.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both make Claude Code activity visible outside the terminal and alert when Claude needs permission or has stopped. CloudCLI goes further on control: you approve, deny or answer from any browser or phone, push notifications deep-link to the session, it handles several agents (Codex, Cursor CLI, OpenCode) and many sessions, and it has a hosted cloud option. It has none of the reference's motivation and ambient layer: no levels against a personal baseline, no streaks or daily goal, no mascot, no detection of test fail-to-pass, loops or drift, no AI session recaps, no built-in 30-day dashboard (only through third-party usage plugins), no second-screen scene and no desk hardware. The reference is local-only, macOS and Claude Code only, and does not approve from the robot. CloudCLI is a full remote GUI that replaces the terminal rather than sitting beside it.

products.name: Fetch (tryfetch.dev)
products.scope_note: In scope. This is a paid, closed-source macOS notch app that shows a status light for each running Claude Code and Codex session. It also lets you answer questions and tool-call approvals, approve plans, start background agents, drop files onto a session as a prompt, and dictate from the notch. It is not the same product as the open-source notch projects with similar names (Notchy, claude-notch, NotchStatus, cc-sessions-viewer).
products.one_liner: A $19.99 one-time macOS notch app ("a status light for Claude Code and Codex"). Each session gets its own light: green when idle, red when working, yellow when it is waiting on you. From the notch you can answer Claude Code's questions, approve tool calls and plans, start background agents, drop files onto a session as a prompt, and dictate on-device.

agent_status.note: Each session has its own light: green idle, red working, yellow waiting on you. Hover to 'see exactly what any one of them is doing'. The Polar listing describes a coloured dot per session for 'working, waiting, or finished', and the notch 'lights up when it's done' for agents you dispatch.

multi_session.note: Tagline: 'Run a fleet of agents from your notch'. Claude Code and Codex sessions appear side by side, each with its own logo and light, grouped by tool when more than one kind is running. Fetch finds every session on its own. The Polar listing says 'Run six agents at once and know which one is blocked, at a glance' (https://polar.sh/checkout/polar_c_QUQqG4Njsh0vGHNRYPFl3JTEY5mn6bKFisk0T4Ga0rG).

permission_alert.note: The yellow light means an agent is waiting on you. Meta description: 'Never miss an agent waiting on you.' Polar listing: 'See who needs you.'

approve_from_device.note: When Claude Code asks something mid-plan, the answer options appear in the notch (the site mock-up shows a numbered multiple-choice question), and plans can be approved there. The Polar listing adds 'Approve a tool call or pick an option from the notch itself' (https://polar.sh/checkout/polar_c_QUQqG4Njsh0vGHNRYPFl3JTEY5mn6bKFisk0T4Ga0rG). Neither source says whether Codex prompts can be answered the same way.

jump_to_session.note: 'Hover for detail, click through to the session' and 'click straight through to that agent' (site and its JS feature text).

token_usage_cost.note: Not mentioned on the site or the Polar listing.

Activating a licence key on up to 3 Macs probably means an online licence check (inferred, not documented). Purchase goes through Polar (merchant of record). products.distinctive: Commercial take on the notch-status-light idea. One glance covers a mixed Claude Code and Codex fleet, and you can act without opening a terminal: answer Claude Code's mid-plan questions or approve a tool call, approve plans, dispatch a background agent from the notch (pick project, task and permission mode), and use a 'drop shelf' to park files or drop one onto a session as a prompt. products.overlap_with_reference: Both are macOS apps that make Claude Code activity visible outside the terminal, flag when the agent is waiting on you, and can bring you to the session (Fetch: click through; reference: 'Go to it'). They differ on almost everything else. Fetch is paid ($19.99), adds Codex, is built for many sessions at once, and acts on the agent: answering questions and tool-call approvals, approving plans, launching agents, sending files as prompts and on-device dictation, none of which the reference does. The reference is free and has things Fetch does not mention: a pixel-art robot character, intensity levels calibrated to the user's own 30-day history, moment detection (test/build fail-then-pass, loops, drift to another app, long sessions), daily goal and streak, AI session recaps, a today/30-day dashboard, a full-screen second-monitor scene and a DIY USB desk screen.

products.name: Vibe Notch (formerly Claude Island)
products.scope_note: This is a real product and is in scope. The repo was renamed from Claude Island to Vibe Notch with v1.3.2 on 2026-04-20, and github.com/farouqaldori/claude-island now 301-redirects to the vibe-notch repo (checked 2026-11-18). The Homebrew cask vibe-notch lists claude-island as its former token. It is a different product from Vibe Island (vibeisland.app), a paid app by another maker ('Edward'): $19.99 one-time for one Mac, with a 2-day free trial. That site does not say whether Vibe Island is open source.
products.one_liner: Free, open-source macOS menu-bar app that expands from the MacBook notch. It shows live Claude Code session status, lets you Allow or Deny tool permissions in place, and shows each session's chat history and token count.

agent_status.note: Each session row shows its phase: 'Processing...', 'Compacting...', 'Waiting for approval' or 'Ready'. It also shows the latest tool call or message. Processing, compacting and approval show an animated spinner; ready shows a green dot; idle and ended show a gray dot (ClaudeInstancesView.swift). The site says: 'See processing states, tool calls, and file operations live' (https://vibenotch.app/).

multi_session.note: README: 'Track multiple Claude Code sessions in real-time'. Site: 'Monitor multiple instances and switch with a click' (https://vibenotch.app/). Sessions are sorted with approval, processing and compacting first, then ready, then idle or ended (ClaudeInstancesView.swift). v1.3 added live subagent tracking.

permission_alert.note: Site: 'Get notified when Claude needs your approval.' The closed notch widens to show an amber indicator for a pending permission. It opens automatically only when no terminal window is visible on the current Space (NotchView.swift). AskUserQuestion prompts show 'Claude Code needs your input' (ChatView.swift).

approve_from_device.note: Allow and Deny buttons appear inline in the instances list and in the chat view. They call sessionMonitor.approvePermission / denyPermission over the hooks socket (ClaudeInstancesView.swift, ChatView.swift). Limits: AskUserQuestion cannot be answered here and offers a 'Terminal' button instead. The 'Message Claude...' text field works only for tmux sessions; otherwise it reads 'Open Claude Code in tmux to enable messaging'.

jump_to_session.note: The eye/focus button appears only when the session runs in tmux and yabai is installed. WindowFocuser runs 'yabai -m window --focus' and has no fallback without yabai (WindowFocuser.swift, ClaudeInstancesView.swift). A competitor's comparison rates its terminal jump as 'Basic' (https://vibeisland.app/alternatives/).

token_usage_cost.note: v1.3 (2026-04-12) added a token total per session (session.usage.formattedTotal), shown next to each title and hidden when it is zero. There is no $ cost (https://github.com/farouqaldori/vibe-notch/releases).

plan_limits.note: Not in the README or site features. A competitor's comparison table marks 'Usage limits tracking: No' for Claude Island (https://vibeisland.app/alternatives/).

personal_baseline_levels.note: No activity or intensity levels of any kind. It shows phase status only.

test_build_red_green.note: Tool calls and results appear raw in the chat view (ToolResultViews). Nothing in the README, site or the views inspected detects test or build pass/fail.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Not in the README, the site or the views inspected. The only liveness feature is v1.3's dead-process detection.

drift_away_detection.note: TerminalVisibilityDetector checks whether the session's terminal is the frontmost app (and, for tmux, the active pane). It also checks whether any terminal is visible on the current Space. The app plays the ready sound only when the session is not focused, and auto-opens the notch for a permission only when no terminal is visible. It does not track time away or report drift as an event (TerminalVisibilityDetector.swift, NotchView.swift).

ai_session_recap.note: It shows the full chat transcript with markdown, but no AI-written summary.

history_dashboard.note: Chat history is a per-session transcript only. There are no analytics across days or weeks.

streaks_goals_achievements.note: No gamification in the README, site or UI.

leaderboard.note: No social or team comparison.

character_personality.note: The header shows a small Claude Code crab icon (ClaudeCrabIcon, 16 pt, drawn in Canvas rectangles). Its legs animate while a session is processing, and the notch bounces when a session becomes ready. The eyes are fixed, with no expressions or emotion states (NotchHeaderView.swift, NotchView.swift).

sound_voice_out.note: A 'Notification Sound' setting offers None or one of 14 macOS system sounds (Pop, Ping, Glass and others). The sound plays when a session finishes and is ready for input, and only if that session's terminal is not focused (Settings.swift, SoundPickerRow.swift, NotchView.swift). There is no speech.

voice_input.note: ChatView.swift has no microphone, speech or dictation code. Input is a text field, and only for tmux sessions.

physical_controls.note: Software only.

second_screen_mode.note: It runs as a notch overlay. A screen picker chooses which display hosts it, but there is no dedicated full-screen or device mode.

products.price_text: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). Download the DMG from GitHub releases or vibenotch.app, or run `brew install --cask vibe-notch` (a Homebrew cask, not mentioned in the README). No paid tier. As of 2026-11-18.
products.license: Apache-2.0
products.privacy_note: Claude Code hooks send session state to the app over a local Unix socket, whose permissions v1.3 tightened. There is no account. The app is not fully offline. The README says it sends 'anonymous' Mixpanel analytics: app launches with version, build and macOS version, and session starts. It says no personal data or conversation content is collected. In AppDelegate.swift, the Mixpanel distinct ID is the Mac's hardware platform UUID (kIOPlatformUUIDKey), with a random UUID as fallback, and the Claude Code version is also sent. There is no opt-out setting in the code. Sparkle checks for updates every hour.
products.distinctive: It is an early (December 2025) open-source 'Dynamic Island for Claude Code' notch app, and Notchi's README credits it as 'design inspiration'. Its strength is in-place Allow/Deny of tool permissions across several live sessions, with a full markdown chat transcript in the notch. Since v1.3 it also shows a token count per session. It alerts only when you are not looking at the session's terminal.
products.overlap_with_reference:
Overlap with the reference: both are free macOS apps for Claude Code only, built on hooks. Both show live agent status, alert when Claude waits for permission, can bring the terminal forward and play sounds. Both have some sense of whether you are looking at the terminal: Vibe Notch mutes its sound and auto-open when the session's terminal is frontmost or visible.

Differences: Vibe Notch lets you approve or deny from the notch, which the reference does not. It handles many sessions in a list with full chat transcripts. Its jump to terminal needs tmux plus yabai, while the reference's 'Go to it' does not. Its only character is a tiny crab icon whose legs move while Claude works. It has no emoting robot.

It lacks the rest of what defines the reference: no intensity levels from personal baselines, no test/build, loop or long-session moments, no daily goal or streak, no AI recaps, no history dashboard, no second-monitor scene and no DIY hardware. It also always sends Mixpanel telemetry keyed to the hardware UUID, unlike the local-first reference.

products.name: Petdex
products.scope_note: In scope. Petdex has three parts: a pet-skin gallery, a CLI, and a free desktop app. The app floats a pet that reacts to hooks from Claude Code, Codex and other agents, keeps an activity bubble for each conversation (up to 8), and focuses the originating terminal when you click the pet. It is not a duplicate: third-party projects such as petdex-cc, petdex-dock and pi-pokepet only reuse its pets or manifest.
products.one_liner: An open-source gallery of 5,200+ community-made animated pixel pets for coding agents, installed with `npx petdex install <slug>`. A free floating desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) animates the pet on agent hook events and shows an activity bubble for each conversation. Clicking the pet focuses the originating terminal.

agent_status.note: The pet 'animates on every tool call your agent makes'. It has 9 sprite states: idle, running-right, running-left, waving, jumping, failed, waiting, running and review. Supported agents' hooks map onto these states, and an activity bubble keeps each conversation's title, state and agent (README; https://github.com/crafter-station/petdex/issues/657). Dr. Web's list of states (Running, Needs input, Done, Blocked) comes from OpenAI's Pets documentation, not from Petdex.

multi_session.note: There is one activity bubble per conversation or session, keyed by session ID and capped at 8 with least-recently-updated eviction. It shipped in desktop v0.5.0 (https://github.com/crafter-station/petdex/issues/657). After a focus, the other conversations stay visible (https://github.com/crafter-station/petdex/pull/810). Durable session recovery covers Codex, Claude, Gemini, OMP and Hermes, and remote SSH agents can drive the same pet (desktop README).

permission_alert.note: The pet enters the 'waiting' state when the agent is blocked on the user. An opt-in 'Waiting sound' chime plays then, with one follow-up chime if the prompt goes unanswered for 2 minutes (https://github.com/crafter-station/petdex/pull/608, merged 2026-07-28). Since 0.9.2-rc.2, pending input survives a restart (https://github.com/crafter-station/petdex/releases).

approve_from_device.note: No source shows approving or answering from the pet. Clicking the pet focuses the originating terminal, and clicks on the bubble pass through to the window behind it (https://petdex.dev/docs).

jump_to_session.note: Clicking the PET (not the bubble) focuses the originating window of the most recent conversation. The first version was macOS only and allowlisted two apps: Apple Terminal (exact tab, matched by TTY) and VS Code (app-level activation only) (https://github.com/crafter-station/petdex/pull/656, merged 2026-08-08). The bubble is cleared after a successful focus (PR #810, v0.9.2). The Herdr plugin focuses the exact pane, and DSH activates the browser (desktop README). Clicks on the bubble itself pass through (https://petdex.dev/docs).

token_usage_cost.note: Not mentioned in the README, docs, download page, releases or press.

test_build_red_green.note: There is a 'failed' sprite state, but no source shows the app detecting a test or build failure and then a pass. The daily.dev post makes no claims about tests.

drift_away_detection.note: The only related behavior is a timed re-chime after 2 minutes with no answer (PR #608). It does not detect that the user is away or in another app.

history_dashboard.note: The web gallery has install and like stats for pets, but no source shows a history of coding activity.

leaderboard.note: The public Creators leaderboard (petdex.dev/leaderboard) ranks pet artists, with tabs Most pets, Most loved, Most installed, Rising and Collectors. It does not rank coding activity.

character_personality.note: Animated pixel pets with 9 emotive sprite states (waving, jumping, failed, waiting, review and others), drawn from 5,208+ community skins.

sound_voice_out.note: An opt-in 'Waiting sound' toggle in Appearance, off by default, plays a system sound when the pet starts waiting for input, plus one follow-up chime after 2 minutes unanswered. The sound is Glass.aiff via afplay on macOS, canberra-gtk-play on Linux, and MessageBeep on Windows (https://github.com/crafter-station/petdex/pull/608). The app does not speak.

physical_controls.note: Software only. You interact by dragging, right-clicking (which cycles the 9 sprite states) and keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+, and Cmd+W).

second_screen_mode.note: Only a floating, always-on-top sprite window is documented. A fix for multi-display input exists, but there is no dedicated full-screen mode.

products.price_text: Free (as of 2026-11-18). The CLI, desktop app and gallery cost nothing, and the source code is MIT-licensed. Dr. Web: 'Installation und Nutzung kosten nichts.' An account is needed only to submit pets, manage collections, or use Flock and account sync.
products.license: MIT for the source code. Pet assets stay with their submitters under the license each one declares (per-pet license declared since CLI v1.3.0); many are fan art.
products.privacy_note: Agent hooks post to a token-gated local server on 127.0.0.1:7777. The token rotates on every boot and is stored with mode 0600. Session recovery reads local transcripts read-only, and there is a killswitch file. Pets are downloaded from petdex.dev. Sign-in is optional ('No account required to install. Sign in only when you submit'). The CLI keeps its tokens in the OS keychain (service petdex-cli). Tracing is off by default. No telemetry policy was found. unverified: sign-in uses Clerk OAuth with PKCE.

The homepage lists 5,208+ pets (as of 2026-11-18). A daily.dev post (2026-11-07, Crafter Station squad) had 21 upvotes and 3 comments (seen 2026-11-18) and cites 32 third-party integrations using the manifest. products.distinctive: Petdex combines a very large community skin catalog with a cross-platform native desktop pet. The catalog has 5,208+ pets, a creators leaderboard, an open sprite-sheet format, and a public manifest API that about 32 other projects reuse. The pet hooks into 8+ coding agents, including remote agents over an SSH reverse tunnel. It keeps one activity bubble per conversation (up to 8) and has an opt-in waiting chime. Clicking the pet focuses the originating terminal.
products.overlap_with_reference: Strong overlap on the core loop. Both put a pixel character on the desktop that reacts to Claude Code hooks, shows when the agent is waiting for input, and offers a click that brings the waiting terminal forward (like "Go to it"). Petdex's click is on the pet, focuses only the most recent conversation, and covers only Apple Terminal tabs and VS Code at app level on macOS. Both are free and local-first. Petdex goes wider on breadth: 8+ agents instead of Claude Code only, macOS/Windows/Linux, 5,200+ swappable skins, per-session bubbles, remote SSH agents, an opt-in waiting chime, a creators leaderboard, and optional accounts. No source shows any of the reference product's motivation layer: intensity levels calibrated to the user's own history, tokens/hour, test fail-then-pass moments, loop or drift detection, a daily goal and streak, AI recaps, a 30-day dashboard, a second-monitor scene, or a DIY desk screen.

products.name: Clauddy for Divoom MiniToo (bugzmanov)
products.scope_note: In scope. It is an open hobby project that turns an off-the-shelf Divoom MiniToo pixel speaker into a Claude Code status display. It is not a product for sale. Do not confuse it with other projects called "Clauddy": fwnzyy/clauddy is a Windows desktop pet, clauddy.github.io is an API reseller, and a "clauddy" theme also appears in sliceofsanta/divoom-ditoo-pro-controller. (These name clashes come from the earlier research and were not re-checked here.)
products.one_liner: Claude Code hooks plus a reverse-engineered Bluetooth toolkit. Together they switch a Divoom MiniToo (or Tiivoo 2) pixel display between three animated faces of a pixel mascot: working, alerting (waiting on you) and chilling. The code is public but has no licence.

agent_status.note: Three faces. Working is set on UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse, alerting on Notification, and chilling on Stop. The README says it 'switches faces in under a second'. The PreToolUse mapping was added by contributor Scott Jennings on 2026-04-28. Source: https://github.com/bugzmanov/divoom-minitoo/tree/main/apps/clauddy

multi_session.note: clauddy-hook.sh merges several concurrent Claude sessions into one face through the shared file /tmp/clauddy-hook-state, ranked chilling < working < alerting. By default an alert is held for 5 s and working for 2 s before a lower state can replace it, and blocked downgrades are retried later. There is no per-session view and no way to switch between sessions.

permission_alert.note: The README maps the Notification hook to 'alerting (permission prompt or idle waiting on you)'. That face shows the mascot with a yellow '!' overhead.

approve_from_device.note: The hook wrapper runs the Bluetooth call in the background, discards its output and always exits 0. It never returns a decision to Claude Code, so the data flows one way only. The README does not describe any input from the device.

jump_to_session.note: Not offered. It is a one-way Bluetooth display driven by hooks.

token_usage_cost.note: Shows only three state faces.

plan_limits.note: Not tracked.

personal_baseline_levels.note: Three fixed states mapped from hook events.

test_build_red_green.note: Only the UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Notification and Stop hooks are used. Tool results are not inspected.

loop_stuck_detection.note: Not present.

drift_away_detection.note: Not present.

ai_session_recap.note: Not present.

history_dashboard.note: No history is kept. The state file holds only the current face and a Unix timestamp (clauddy-hook.sh).

streaks_goals_achievements.note: Not present.

leaderboard.note: Not present.

character_personality.note: An orange pixel mascot in three animated GIFs, checked frame by frame: typing at a laptop with the caption 'Kombuchaching' (83 frames), standing with a yellow '!' overhead (17 frames), and lounging in a deck chair with a drink and a music note (27 frames). The Aseprite sources are included and can be edited. Source: https://github.com/bugzmanov/divoom-minitoo/tree/main/apps/clauddy/assets

sound_voice_out.note: The MiniToo is a Bluetooth speaker, but clauddy-hook.sh only writes the state file and calls set-clauddy-state.sh to switch faces. Nothing plays audio.

voice_input.note: Not present.

physical_controls.note: The interface is display only and driven by hooks. Clauddy reads no input from the device. Divoom's comparison page lists the MiniToo's controls as 'App + one-tap sync'.

second_screen_mode.note: A separate desk device: a Divoom MiniToo with a 1.77 in, 160x128 pixel display, or a Divoom Tiivoo 2, controlled over Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM.

products.price_text: The software is free, but the repo has no LICENSE file. It needs a Divoom MiniToo, bought separately. Divoom's own comparison article (published 2026-07-22, seen 2026-11-18) lists it at $69.99 and the MiniToo + Ditoo-Pro bundle at $149.98. The Divoom Tiivoo 2 also works. unverified: a $20 code MNT20 on some Divoom regional pages, and third-party listings (AUD 79 at JB Hi-Fi, CAD 89.99 at Staples Canada, EUR 53.99 at aio.lv). These came from the earlier researcher's search results and could not be re-opened on 2026-11-18.
products.license: None specified. There is no LICENSE or LICENSE.md (raw fetch returns 404), and the GitHub search API reports license null. The code is public but has no open-source licence. The README also warns that the eZip bridge patches Divoom's iOS framework object files and asks people to read FINDINGS.md §8h before redistributing builds.
products.privacy_note: At run time, state goes from local Claude Code hooks to the device over local Bluetooth, and no agent data leaves the Mac. The installer requires a one-time Divoom account login (install.sh --email) to look up custom face IDs and style settings. The README says the password is entered at a hidden prompt and never written to disk, and the Divoom token is kept in memory only. ~/.clauddy/config stores only the Bluetooth MAC, DeviceId, ClockIds and StyleIds.
products.distinctive: The author reverse-engineered the MiniToo's undocumented Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM protocol and built an uploader that works around the SiFli eZip native library. Three GIFs are preloaded into the device's custom-face slots, and Channel/SetClockSelectId switches between them almost instantly. It uses a cheap retail pixel speaker instead of DIY electronics, and adds simple severity-based merging when several sessions run at once.
products.overlap_with_reference: Both target Claude Code only, run locally, and use a pixel character that emotes to show agent state, including a 'waiting on you' alert, on a dedicated desk screen. The reference's optional DIY ESP32/XIAO TFT board is the closest match. Clauddy is much narrower: three fixed hook-driven states on an off-the-shelf $69.99 Divoom MiniToo over Bluetooth. It has none of the reference's other features: no desktop robot, no intensity levels set against the user's own history, no test, loop, drift or long-session moments, no 'Go to it' jump, no goals or streaks, no AI recaps, no usage dashboard and no sound. It needs a Divoom account login at install. It does merge several concurrent sessions into one face ranked by severity.
products.hardware: Uses a retail Divoom MiniToo, a small retro-TV-style Bluetooth speaker. Divoom gives the display as 1.77 in, and the repo says it is 160x128. Tested on firmware 2.4.0. A macOS IOBluetooth daemon controls it over Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM, on channel 1 only since PR #3. The Divoom Tiivoo 2 (advertised as 'Divoom Tiivoo 2-Audio') is also supported: it runs the same Jieli firmware and protocol. The face art is 160x160 and center-cropped to the 160x128 screen. Divoom lists the MiniToo at $69.99. Clauddy does not use the device's speaker or any input from it.

products.name: Clauddy (desktop pet, renatoaug)
products.scope_note: In scope. The product is now called "Clauddy" (npm package 'clauddy'; the first release ran as 'bunx claude-usage-monitor'). The two other URLs from discovery are different, unrelated products, not aliases. theDanButuc/Claude-Usage-Monitor is a native Swift macOS menu-bar usage app with no pet (56 stars as of 2026-11-18). gaborvidovics76/ClaudeUsageMonitor is a Windows/macOS always-on-top usage-limit widget with no pet (3 stars as of 2026-11-18). This profile covers only renatoaug's repo. Repos under dipedro, Sarcineli and jonathanpiette are forks of it.
products.one_liner: Free, open-source pixel-art desktop pet (native Rust) for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. It shows real session and weekly limit percentages, token counts and a 30-day heatmap, and it reacts with moods, speech bubbles and an optional chiptune voice.

agent_status.note: Moods are idle, working (a turn is open), sleeping (idle 5+ min), on fire and maxed out. A status line shows '● working · 1.6M tok/min' and names the current activity (reading, editing, running, planning, researching, delegating, waiting), classified from tool names in the Claude Code logs. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/docs/design/02-features.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/native/src/usage.rs

multi_session.note: Tokens are summed across all session logs, but the activity label follows a single session: the first open turn among the 8 newest logs written in the last 30 minutes. Compact view has one row per connected service (Claude, Codex, Cursor), and the mood follows whichever service is working, with provider logos. It follows one Claude account at a time. There is no per-session overview. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/native/src/usage.rs

permission_alert.note: The status line says 'waiting' only when Claude calls the AskUserQuestion tool. Permission prompts are not detected: an unanswered prompt shows as an open turn ('working'). No notification or remark is sent for either. Its notifications are about usage thresholds and resets. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/native/src/usage.rs

approve_from_device.note: Read-only monitor of logs and usage. The documented controls are the ⋯ menu (Change pet, Settings, Usage page, Check for updates), Notify at reset, size toggles and × to quit.

jump_to_session.note: 'A click on a notification brings the widget to the front', not the terminal. No terminal-focus action is documented (05-alerts.md, 02-features.md).

token_usage_cost.note: Session tokens, 7-day tokens, tokens by model and by project, tokens/min and today's tokens. 'All figures are in tokens and percent, never dollars.' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/docs/design/02-features.md

plan_limits.note: Real 5-hour session % and weekly % from api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage, plus scoped per-model weekly limits (e.g. Opus, Sonnet), each with time until reset. A burn-rate projection (Claude only) appears about 5 minutes into a session. Threshold alerts at 80% and 95% by default, plus a one-shot 'Notify at reset' reminder. Codex % and Cursor's monthly budget (included and API models) are also tracked. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/docs/design/04-usage.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/native/src/auth.rs Catches fire when session usage passes a configurable threshold (90% by default). The npm 'clauddy' package is a launcher that downloads the native app.

personal_baseline_levels.note: The 30-day heat map shades each day relative to the user's own busiest day in the window (ratio bands <0.3, <0.6, <0.85, else top level), and a 'new record day' remark compares with the 30-day best. Moods use fixed thresholds: fire at 90% of the session by default, maxed at 100%, sleep after 5 min idle. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/native/src/components/heat_map.rs

test_build_red_green.note: Activity is classified by tool name only (Bash means 'running'). Tool results are not parsed for content or is_error, so test or build output is never read (native/src/usage.rs).

loop_stuck_detection.note: No loop or stuck trigger among the moods or the speech triggers in native/src/talk.rs.

drift_away_detection.note: After the fact only: a 'Welcome back! You were gone 3h 0m' remark fires when the pet wakes after 120+ minutes with no agent activity, and a stretch remark fires after 90 minutes of unbroken work. It does not detect the user leaving or switching apps while the agent waits. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/native/src/talk.rs

ai_session_recap.note: The session-reset recap is built from usage tracking (previous %, peak tokens, active time, most-used activity, e.g. 'Fresh window! That was 34.0M tokens, mostly editing code'), not AI-written (native/src/talk.rs).

history_dashboard.note: 30-day map with one square per day, green (light) to red (heavy), and a total, plus 7-day breakdowns by model and by project. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/docs/design/02-features.md

streaks_goals_achievements.note: No streaks, goals, XP, badges or unlocks are documented. The code's 'streak' is 90 minutes of continuous work that triggers a stretch remark, and there is a 'new record day' remark. Pets are chosen freely or swapped in by holiday packs (06-pets.md, talk.rs).

leaderboard.note: Local-only. No social or team features are documented.

character_personality.note: Animated pixel pet. Its working sprite sheet has typing at a desk, blinking, struggling and cheering. It also has idle, sleeping ('Z z'), on-fire (flames) and maxed-out (slumps and sweats) moods, with speech bubbles on events. Pets: Clauddy, Wizard, Astronaut and Getaway, plus holiday Santa, Reindeer and Gingerbread (Dec 24-25) and Pumpkin (Oct 31). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/docs/design/06-pets.md

sound_voice_out.note: An optional chiptune 'voice' of square-wave blips, one per letter, generated live. It plays only on headline remarks, is macOS-only for now, is off by default, and is silent in menu-bar mode and outside expanded size. The macOS notification sound plays only for the highest threshold. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/docs/design/02-features.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renatoaug/claude-usage-monitor/main/docs/design/05-alerts.md

voice_input.note: None documented. Output-only monitor.

physical_controls.note: Software only, no hardware.

second_screen_mode.note: A floating widget (expanded, compact or pet-only) or a menu-bar/tray icon. No full-screen or second-monitor mode is documented (02-features.md).

products.price_text: Free; MIT-licensed open source. Install with a curl script (macOS app that opens at login) or run with `bunx clauddy` (npx with Node 18+ also works); npm 'clauddy' v2.7.2 is a launcher that downloads the native build. No paid tier (as of 2026-11-18).
products.license: MIT
products.privacy_note: Data stays in ~/.claude-usage-monitor/ and there is no maker account or server. Token counts come from local Claude Code (and Codex) logs. Outbound calls: an optional Claude OAuth login and usage reads to api.anthropic.com (for the real session and weekly %), Cursor's dashboard endpoints if Cursor is connected, and a GitHub releases check 8 seconds after launch and every 6 hours that cannot be turned off in settings. The README's privacy line leaves out the update check.
products.distinctive: A desktop pet focused on plan limits. It mirrors the official Claude Settings > Usage panel through OAuth: session and weekly %, scoped per-model weekly %, reset times, a burn-rate projection, threshold alerts and reset reminders. It also follows Codex and Cursor. Rewritten on 2026-11-07 from Electron into a native Rust/egui app (v2.0.0, PR #70) of about 20 MB. It runs on macOS on Apple Silicon (the first-class build), Windows x64 (including WSL logs) and Linux x64, with holiday costume packs and a chiptune voice generated live. Released very often (v1.0.0 on 22 Jun 2026, v2.7.2 on 17 Nov 2026).
products.overlap_with_reference: Both are free, local-first pixel-art desktop characters for Claude Code with moods and a 30-day history view. Clauddy leans toward quota monitoring: real session, weekly and per-model limits through OAuth, reset times, burn rate and 80%/95% alerts. It also supports Codex, Cursor, Windows and Linux, which the reference does not. Its moods use fixed usage thresholds. Only its heat map shading and a 'record day' remark are relative to the user's own 30-day history. It lacks the reference's test/build red-green, loop and drift reactions, its Go-to-terminal button, its daily goal and streak, its AI session recaps, and its second-monitor scene and DIY desk screen. Its permission awareness is limited to AskUserQuestion showing as 'waiting'.

adjacent.name: Codex pets (OpenAI)
adjacent.one_liner: First-party optional animated pets that show Codex agent state. In the ChatGPT desktop app (macOS and Windows) the pet floats above other windows. It tracks four states across multiple chats (Running, Needs input, Ready, Blocked) and shows the most urgent one first, in this order: Needs input > Blocked > Ready > Running. Terminal pets in the Codex CLI cover a single session and need iTerm2 3.6+, Kitty graphics or Sixel (not inside tmux or Zellij). The web version is limited to an in-chat pet, and the IDE extension has none. You can make custom pets with the bundled 'hatch-pet' skill (stored locally) or upload a 1536x1872 PNG/WebP sprite sheet on the web.
adjacent.price_text: No extra charge. Included with ChatGPT/Codex plans, which as of 2026-11-18 are listed as Free $0, Go $8, Plus $20, Pro from $100 ($100/$200/$500) and Business $20/user/mo billed annually ($25 monthly). OpenAI's pets page names no plan requirement and says availability depends on account and workspace.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party for Codex only (desktop app, CLI, web). OpenAI documents no public API or hooks for third parties driving the pet. The pet format has nonetheless become a de facto cross-agent standard: a folder holding pet.json plus a spritesheet in an 8x9 grid of 192x208 px frames, with an 8x11 v2 grid, following the hatch-pet spec. Community reuse: (1) Petdex (github.com/crafter-station/petdex) is a gallery plus npm CLI plus desktop app. It runs a local hook server on 127.0.0.1:7777 and animates pets for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and others. MIT licence, about 4.4k stars and 218 forks as of 2026-11-18. (2) Clawdex (github.com/danielkempe/clawdex) is a macOS overlay for Claude Code. It loads unmodified pets from ~/.codex/pets via Claude Code hooks and a statusline heartbeat. MIT licence, 5 stars as of 2026-11-18. (3) YaKun9/codex-pets is a community pet library (yakun9.github.io/codex-pets) with 9 pets as of 2026-11-18. (4) Search results also show agentpet, petpet and nom-pet, which reuse the format for Claude Code and Codex (repos not opened).
adjacent.relevance: Direct threat and benchmark. OpenAI ships, at no extra cost, the core of a desktop agent companion: an always-on-top pet that tracks multiple sessions with exactly the states that matter (working, needs you, done, failed) and a sensible priority order. This commoditises software desk pets for Codex users and resets what users expect. It is also inspiration and a possible partner surface: the open pet format and its community (Petdex, Clawdex) mean a companion that reads Codex pet packs gets hundreds of characters for free and could work across agents. Remaining gaps a maker can own: physical or hardware presence, Claude Code and other agents (OpenAI's pet is Codex-only), tmux users, and IDE users.

adjacent.name: Claude Code Remote Control and mobile push
adjacent.one_liner: First-party feature that connects claude.ai/code and the Claude iOS/Android app to a Claude Code session running on your own machine (from the CLI, VS Code or the Desktop app). You start it with 'claude remote-control' (server mode, up to 32 concurrent sessions by default, same-dir or worktree spawn modes, QR code) or with /remote-control (/rc) inside a session. Permission prompts and questions are forwarded to the phone or browser and stay open until you answer. Two /config toggles control mobile push: 'Push when Claude decides' and 'Push when actions required'. Pushes are skipped while you are focused on the terminal, and CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE can suppress them whenever you are at the machine. The connection is outbound HTTPS only, and there is an optional Trusted Devices requirement. Related first-party options: Dispatch (send the Desktop app a task from the phone), Channels (Telegram, Discord, iMessage) and cloud sessions.
adjacent.price_text: No separate charge. Included with claude.ai Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise plans (Team and Enterprise need an Owner to enable it). Not available with Console API keys, third-party providers such as Bedrock, or a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party for Claude Code: CLI, VS Code extension and Claude Desktop Code tab on the computer side, with the Claude mobile apps and claude.ai/code as clients. Extension points relevant to hardware: the CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE marker file (pushes are skipped while it exists), Channels plugins for pushing events in, and the /config push toggles. No third-party hardware integration with Remote Control itself was found.
adjacent.relevance: Major platform risk for approval-remote and notification products. Anthropic now gives subscribers phone approvals of permission prompts, push when Claude needs a decision or finishes, multi-session steering, and attachments from the phone, all at no extra cost. A desk companion has to win on what this lacks: ambient, glanceable, physical status without unlocking a phone; one-press approvals at the desk; and support for API-key, Bedrock or gateway users and other agents, who are excluded. Possible partner hook: a desk device that senses presence could write CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE so pushes go to the phone only when you are away.

adjacent.name: Claude Code status line
adjacent.one_liner: First-party custom status bar: Claude Code runs any shell command you configure and passes it session JSON on stdin. The JSON includes model.id/display_name, workspace and repo, cost.total_cost_usd (client-side estimate), total_duration_ms, lines added/removed, context_window (input/output tokens, size, used_percentage/remaining_percentage, current_usage), effort.level, prompt_cache stats, session_id/session_name, transcript_path, pr.number/review_state, worktree.*, and rate_limits.five_hour/seven_day used_percentage and resets_at. rate_limits appears only for Pro/Max/Ultra subscribers, or behind a gateway spend limit, and only after the first API response. Updates are event-driven with a 300 ms debounce, plus an optional refreshInterval timer (minimum 1 s).
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party for Claude Code. The docs link community configs ccstatusline (github.com/sirmalloc/ccstatusline) and starship-claude (github.com/martinemde/starship-claude). daniel3303/ClaudeCodeStatusLine shows model and effort, git, context tokens and 5h/7d rate limits with reset times, colour-coded; MIT licence, 622 stars and 67 forks as of 2026-11-18. Clawdex uses a statusline heartbeat to reset its desktop pet if Claude Code crashes.
adjacent.relevance: Partner and data source. It is the cheapest official feed for a usage or cost desk display: a statusline script can relay context %, 5h/7d limit % with reset times, session cost and PR state to a device or local server on every update, with no log scraping. It is also a threat to standalone usage-monitor apps, because subscribers now get rate-limit and context data in the terminal for free, and many free community themes already exist. Caveats: rate_limits is absent for API-key users, and updates go quiet when the session is idle unless refreshInterval is set.

adjacent.name: Codex app (OpenAI)
adjacent.one_liner: OpenAI's first-party desktop 'command center' for running coding agents in parallel threads, with built-in git worktrees, in-thread diff review, automations and a review queue. It launched on macOS (Apple Silicon) around Feb 2, 2026, and the docs now present it as the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Turn-completion notifications can be set to never, background-only or always, with separate toggles for permission and question alerts. A sidebar activity bell shows unread, running and waiting chats (Cmd+Option+U). Floating pets show Running, Needs input, Ready or Blocked. A Profile page shows activity insights, lifetime tokens, peak tokens, streaks, longest task and token activity, plus a shareable profile card with usage highlights.
adjacent.price_text: Included in all ChatGPT plans as of 2026-11-18: Free $0 and Go $8 (limited), Plus $20, Pro from $100 ($100/$200/$500), Business $20/user/mo billed annually ($25 monthly), Enterprise and Edu via sales.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party for Codex. Extension points: the Codex CLI and IDE host 'notify' setting runs an external program when a turn completes, and the settings reference links to a separate Hooks doc (not opened). The pet sprite format is reused by the community, e.g. Petdex's local hook server for Codex, Claude Code and Gemini CLI. No official hardware integration was found.
adjacent.relevance: The broadest platform threat in this set. It bundles orchestration (parallel threads and worktrees), notification and approval alerts, a desktop pet, and gamification (streaks, lifetime and peak tokens, shareable profile card) into a free app, overlapping almost every software category a desk-companion maker might sell. It is a benchmark for the state model and the multi-session priority logic. The openings left are physical or ambient hardware, other agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini/Antigravity), and approvals away from the screen. The notify hook makes Codex a straightforward integration target for a hardware display.

adjacent.name: Gemini CLI hooks, notifications, /stats and loop detection
adjacent.one_liner: First-party Gemini CLI features that overlap with agent companions. (1) Hooks: 11 events (BeforeTool, AfterTool, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, BeforeModel, BeforeToolSelection, AfterModel, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Notification, PreCompress) exchange JSON over stdin/stdout. BeforeTool can deny or rewrite a call. The Notification hook only observes and cannot approve. (2) Terminal notifications for 'action required' and 'session complete' via OSC 9/OSC 777, falling back to a terminal bell; set with general.enableNotifications, which is experimental and off by default. (3) /stats with session, model (token counts and quota), tools and heatmap views; heatmap shows a calendar of daily token usage across local sessions. (4) Automatic loop detection, on by default (model.disableLoopDetection=false).
adjacent.price_text: The CLI is free, open-source software. Since June 18, 2026 it serves only paid Gemini or Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform API keys and Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences. Consumer users (Google AI Pro/Ultra and free Code Assist individuals) were moved to Antigravity CLI.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party hooks are the integration surface. Community: peon-ping (github.com/PeonPing/peon-ping, MIT) registers Gemini CLI SessionStart, AfterAgent, AfterTool and Notification hooks via a gemini.sh adapter for sounds and desktop alerts; it also supports Claude Code and Codex. Petdex lists Gemini CLI among the agents its desktop pets react to. Google says Hooks, Agent Skills and Subagents carry over to Antigravity CLI, and extensions become 'Antigravity plugins', but without 1:1 parity at launch.
adjacent.relevance: Platform risk first. Google announced on May 19, 2026 that Gemini CLI is being replaced by Antigravity CLI, which took over consumer usage on June 18, 2026. A companion maker should target Antigravity CLI ('agy') hooks and treat Gemini CLI as an enterprise and API-key tail. Inspiration and threat: a usage heatmap and automatic loop detection are built in, overlapping 'drift or loop' alerts and streak or recap features. Partner: a hook system close to Claude Code's (tool, turn, session and notification events) makes a single cross-agent adapter practical.

Partner and integration target: support hooks.json events. Inspiration: the 8-agent Live Activity layout is a good model for a multi-session status screen.

adjacent.name: Google Antigravity
adjacent.one_liner: Google's agentic development platform (2.0 announced at I/O on May 19, 2026). It has four parts: the Antigravity App (a 'central command center' that runs many local agents in parallel, with subagents, scheduled cron tasks, voice prompts and JSON hooks), the Antigravity CLI ('agy'; TechCrunch reports it replaces Gemini CLI), an IDE and an SDK. The CLI's /usage panel shows per-model-group quota against a 5-hour and a weekly limit. Remote Control lets you drive desktop and CLI sessions from any browser, answer tool approvals there, and get push notifications through a home-screen web app.
adjacent.price_text: Individuals $0/month with a weekly-refreshed baseline quota. Google AI Pro and Ultra add higher 5-hour and weekly quotas, Remote Control and AI-credit overages (prices not listed on the page). Business via Google Cloud from $30/seat/month, or pay-as-you-go with $0 seat fee (pricing page seen 2026-11-18).
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party agent platform (Gemini models plus Claude and GPT models by tier). Built-in remote-control dashboard with approvals and push notifications (https://antigravity.google/docs/remote-control). JSON hooks for extension. Community quota monitors (seen in search results): Antigravity Quota Watcher VS Code extension (https://github.com/Henrik-3/AntigravityQuota), CodexBar (https://github.com/sibbl/CodexBar), ClaudeBar (https://github.com/tddworks/ClaudeBar), Brekel LLM-O-Meter tray app (https://github.com/Brekel/LLM-O-Meter), usage-cli (https://pypi.org/project/usage-cli/), and the commercial SessionWatcher (https://sessionwatcher.com/antigravity). No desk-hardware integration found.
adjacent.relevance: Platform risk, high. In one free product Google bundles an agent command center (orchestration), a quota panel (usage monitor) and phone or browser remote approval with push notifications (approval-remote). Integration target: a companion that supports Gemini users must now target agy and Antigravity hooks rather than Gemini CLI, and its quota model (shared 5-hour and weekly limits per model group) mirrors Claude's, so a single quota display design can serve both. Price benchmark: the core is free for individuals.

adjacent.name: JetBrains Air
adjacent.one_liner: JetBrains' system for running and reviewing multiple coding agents. It started as a standalone macOS app in public preview (March 2026) and now also ships as 'Air in IDEs', a plugin and 2026.3 EAP builds. It has per-project sessions with unread updates and changed files, in-context diff review with line comments sent back to the agent, automations triggered by merges or PRs, and team governance. It supports Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Junie and OpenCode, plus any ACP agent.
adjacent.price_text: Local sessions with your own provider subscriptions or keys need no JetBrains AI subscription. Cloud runs need JetBrains AI (credits: 1 credit = $1 of provider spend). Junie Lite runs are free for a limited time. Org plans: Basic free; Business $20 per AI seat/month; Enterprise on request (help page dated Nov 6, 2026, seen 2026-11-18).

Air Teams follows cloud tasks from web or mobile; the page said mobile was 'coming on November 15', and it was not confirmed as shipped. No community hardware or companion integration found.
adjacent.relevance: Platform risk for orchestration and multi-session dashboards. JetBrains is turning 'many agents, one review surface' into an IDE-vendor feature that spans Claude, Codex, Gemini and Copilot. ACP is the protocol to watch: a desk companion that speaks ACP, or listens to ACP-hosted sessions, could plug into Air, Zed and Xcode alike. Price benchmark: governance at $20 per AI seat/month.

adjacent.name: Xcode 26.3 agentic coding
adjacent.one_liner: Xcode 26.3 (announced Feb 3, 2026) put Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex inside Xcode. Agents can search docs, change project settings, run builds and capture Previews to check their own work, and Xcode exposes its capabilities over MCP. MCP server exposure of Xcode capabilities (reported as 'mcpbridge'), and ACP for any compatible agent. GitHub and Figma are launch plug-in partners. adjacent.name: Claude Code Channels
adjacent.one_liner: A first-party research-preview feature. Channel plugins (MCP servers) push Telegram, Discord or iMessage chats, webhooks and alerts into a running local Claude Code session, and can relay tool-permission prompts so you approve or deny them from your phone.
adjacent.price_text: No extra charge. Needs Claude Code via a paid Claude plan (Pro $20/mo billed monthly, Max $100, Ultra $200; Team/Enterprise only if an admin enables channels) or a Console API key. Bun is required for the official plugins. Prices seen on claude.com/pricing as of 2026-11-18.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party to Claude Code. It launched as a research preview around 2026-03-20 (Claude Code v2.1.80+) with Telegram and Discord; iMessage and a localhost 'fakechat' demo were added later. Official plugin source is at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins. A public channel contract lets anyone build a channel (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference). It uses capability 'claude/channel' plus an optional 'claude/channel/permission' for permission relay. In the relay, Claude Code sends notifications/claude/channel/permission_request {request_id, tool_name, description, input_preview}, and the channel answers with notifications/claude/channel/permission {request_id, behavior: allow|deny}. The terminal and the remote approver are live at the same time, and the first answer wins. During the preview, only plugins on Anthropic's allowlist (claude-plugins-official) or an org's allowedChannelPlugins can register. Custom or community channels need --dangerously-load-development-channels, and the docs say 'The community marketplace is not on the channel allowlist'. I found no ESP32 or hardware channel plugin. Hardware approval projects use hooks instead, for example a Clawdmeter PR adding physical Deny/Always/Allow for PreToolUse (https://github.com/HermannBjorgvin/Clawdmeter/pull/168, seen in search results only).
adjacent.relevance: Platform risk and possible partner path. Remote approve/deny is the core value of an approval-remote companion, and Anthropic now ships it free through chat apps, alongside first-party Remote Control and Dispatch for the mobile app. On the other hand, the channel protocol (push events in, reply tool out, permission relay with a 5-letter request ID) is a documented, hardware-friendly contract that a desk device could implement, for example with a local bridge daemon. Distribution is gated, though: outside the allowlist, users must launch with a scary dev flag, and the docs say to work with an Anthropic partner contact for an official-marketplace listing. Team/Enterprise orgs can also allowlist a plugin themselves. The protocol may change while it is in preview. For now, hooks are the friction-free route for third-party hardware.

adjacent.name: Claude Desktop app, Code tab
adjacent.one_liner: Claude Code inside the Claude desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux beta). It runs parallel sessions with optional git worktrees, split view, permission modes, a usage ring and context card, OS notifications when a session finishes, and cloud/SSH/Remote Control/Dispatch sessions you can follow from the mobile app. In developer mode it also offers a 'Hardware Buddy' BLE API for maker devices.
adjacent.price_text: No extra charge. Included with paid Claude plans (Pro $20/mo billed monthly, Max $100, Ultra $200, Team $20-25 or $100-125 per seat, Enterprise). Computer use and Dispatch are Pro/Max/Ultra only. Prices seen on claude.com/pricing as of 2026-11-18. The Hardware Buddy reference device (M5StickC Plus) costs about $30 per CNX Software.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party Claude Code surface. The desktop app exposes an opt-in BLE 'Hardware Buddy' API: 'Claude for macOS and Windows can connect Claude Cowork and Claude Code to maker devices over BLE, so developers and makers can build hardware that displays permission prompts, recent messages, and other interactions.' To use it, enable Help > Troubleshooting > Enable Developer Mode, then open Developer > Open Hardware Buddy. It uses the Nordic UART Service. Anthropic's open-source reference firmware is an ESP32 desk pet for the M5StickC Plus, with states sleep, busy, attention (approval pending) and celebrate ('level up (every 50K tokens)'), plus button approve/deny. The repo says it 'isn't an officially supported product feature'. Repo: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-desktop-buddy (2.7k stars, 474 forks as of 2026-11-18); CNX Software covered it on 2026-05-16. Community ports seen in search results: ESP32-S3 AMOLED (https://github.com/vthinkxie/claude-desktop-buddy-esp32), ESP-IDF/xiaozhi (https://github.com/MoveCall/claude-desktop-buddy-esp32), M5 Cardputer (https://github.com/y88huang/claude-desktop-buddy-cardputer), and LilyGO wiki guides for T-LoRa Pager and T-Keyboard S3 Pro. A commercial e-ink pet (InksPet v1.1) also says it pairs as a Hardware Buddy (https://inkspet-web.pages.dev/blog/claude-desktop-hardware-buddy/).
adjacent.relevance: Direct threat and a key inspiration. Anthropic itself published a free, open-source reference desk companion: a pet with busy, attention and celebrate states, token-based 'level up', and physical approve/deny. It also gave makers an official, if unsupported, BLE bridge, so a cheap ESP32 board can become a Claude Code companion without custom hooks. That lowers the barrier for competitors and sets a ~$30 hobby price anchor. It is also a partner path: a product that speaks the Hardware Buddy protocol works with Desktop sessions out of the box. The risk is that it is developer-mode-only and unsupported, so the protocol can change. The app also takes over 'which session is done/needs me' with native notifications, the usage ring, Dispatch push notifications on finish or approval, and parallel-session management.

adjacent.name: Claude Code /usage, /stats, /insights and /recap
adjacent.one_liner: Built-in Claude Code usage and reflection tools. /usage (aliases /cost and /stats) shows session cost, plan usage bars, activity stats and an attribution and recommendations breakdown with an 'f to fix' shortcut. /stats opens a Stats tab with an activity heatmap and streaks. /insights writes an HTML report on how you work. /recap gives a one-line session summary. The status line receives live rate-limit data.
adjacent.price_text: Free. Built into Claude Code on any plan. /insights spends tokens from your plan or API usage.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party. The /usage plan breakdown attributes usage to skills, subagents, plugins and MCP servers, recommends changes, lists loops, and switches between 24h and 7d views. It is computed from local history only. /stats opens on the Stats tab. Third-party write-ups and many bug reports describe a 12-week GitHub-style heatmap, current and longest streak, favorite model, peak hours, top projects and achievements such as 7-Day Streak. These come from a third-party blog; the official docs do not enumerate the tab. /insights writes ~/.claude/usage-data/report.html and analyzes up to 200 new sessions per run. /recap and an automatic session recap appear after you have been away. Status line scripts receive JSON on stdin, including rate_limits.five_hour and seven_day used_percentage and resets_at (Pro/Max/Ultra), cost.total_cost_usd, context_window.used_percentage and prompt_cache. That stdin feed is the hook a desk display or usage monitor can read. Community equivalents remain large: ccusage covers 20 agents, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot CLI and Gemini CLI (https://github.com/ryoppippi/ccusage, 19.5k stars as of 2026-11-18).
adjacent.relevance: Platform risk for usage/cost monitors and for gamification. Anthropic now ships usage bars, streaks, a heatmap, achievements, a 'how you work' report and recaps natively, so a companion that only shows burn rate or streaks adds little. It is also an enabler: the status line JSON (5h/7d percentage plus reset times, cost, context) is an official, stable data feed a desk display can mirror without scraping. Known heatmap and streak bugs (sessions bucketed by start date, VS Code or claude.ai usage missing) leave room for a more accurate or cross-device view. The built-in stats are per machine only, a gap a cross-device companion could fill.

The Leaderboard ranks the top 10 users by PRs or lines with Claude Code. The Enterprise Analytics API (read:analytics scope) and the Claude Code Analytics API (Admin key) return daily per-user metrics programmatically. OpenTelemetry export streams per-user token and cost metrics in near real time. I found no community hardware or desk-display integration of this dashboard.
adjacent.relevance: Low direct threat to a personal desk companion. This is admin and ROI reporting, not a motivating real-time experience. It shows Anthropic is comfortable with leaderboards and 'contribution' gamification at org level, which validates team leaderboards. It is also a possible data source for a team-facing desk display (an office scoreboard) through the Analytics API or OpenTelemetry. The platform risk is limited to team-level gamification and analytics products.

adjacent.name: Codex CLI /statusline, /status, /usage
adjacent.one_liner: Built-in Codex CLI commands. /statusline configures TUI footer items interactively (model plus reasoning, context used, 5-hour and weekly limits, git branch, token counters and more; saved to tui.status_line). /status shows session config and token usage. /usage shows account token activity (daily, weekly, cumulative). /title sets terminal-title fields such as status and task progress.
adjacent.price_text: Free. Built into the Codex CLI. Codex comes with ChatGPT Free ($0), Go ($8/mo), Plus ($20/mo), Pro (from $100/mo), Business ($20-25/user/mo) and Enterprise, or API-key billing. Prices seen on learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing as of 2026-11-18.
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party to Codex. /statusline arrived in rust-v0.99.0 (2026-02-11). The status line is a fixed enum of built-in items (e.g. model-with-reasoning, task-progress, current-dir, context-used, five-hour-limit, weekly-limit), not a user command. A request for a command-backed custom statusline like Claude Code's (#20140, 2026-04-29) was closed as a duplicate of #17827 'Customizable status line'. External integrations therefore go through Codex hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop) or the notify program (agent-turn-complete). Community hardware via hooks includes codex-lamp, which drives a Moonside BLE lamp (amber idle, blue working, purple awaiting approval; https://github.com/loopbrew/codex-lamp, 40 stars as of 2026-11-18). Search leads, not opened: ThinkLight, which uses the Mac camera LED for Claude Code and Codex (https://github.com/lichengzhe/thinklight), and Semaphore, a USB-HID traffic light for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode (https://github.com/artemy/semaphore). ccusage also reads Codex usage (https://github.com/ryoppippi/ccusage).
adjacent.relevance: Moderate platform risk for usage monitors: Codex users get 5h and weekly limit gauges and context in the footer for free. But the closed, fixed-item statusline has no stdin JSON feed like Claude Code's, so a desk companion must rely on hooks or notify, or read local session files, to mirror Codex state. A multi-agent companion has to build that adapter. The hook events (PermissionRequest, Stop) do map cleanly to companion states, as codex-lamp shows. It is also a price benchmark: basic status visibility costs nothing.

adjacent.name: Codex on mobile
adjacent.one_liner: In the ChatGPT mobile app you can start, follow, steer and review Codex tasks running in the cloud or on a paired Mac or Windows PC. It pairs by QR code from the desktop app (Settings > Connections > Control this Mac or PC). On the phone you approve, always-approve, deny or redirect commands, see when input is needed, and inspect diffs.
adjacent.price_text: No extra charge. Included in the ChatGPT mobile app with a Codex-enabled ChatGPT plan (Plus $20/mo and up per the pricing page). The exact plan gating for remote control was not clearly stated as of 2026-11-18. Docs say 'Availability depends on rollout and your workspace settings.'
adjacent.ai_agent_integration: First-party to Codex. It launched as a preview on 2026-05-14 for iPhone, iPad and Android, connecting to Codex for Mac only, with Windows 'coming soon' (9to5Mac). Current official docs list connected 'Mac or Windows PC' hosts and Cloud. The phone streams screenshots, terminal output, diffs, test results and approval requests in real time, while files and credentials stay on the host. The host must stay awake and online. A third-party report says Codex Remote went GA with Windows hosts around 2026-06-25; I did not confirm that on an OpenAI page, and the OpenAI announcement page returned 403. No third-party hardware integration exists, since this is a closed first-party relay.
adjacent.relevance: Platform risk for approval-remote and phone-companion products. OpenAI now ships free, first-party remote steering and approval for Codex, and Anthropic does the same for Claude Code with Remote Control, Dispatch and Channels. 'Approve from your phone' is no longer a differentiator. A desk companion has to win on ambient, glanceable, physical presence at the desk and on cross-agent coverage, not on remote approval. The relay is closed, so it is not a partner surface, though Codex hooks (PermissionRequest) still let a desk device show that approval is pending alongside the phone.
